Married to Jacob by Laban's trick (Gen 29:23-25)
Mother of six sons and Dinah, including Levi and Judah
Named Judah saying 'I will praise the LORD' (Gen 29:35)
Buried at Machpelah (Gen 49:31)

people.name: Mary, Mother of Jesus
people.summary: A virgin of Nazareth betrothed to Joseph, Mary was greeted by the angel Gabriel and conceived Jesus by the Holy Spirit, answering 'let it be done to me according to your word'. She visited her relative Elizabeth and sang the Magnificat, gave birth in Bethlehem, presented Jesus in the Temple and found him there at twelve. She prompted his first sign at Cana, stood by the cross where Jesus entrusted her to the beloved disciple, and prayed with the apostles awaiting the Spirit.
people.catholic: The Church professes four Marian dogmas: Mary is the Mother of God (Theotokos), defined at the Council of Ephesus in 431 (CCC 495); she is ever-virgin, before, during and after the birth of Christ (CCC 496-507); she was preserved from all stain of original sin from her conception (Immaculate Conception, defined by Pius IX in 1854; CCC 490-492); and she was assumed body and soul into heavenly glory (Assumption, defined by Pius XII in 1950; CCC 966). The Fathers call her the New Eve, whose obedience untied the knot of Eve's disobedience (St Irenaeus, CCC 494), and she is the Ark of the Covenant where the glory of the Lord dwells (CCC 2676) - Luke's Visitation deliberately echoes David bringing up the Ark (2 Sam 6). From the cross Jesus gave her as mother to the beloved disciple (Jn 19:26-27), which the Church reads as her spiritual motherhood of all believers (CCC 964-970). The 'brothers' of Jesus are understood as kinsmen, not further children of Mary (CCC 500).
know: Mother of God (Theotokos): Council of Ephesus, 431.
Immaculate Conception defined 1854 (Pius IX); Assumption defined 1950 (Pius XII).
Perpetual virgin: James and Joses, called Jesus' 'brothers', are sons of 'another Mary' (Mt 27:56; CCC 500).
Her Magnificat (Lk 1:46-55) is sung daily at Vespers; the Hail Mary joins Gabriel's and Elizabeth's greetings.
Tradition (Protoevangelium of James), not Scripture, names her parents Joachim and Anne.
people.feast: January 1 (Mary, Mother of God); March 25 (Annunciation); May 31 (Visitation); August 15 (Assumption); September 8 (Nativity of Mary); December 8 (Immaculate Conception)

relations.type: visited before his birth (he leapt in the womb)
received the prophecy of the sword
New Eve (the woman of the first promise)
stood with her at the cross

people.name: Ahaziah of Judah
people.summary: Ahaziah son of Jehoram and Athaliah reigned one year, following the counsel of his mother and Ahab's house. Visiting the wounded Joram of Israel at Jezreel, he was caught up in Jehu's revolt and killed.
know: Reigned one year
Son of Athaliah
Killed by Jehu's men
Called Jehoahaz in 2 Chr 21:17

people.name: Eli
people.summary: Eli was priest at the sanctuary of Shiloh and judged Israel forty years. He blessed Hannah's prayer and raised the boy Samuel, teaching him to answer God's call, but he failed to restrain his corrupt sons Hophni and Phinehas, and a man of God foretold the fall of his house. When news came that the Ark was captured and his sons dead, the ninety-eight-year-old Eli fell backward and died.
people.catholic: The Catechism notes that Samuel learned from Eli the priest how to listen to God's word: 'Speak, LORD, for your servant is listening' (CCC 2578) - Eli's counsel became a model for discernment and vocational prayer, read on the 2nd Sunday in Ordinary Time (Year B). His story is also a sober warning about a shepherd who honours his children above God (1 Sam 2:29), and the prophecy against his house is fulfilled when Solomon removes Abiathar from the priesthood (1 Kgs 2:27).
know: Priest at Shiloh, where the Ark rested
Taught Samuel to say 'Speak, LORD, for your servant hears'
Did not restrain his sons' sins against the offerings
Died on hearing the Ark had been captured

people.name: Judith
people.summary: A devout and beautiful widow of Bethulia who, when the city was about to surrender to Holofernes' besieging army, rebuked the elders for putting God to the test, prayed, and went into the enemy camp. After four days she cut off the drunken Holofernes' head with his own sword and returned with it, and the Assyrian army fled. She sang a hymn of victory, refused remarriage and died at 105.
people.catholic: This book is one of the deuterocanonical books — part of the Greek Old Testament (Septuagint) used by the apostolic Church, listed in the canon by the councils of Rome (382), Hippo (393) and Carthage (397), reaffirmed at Florence and defined at Trent (1546) — which Protestant Bibles place among the 'Apocrypha'. The Church sees Judith as a type of Mary: as the elder Ozias blessed her 'above all the women upon the earth' (Jdt 13:18; cf. Luke 1:42), and the people acclaimed her, 'You are the exaltation of Jerusalem! You are the great glory of Israel!' (Jdt 15:9 — in the Latin Vulgate 'Tu gloria Ierusalem, tu laetitia Israel, tu honorificentia populi nostri', words sung of the Immaculate Virgin in the antiphon Tota pulchra es and used in Marian feasts). Like Mary, the humble woman crushes the head of the enemy (cf. Gen 3:15). The Catechism lists her among the holy women who kept Israel's hope alive and prepared for Mary (CCC 64, 489).
know: Daughter of Merari, widow of Manasses (Jdt 8:1-2).
Rebuked the elders for setting a deadline for God (Jdt 8:11-27).
Beheaded Holofernes (Jdt 13:6-10).
Her canticle (Jdt 16:1-17) is prayed in the Liturgy of the Hours.
Lived to 105 and never remarried (Jdt 16:22-23).

people.name: Nun
people.summary: Man of the tribe of Ephraim, father of Joshua. 1 Chronicles 7 places him in the line of Ephraim as son of Elishama son of Ammihud.
know: Father of Joshua (Exo 33:11).
Of the tribe of Ephraim (Num 13:8).
Son of Elishama in 1 Chr 7:26-27.

people.name: Caleb
people.summary: Son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, the spy from Judah who, with Joshua, urged Israel to trust God and take the land. God promised that because he 'followed me fully' he would enter Canaan. At eighty-five he claimed Hebron, drove out the three sons of Anak, and gave his daughter Achsah to Othniel for capturing Kiriath Sepher.
people.catholic: Caleb is the Bible's portrait of wholehearted fidelity and undiminished strength in old age (Jos 14:10-11); Sirach 46:7-10 praises him with Joshua, and 1 Maccabees 2:56 says he received an inheritance 'for testifying in the congregation'. The Church holds him up as an example of courageous witness against the discouragement of the crowd.
know: Spy from Judah (Num 13:6).
'Let's go up at once, and possess it' (Num 13:30).
Had 'another spirit' and followed God fully (Num 14:24).
Took Hebron at age 85 (Jos 14:10-14).
Father of Achsah.

people.name: Rebekah
people.summary: Daughter of Bethuel, found at the well by Abraham's servant, whom she generously watered with his camels. She agreed to go and marry Isaac, and after twenty years of barrenness bore Esau and Jacob, receiving the oracle that 'the elder will serve the younger'. She helped Jacob obtain Isaac's blessing and then sent him to her brother Laban to escape Esau's anger.
people.catholic: St Paul cites the oracle given to Rebekah before the twins were born as a sign of God's free election (Rom 9:10-13). The story of her betrothal (Gen 24) has long been read as a model of providence in marriage; the traditional Roman nuptial blessing prayed that the bride be 'wise like Rebecca'. Some Fathers saw her, leaving home to go to an unseen bridegroom, as an image of the Church called to Christ.
know: Watered the servant's camels at the well (Gen 24:15-20)
Said 'I will go' and married Isaac (Gen 24:58)
Mother of Esau and Jacob (Gen 25:24-26)
Planned Jacob's taking of the blessing (Gen 27:5-17)
Buried at Machpelah (Gen 49:31)

people.name: Tobias
people.summary: The son of Tobit, sent to Media to recover his father's money and guided by the angel Raphael disguised as 'Azarias'. On the journey he caught the fish whose heart, liver and gall drove away the demon Asmodaeus and healed his father. He married his kinswoman Sarah, and on their wedding night the couple prayed together before anything else; he then returned home and cured Tobit's blindness.
people.catholic: Tobias and Sarah's prayer (Tob 8:4-8) — 'I take not this my sister for lust, but in truth' — is one of the Old Testament readings offered in the Lectionary for the Celebration of Marriage, and the book is a classic image of marriage as a vocation lived in prayer and chastity. Raphael accompanying Tobias has made him a beloved figure of the guardian angel walking with every Christian.
know: Guided by Raphael under the name Azarias.
Married Sarah, daughter of Raguel (Tob 7:13).
Prayed with Sarah on the wedding night (Tob 8:4-8).
Healed Tobit's eyes with the fish's gall (Tob 11:10-13).
Had six sons (Tob 14:3) and died at Ecbatana.

people.name: Abiathar
people.summary: Abiathar son of Ahimelech alone escaped Saul's massacre of the priests of Nob and fled to David with the ephod. He served as priest beside Zadok throughout David's reign and stayed loyal during Absalom's revolt, but backed Adonijah's bid for the throne; Solomon spared his life but banished him to Anathoth, fulfilling the word spoken against Eli's house.
people.catholic: Abiathar's removal marks the end of Eli's priestly line and the rise of Zadok's, which Ezekiel later names as the faithful priesthood. Mark 2:26 recalls 'the time of Abiathar the high priest' when David ate the showbread, a passage Jesus uses to teach that the Sabbath is made for man.
know: Sole survivor of the massacre at Nob
Brought the ephod to David
Co-priest with Zadok
Sided with Adonijah and was exiled to Anathoth

people.name: Kohath
people.summary: Second son of Levi, who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household. He was the grandfather of Moses, Aaron and Miriam, and his descendants, the Kohathites, were charged with carrying the most holy things of the tabernacle, including the ark.
people.catholic: Kohath matters chiefly as the link in the priestly genealogy from Levi to Aaron. The Kohathite duty of bearing the ark and the holy vessels (Num 4) shows that in Israel holiness required ordered, appointed ministry, a theme the Church sees fulfilled in the ordered ministries of the New Covenant.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)
Grandfather of Moses, Aaron and Miriam through Amram (Ex 6:18-20)
The Kohathites carried the ark and holy vessels (Num 4:4-15)
Son of Levi; went down to Egypt with Jacob (Gen 46:11).
Father of Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.
Lived 133 years (Exo 6:18).
Kohathites carried the ark and holy furnishings but could not touch or look on them (Num 4:15-20).

people.name: Nathan
people.summary: Nathan the prophet brought David God's covenant promise of an everlasting house and throne (2 Sam 7). After David's sin with Bathsheba he confronted the king with the parable of the poor man's ewe lamb - 'You are the man!' - and announced both forgiveness and its consequences. He named the infant Solomon 'Jedidiah' and, with Bathsheba, ensured Solomon succeeded David.
people.catholic: Nathan's oracle (2 Sam 7:12-16), read on the 4th Sunday of Advent (Year B) alongside the Annunciation, is the foundation of the Church's teaching that Christ is the promised Son of David whose kingdom has no end (Lk 1:32-33). His rebuke of David is a model of fraternal correction and prophetic courage, and David's 'I have sinned against the LORD' with Nathan's word of pardon foreshadows sacramental confession and absolution (2 Sam 12:7-13 is read on the 11th Sunday in Ordinary Time, Year C).
know: Delivered the Davidic covenant oracle
Told the parable of the ewe lamb
Declared David's sin forgiven
Named Solomon Jedidiah
Secured Solomon's anointing

people.name: Barnabas
people.summary: Joses, a Levite from Cyprus, was named Barnabas ('Son of Encouragement') by the apostles; he sold a field and laid the money at their feet. He vouched for the newly converted Saul before the frightened Jerusalem disciples, was sent to the new church at Antioch, and brought Saul there to teach. Set apart by the Holy Spirit with Saul, he led the first missionary journey through Cyprus and Galatia and defended the Gentile mission at the Council of Jerusalem. He and Paul parted over whether to take his cousin John Mark on the second journey.
people.catholic: Though not one of the Twelve, Barnabas is called an apostle in Acts 14:14 and honored as such; his memorial is June 11. His sending with Saul, after prayer, fasting and the laying on of hands by the prophets and teachers of Antioch (Acts 13:2-3), is read as a model of the Church's commissioning of missionaries by the Holy Spirit through the community. His generosity (Acts 4:36-37) is an image of the communion of goods in the early Church, and his reconciling role toward Saul and Mark makes him a patron of encouragement. Tradition holds he was martyred at Salamis in Cyprus.
know: His name means 'Son of Encouragement' (Acts 4:36).
Introduced the converted Saul to the apostles (Acts 9:27).
At Antioch, where he worked, the disciples were first called Christians (Acts 11:26).
Called 'Zeus' by the crowd at Lystra (Acts 14:12).
Cousin of John Mark (Col 4:10); memorial June 11.

relations.type: carried away by the hypocrisy of
given the right hand of fellowship by

people.name: Benaiah
people.summary: Benaiah son of Jehoiada, a valiant warrior who killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day, commanded David's bodyguard (the Cherethites and Pelethites). He supported Solomon, executed Adonijah, Joab and Shimei, and became Solomon's army commander.
know: Killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day
Captain of the Cherethites and Pelethites
Executed Joab at the altar
Solomon's commander-in-chief

people.name: James, son of Zebedee
people.summary: James and his brother John were fishermen, partners of Simon, who left their father Zebedee in the boat to follow Jesus. Named 'Boanerges', Sons of Thunder, he belonged with Peter and John to the inner circle present at the raising of Jairus's daughter, the Transfiguration and Gethsemane. He was the first of the Twelve to be martyred, put to the sword by Herod Agrippa I.
people.catholic: Known as St James the Greater to distinguish him from James the Less. His request for a place of glory led Jesus to teach that he would drink his cup, fulfilled in his martyrdom (Mk 10:38-39; Acts 12:2). Tradition holds his relics rest at Santiago de Compostela, goal of the great pilgrimage, and he is patron of Spain and of pilgrims.
know: Son of Zebedee; brother of John (Mt 4:21).
With Peter and John, witness of the Transfiguration (Mt 17:1).
First apostle martyred (Acts 12:2).
Feast July 25.

people.name: Jehoiada
people.summary: Jehoiada the priest, husband of Jehosheba, guarded the hidden Joash in the Temple and in the seventh year organised the guard, crowned and anointed the boy king, had Athaliah executed, destroyed the temple of Baal and renewed the covenant. Joash did right all his days; Jehoiada died at 130 and was buried among the kings.
know: Crowned Joash in the Temple
Led a covenant renewal
Buried among the kings of Judah
Father of Zechariah the martyr

people.name: Jeshua the high priest
people.summary: Jeshua (Joshua) son of Jozadak was the first high priest after the return from Babylon. With Zerubbabel he rebuilt the altar, offered the first sacrifices and laid the foundations of the Second Temple. In Zechariah's visions he is cleansed of filthy garments and crowned as a sign of 'the Branch'.
people.catholic: Jeshua bears the same name as Jesus (Hebrew Yeshua; Sirach's Greek even calls him 'Jesus the son of Josedek', Sir 49:12). The Fathers saw in Zechariah 3 and 6 — the high priest stripped of filthy garments, clothed anew and crowned — a striking figure of Christ, the great High Priest who is also King (Heb 4:14). His restoration of daily sacrifice anticipates the perfect worship of the New Covenant.
know: Son of Jozadak, of the high-priestly line.
Called Joshua in Haggai and Zechariah.
Crowned in Zechariah 6:11 as a sign of 'the Branch'.
Praised in Sirach 49:12 as 'Jesus the son of Josedek'.

people.name: Manasseh
people.summary: Joseph's firstborn by Asenath, named because 'God has made me forget all my toil'. Jacob adopted him and Ephraim as his own sons but, crossing his hands, gave the greater blessing to the younger Ephraim.
people.catholic: Jacob's blessing, 'God make you as Ephraim and as Manasseh' (Gen 48:20), became a blessing of children in Israel. Tertullian (On Baptism 8) saw in Jacob's crossed hands a figure of the Cross through which Christ's blessing comes.
know: Joseph's firstborn (Gen 41:51)
Adopted by Jacob as his own (Gen 48:5)
Received the lesser blessing under Jacob's crossed hands (Gen 48:13-20)
Father of Machir (Gen 50:23)
Not King Manasseh of Judah

people.name: Baasha
people.summary: Baasha son of Ahijah, of Issachar, killed Nadab, wiped out Jeroboam's house and reigned twenty-four years at Tirzah, warring with Asa of Judah; yet he walked in Jeroboam's sins, and the prophet Jehu son of Hanani foretold the same end for his house.
know: Usurper who founded Israel's second dynasty
Fortified Ramah against Judah
Condemned by Jehu son of Hanani

people.name: Gedaliah
people.summary: After the fall of Jerusalem Nebuchadnezzar appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam governor over those left in Judah, with his seat at Mizpah, and Jeremiah went to live with him. He urged the people to serve Babylon and live, but ignored warnings and was assassinated by Ishmael son of Nethaniah, after which the remnant fled to Egypt.
know: Governor at Mizpah after 587 BC
Protector of Jeremiah
Assassinated by Ishmael
His murder is remembered by the Jewish Fast of Gedaliah

people.name: Jehoiachin
people.summary: Jehoiachin (Jeconiah, Coniah), son of Jehoiakim, reigned three months at eighteen before surrendering Jerusalem to Nebuchadnezzar in 597 BC. He was taken to Babylon with his mother, officials, craftsmen and the Temple treasures. Jeremiah declared that none of his offspring would sit on David's throne, yet after thirty-seven years Evilmerodach released him from prison and gave him a seat at the king's table - a sign that David's line endured.
people.catholic: Matthew's genealogy names 'Jechoniah' at the Babylonian exile and continues through his son Shealtiel to Zerubbabel and on to Joseph (Mt 1:11-12), showing that God kept his promise to David even through the Exile. His release from prison at the end of 2 Kings is a quiet note of hope for the Davidic line. Ezekiel dates his visions by 'King Jehoiachin's captivity' (Ezek 1:2).
know: Reigned three months
Exiled to Babylon in 597 BC
Called Jeconiah / Jechoniah / Coniah
Released from prison by Evilmerodach
Ancestor of Jesus through Shealtiel

people.name: Jephthah
people.summary: Mighty warrior of Gilead, son of Gilead by a prostitute, driven out by his half-brothers and living as a raider in Tob. When Ammon attacked, the elders of Gilead made him their head. After arguing Israel's case to the Ammonite king, he made a rash vow to offer whatever first came out of his house if he returned victorious; he defeated Ammon, and his only daughter came out to meet him. He judged Israel six years.
people.catholic: Hebrews 11:32 lists Jephthah among those who through faith conquered kingdoms, yet St. Jerome (quoted by St. Thomas Aquinas) judged him 'foolish in vowing and impious in keeping' his vow, and the Church uses his story as a warning about imprudent vows; the Catechism teaches that vows must concern a 'better good' that is possible (CCC 2102). His daughter's acceptance has been compared by some writers to self-offering, but Scripture presents the vow itself as a tragedy.
know: Son of Gilead by a prostitute (Jdg 11:1).
Made head of Gilead against Ammon (Jdg 11:4-11).
Made a rash vow (Jdg 11:30-31).
Fought Ephraim; the 'Shibboleth' test (Jdg 12:5-6).
Named in Heb 11:32.

people.name: Levi
people.role: Son of Jacob; ancestor of the priestly tribe
people.summary: Third son of Jacob and Leah, whose name Leah linked to her hope that Jacob would be 'joined' to her. With Simeon he slaughtered the men of Shechem. His sons Gershon, Kohath and Merari head the Levitical clans; Moses, Aaron and Miriam descend from him through Kohath.
people.catholic: Though Jacob rebuked Levi's anger (Gen 49:5-7), his descendants were consecrated to the service of the sanctuary, and Aaron's line became the priesthood of the Old Covenant. Hebrews argues that Levi, 'in the loins of his father' Abraham, paid tithes to Melchizedek, showing that Christ's priesthood after Melchizedek's order surpasses the Levitical one (Heb 7:9-11). The Levitical priesthood is seen as a preparation for the ordained priesthood of the New Covenant (CCC 1539-1541).
know: Third son of Jacob and Leah (Gen 29:34)
Avenged Dinah with Simeon (Gen 34:25)
Father of Gershon, Kohath and Merari (Gen 46:11)
Ancestor of Moses, Aaron and the priests
Paid tithes to Melchizedek 'in Abraham' (Heb 7:9-10)

people.name: Nebat
people.summary: Nebat, an Ephraimite of Zeredah, was the father of Jeroboam I, who is constantly called 'Jeroboam the son of Nebat'.
know: His name became a byword through his son

people.name: Antiochus IV Epiphanes
people.summary: 'A sinful root', son of Antiochus III, who reigned 175-164 BC. He sold the high priesthood, plundered the Temple, and in 167 BC outlawed the Jewish religion, setting up 'an abomination of desolation' on the altar and putting to death those who kept the Law — including Eleazar and the seven brothers. His persecution provoked the Maccabean revolt. He died in Persia in agony, after (according to 2 Maccabees) vainly vowing to become a Jew.
people.catholic: Antiochus is the Old Testament's archetype of the persecutor of God's people. The Church, following the Fathers, sees him in Daniel's 'little horn' (Dan 8:9-12; 11:21-45), and his 'abomination of desolation' (1 Macc 1:54; Dan 11:31) is the background of Jesus' warning (Matt 24:15) and a type of the final Antichrist (2 Thess 2:3-4). His miserable end (2 Macc 9) shows that 'it is right to be subject to God' (2 Macc 9:12).
know: Called 'Epiphanes' ('God manifest'); his enemies punned 'Epimanes' (madman).
Profaned the Temple and set up the abomination of desolation (1 Macc 1:20-24, 54).
Persecutor of Eleazar and the seven brothers (2 Macc 6-7).
Died in Persia (1 Macc 6:1-16; 2 Macc 9).
The 'little horn' of Daniel 8.

people.name: Ezra
people.summary: A priest descended from Aaron and 'a skilled scribe in the law of Moses', Ezra led a second group of exiles from Babylon to Jerusalem under Artaxerxes (c. 458 BC). He confronted the problem of mixed marriages with penitential prayer and reform, and, together with Nehemiah, publicly read the Law to the assembled people, who wept and then celebrated the Feast of Tabernacles.
people.catholic: Ezra is honored as a father of Judaism as a 'people of the Book'. The great assembly of Nehemiah 8 — the Word proclaimed from a raised platform, explained so that the people understood, answered with 'Amen' and followed by a feast — is often taken as a model of the Liturgy of the Word, and Neh 8:2-10 is read on the Third Sunday in Ordinary Time (Year C) alongside Jesus reading Isaiah in the synagogue (Luke 4). His penitential prayer (Ezra 9) is a model of confession on behalf of the whole people.
know: Descended from Aaron (Ezra 7:1-5).
Came to Jerusalem in the seventh year of Artaxerxes (Ezra 7:7-8).
Led the reform against mixed marriages (Ezra 9-10).
Read the Law publicly at the Water Gate (Neh 8).
Notably absent from Sirach's 'praise of the fathers', which praises Nehemiah instead.

people.name: Jehoash (Joash) of Israel
people.summary: Jehoash son of Jehoahaz reigned sixteen years. He wept over the dying Elisha - 'my father, the chariots of Israel' - and at the prophet's word shot the arrow of victory and struck the ground three times, winning three victories over Syria. He defeated Amaziah of Judah, broke down Jerusalem's wall and plundered the Temple.
know: Visited Elisha on his deathbed
Struck the ground only three times
Defeated Amaziah of Judah

people.name: Jonah
people.summary: Jonah son of Amittai, from Gath-hepher, prophesied in the time of Jeroboam II. Sent to preach to Nineveh, he fled by ship toward Tarshish, was thrown overboard in a storm and swallowed by a great fish for three days and nights, then prayed and was cast onto dry land. His preaching brought all Nineveh to repentance, to his displeasure, and God taught him his compassion for the city.
people.catholic: Jesus himself made Jonah a sign of his death and Resurrection: 'as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the huge fish, so will the Son of Man be three days... in the heart of the earth' (Mt 12:40). Nineveh's repentance is a model for Lent — Jonah 3 is read on the Wednesday of the First Week of Lent — and the book proclaims God's mercy to the Gentiles. Jonah and the fish are among the most frequent images in early Christian catacomb art as a figure of resurrection.
know: Son of Amittai from Gath-hepher (2 Kings 14:25).
Fled toward Tarshish; three days in the fish (Jonah 1:17).
Nineveh repented at his preaching (Jonah 3).
'The sign of Jonah' given by Jesus (Mt 12:39-41; Lk 11:29-32).

people.name: Zerubbabel
people.summary: A grandson of King Jehoiachin who led the first great return of exiles from Babylon under Cyrus and served as Persian governor of Judah. With the high priest Jeshua he rebuilt the altar and laid the foundation of the Second Temple, and, spurred on by the prophets Haggai and Zechariah, finished the Temple in the reign of Darius (515 BC).
people.catholic: Zerubbabel keeps the royal line of David alive after the Exile, and both Matthew and Luke name him among the ancestors of Jesus. God's promise through Haggai to make him 'like a signet ring' (Hag 2:23) reverses the curse on his grandfather Jeconiah and points forward to the Messiah, the true Son of David who builds the true Temple of his Body (John 2:19-21). Sirach praises him in the 'praise of the fathers' (Sir 49:11). The pairing of a Davidic prince and a high priest (Zerubbabel and Jeshua, Zech 4) foreshadows Christ, who is both King and Priest.
know: Grandson of Jeconiah (Jehoiachin), the exiled king of Judah.
Led the first return and rebuilt the altar and Temple foundation (Ezra 3).
Haggai calls him God's 'signet ring' (Hag 2:23).
Named in both genealogies of Jesus (Matt 1:12-13; Luke 3:27).
1 Chr 3:19 lists him as a son of Pedaiah, Shealtiel's brother — possibly a levirate or legal-heir arrangement.

people.name: Zeruiah
people.summary: Zeruiah, David's sister, was the mother of his three fierce commanders Abishai, Joab and Asahel, who are usually named after her.
know: Her sons are called 'sons of Zeruiah'
David found them 'too hard' for him

people.name: Abishai
people.summary: Abishai son of Zeruiah went with David into Saul's camp and wanted to kill the sleeping king, but David refused to touch the LORD's anointed. He later commanded part of the army, offered to kill Shimei, and rescued David from a Philistine giant.
know: Urged David to kill Saul
Chief of the Thirty
Saved David's life in battle

people.name: Adonijah
people.role: Son of David, claimant to the throne
people.summary: Adonijah, David's fourth son by Haggith, tried to make himself king as David lay dying, backed by Joab and Abiathar. Nathan and Bathsheba secured Solomon's anointing instead; Adonijah was spared, but when he asked for David's companion Abishag as wife, Solomon saw a claim to the throne and had him executed.
know: Proclaimed himself king at En-rogel
Clung to the horns of the altar
Asked Bathsheba to request Abishag
Executed by Benaiah

people.name: Benjamin
people.summary: Rachel's second son, born near Bethlehem as she died; she named him Benoni ('son of my sorrow'), but Jacob called him Benjamin ('son of the right hand'). Jacob kept him at home when the brothers first went to Egypt; Joseph then demanded him, favoured him with five portions, and tested the brothers by planting his silver cup in Benjamin's sack.
people.catholic: St Paul proudly names himself 'of the tribe of Benjamin' (Rom 11:1; Phil 3:5), as was King Saul, whose name Paul originally bore. Jacob's blessing calls Benjamin 'a ravenous wolf' (Gen 49:27), which some Fathers, such as Tertullian, applied to Paul, the persecutor who became the apostle.
know: Born as Rachel died; first named Benoni (Gen 35:16-18)
Joseph's only full brother
Joseph's cup was hidden in his sack (Gen 44)
Father of ten sons (Gen 46:21)
St Paul was of his tribe (Rom 11:1; Phil 3:5)

people.name: Demetrius II Nicator
people.summary: Son of Demetrius I, who came from Crete, became king after Ptolemy VI defeated Alexander, confirmed Jonathan as high priest but broke faith with him. Driven from Antioch by Tryphon, he granted Simon independence, then was captured by Arsaces king of Persia.
know: 'Demetrius son of Demetrius' (1 Macc 10:67).
Rescued at Antioch by Jewish troops (1 Macc 11:43-51).
Granted Simon immunity (1 Macc 13:34-40).
Captured by Arsaces (1 Macc 14:1-3).

people.name: Herod Antipas
people.summary: Herod Antipas, son of Herod the Great, was tetrarch of Galilee and Perea (4 BC - AD 39). He married Herodias, his brother Philip's wife; rebuked by John the Baptist, he imprisoned him and, trapped by an oath at his birthday feast, had him beheaded. Jesus called him 'that fox'; at the Passion Pilate sent Jesus to him, and he mocked him and sent him back.
people.catholic: Antipas is a figure of conscience stifled by pride and human respect: he 'heard John gladly' yet killed him rather than break a rash oath before his guests. The early Church remembered him with Pilate among those gathered against God's 'holy servant Jesus' (Acts 4:27). Rome later exiled him (Josephus).
know: Tetrarch of Galilee (Lk 3:1) - the 'Herod' of Jesus' ministry.
Beheaded John the Baptist (Mk 6:14-29).
Called 'that fox' by Jesus (Lk 13:32).
Mocked Jesus and became friends with Pilate (Lk 23:8-12).

relations.type: took the wife of his brother

people.name: Hiram
people.summary: Hiram (Huram) king of Tyre sent cedar and craftsmen to build David's palace and made a treaty with Solomon, supplying cedar, cypress and skilled workers for the Temple in exchange for grain and oil. He partnered with Solomon's fleet to Ophir.
know: Supplied cedars of Lebanon for the Temple
Friend of David and Solomon
Called Huram in Chronicles

people.name: Manasseh
people.summary: Manasseh son of Hezekiah reigned fifty-five years, the longest of any king of Judah, and was its most wicked: he rebuilt the high places, set altars to the host of heaven in the Temple, burned his son as an offering, practised sorcery and 'shed very much innocent blood'. Kings blames the Exile on his sins; Chronicles adds that he was taken in chains to Babylon, humbled himself and prayed, and was restored, then removed foreign gods.
people.catholic: Manasseh's repentance in captivity (2 Chr 33:12-13) shows that no sinner is beyond God's mercy. The 'Prayer of Manasseh', a penitential prayer attributed to him, appears in some Bibles and in the appendix of the Clementine Vulgate but is not part of the Catholic canon. Jewish and Christian tradition hold that Isaiah was martyred under him. He is in Jesus' genealogy (Mt 1:10).
know: Reigned 55 years
Filled Jerusalem with idolatry and innocent blood
Taken captive to Babylon and repented (Chronicles)
His sins are given as the cause of the Exile

people.name: Timothy
people.summary: Timothy, a disciple of Lystra, son of a believing Jewish mother and a Greek father, joined Paul on the second missionary journey; Paul circumcised him because of the Jews of the region. He became Paul's closest co-worker, sent to Thessalonica, Corinth and Philippi, co-sender of six Pauline letters, and recipient of 1 and 2 Timothy, which charge him to guard the deposit of faith at Ephesus.
people.catholic: Saints Timothy and Titus are celebrated together on January 26, the day after Paul's Conversion. Tradition holds that Timothy was the first bishop of Ephesus. Paul reminds him to 'stir up the gift of God which is in you through the laying on of my hands' (2 Tim 1:6; cf. 1 Tim 4:14), texts the Church reads as witness to the sacrament of Holy Orders conferred by the laying on of hands (CCC 1590). The Pastoral Letters addressed to him set out the qualifications of bishops and deacons (1 Tim 3) and the duty to 'guard what has been entrusted' (1 Tim 6:20), foundations of apostolic succession and the deposit of faith. His faith, passed down from his grandmother Lois and mother Eunice, makes him a model of faith handed on in the family, the 'domestic church'.
know: From Lystra; Jewish mother, Greek father (Acts 16:1).
Paul calls him 'my true child in faith' (1 Tim 1:2).
Co-sender of 2 Corinthians, Philippians, Colossians, 1-2 Thessalonians and Philemon.
Ordained by the laying on of hands (1 Tim 4:14; 2 Tim 1:6).
Feast with Titus January 26.

people.name: Abimelech (king of Gerar)
people.summary: King of Gerar who took Sarah into his house when Abraham called her his sister; warned by God in a dream, he returned her untouched. He later made a covenant with Abraham at Beersheba. A king Abimelech of Gerar likewise rebuked Isaac for calling Rebekah his sister and made a treaty with him.
people.catholic: God's dream-warning to Abimelech, a foreign king who acts 'in the integrity of my heart' (Gen 20:5-6), shows God's providence protecting the promise and also the moral conscience of Gentiles.
know: Took Sarah, believing her Abraham's sister, and returned her (Gen 20)
Made a covenant with Abraham at Beersheba (Gen 21:22-32)
Rebuked Isaac for the same ruse (Gen 26:6-11)
The Abimelech of Isaac's time may be a successor bearing the same name or title

people.name: Alexander Balas
people.summary: A claimant who presented himself as 'Alexander Epiphanes, the son of Antiochus', seized Ptolemais, won Jonathan's support by naming him high priest, defeated Demetrius I and married Cleopatra, daughter of Ptolemy VI. His father-in-law later turned against him; he fled to Arabia and was beheaded.
know: Called 'Alexander Epiphanes, son of Antiochus' (1 Macc 10:1) — ancient historians considered his claim false.
Made Jonathan high priest (1 Macc 10:18-21).
Married Cleopatra (1 Macc 10:57-58).
Beheaded by Zabdiel the Arabian (1 Macc 11:17).

people.name: Baruch
people.summary: Baruch son of Neriah was Jeremiah's faithful scribe. He wrote the prophet's oracles at his dictation, read the scroll publicly in the Temple, hid with Jeremiah when Jehoiakim burned it, and wrote it out again; he went with Jeremiah into Egypt. The deuterocanonical Book of Baruch is attributed to him, written in Babylon.
people.catholic: The Book of Baruch belongs to the Catholic canon (deuterocanonical). Its hymn to Wisdom, 'she appeared upon earth and lived with men' (Bar 3:37), was read by the Fathers as a prophecy of the Incarnation of the Word, and Bar 3:9-15, 32-4:4 is the sixth Old Testament reading of the Easter Vigil. Bar 5 ('Jerusalem, take off your robe of mourning') is read in Advent.
know: Son of Neriah, brother of Seraiah the quartermaster.
Wrote and read Jeremiah's scroll; it was burned by King Jehoiakim (Jer 36).
Received a personal oracle: 'your life I will give you as a prize of war' (Jer 45).
The Book of Baruch (incl. ch. 6, the Letter of Jeremiah) is in the Catholic Old Testament.

people.name: Boaz
people.summary: Wealthy landowner of Bethlehem, kinsman of Elimelech, son of Salmon (and of Rahab, per Matthew). He showed kindness to the gleaner Ruth, and when she asked him to spread the corner of his garment over her as near kinsman, he settled the claim of a nearer kinsman at the town gate, bought Elimelech's land, and married Ruth. Their son Obed was David's grandfather.
people.catholic: The Church Fathers read Boaz, the go'el (kinsman-redeemer) who freely takes the poor foreign widow as his bride, as a figure of Christ the Redeemer who unites the Church of the Gentiles to himself. Born in Bethlehem and ancestor of David, he stands in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus (Mt 1:5). His greeting to the reapers, 'The LORD be with you' (Ruth 2:4), echoes in the liturgy.
know: Kinsman of Elimelech (Ruth 2:1).
'The LORD be with you' (Ruth 2:4).
Acted as kinsman-redeemer at the city gate (Ruth 4:1-10).
Husband of Ruth, father of Obed.
Son of Salmon and Rahab (Mt 1:5).

people.name: Jehoram (Joram) of Judah
people.summary: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat married Athaliah, Ahab's daughter, and walked in the ways of Ahab's house. On taking the throne he killed all his brothers. Edom and Libnah revolted; a letter from Elijah foretold his punishment, and he died of a terrible disease of the bowels, 'to no one's regret'.
know: Husband of Athaliah
Murdered his six brothers
Received a letter from Elijah
Called Joram in Matthew 1:8

people.name: Judas Iscariot
people.summary: Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, was one of the Twelve and kept the common purse, from which he stole. He agreed with the chief priests to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver, left the Last Supper into the night, and handed Jesus over in Gethsemane with a kiss. Seized with remorse, he returned the silver and hanged himself; Matthias was chosen to take his place.
people.catholic: Judas shows that even one chosen and close to Christ can freely refuse grace. The Fathers contrast him with Peter: both failed, but Peter repented and trusted in mercy while Judas despaired. Matthew sees the thirty pieces of silver and the potter's field as fulfilment of prophecy (Mt 27:9-10). The Church does not declare any individual damned, but Jesus' own words about him are grave (Mt 26:24).
know: Son of Simon Iscariot (Jn 6:71).
Betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver (Mt 26:14-16).
Betrayed him with a kiss (Lk 22:47-48).
Replaced among the Twelve by Matthias (Acts 1:26).

people.name: Shaphan
people.summary: Shaphan son of Azaliah, Josiah's scribe, received the book of the law from Hilkiah and read it before the king. His family were Jeremiah's protectors: his son Ahikam and grandson Gedaliah.
know: Read the rediscovered law to Josiah
Father of Ahikam

people.name: Abednego (Azariah)
people.summary: Azariah, renamed Abednego in Babylon, was one of Daniel's three companions. In the Greek text of Daniel 3 it is Azariah (Azarias) who stands in the furnace and prays the great prayer of repentance on behalf of his people before the three sing their hymn of praise.
people.catholic: The three young men who would not worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image and were preserved in the furnace are honoured as models of fidelity unto martyrdom; Mattathias cites them (1 Mac 2:59) and the Fathers saw the 'fourth man' in the fire as a figure of the Son of God. Their hymn in the Greek text, the Song of the Three (Dan 3:52-90, the 'Benedicite'), is the Old Testament canticle of Sunday Morning Prayer in the Liturgy of the Hours (Dan 3:57-88, 56 in Weeks I and III; Dan 3:52-57 in Weeks II and IV), and it is traditionally prayed in thanksgiving after Mass. The Prayer of Azariah (Dan 3:26-45), a confession of the nation's sin and plea for mercy, is used in the Lenten liturgy and as a canticle in the Liturgy of the Hours ('with a contrite heart and a humble spirit let us be received').
know: Hebrew name Azariah (Greek Azarias); Babylonian name Abednego (Dan 1:7).
Prayed the Prayer of Azariah in the fire (Dan 3:25-45).
Survived the fiery furnace (Dan 3).

people.name: Jeroboam II
people.summary: Jeroboam II son of Jehoash reigned forty-one years, the most prosperous of Israel's kings, restoring its borders from Hamath to the Dead Sea as the prophet Jonah son of Amittai had foretold. Yet his reign's wealth and injustice drew the denunciations of Amos and Hosea.
know: Reigned 41 years in Samaria
Restored Israel's borders as Jonah prophesied
Amos and Hosea prophesied in his day

people.name: Korah
people.summary: Levite, son of Izhar and cousin of Moses and Aaron. With Dathan, Abiram, On and 250 leaders he challenged the authority of Moses and the priesthood of Aaron, claiming that all the congregation was holy. The earth swallowed the rebels' households and fire consumed the 250 who offered incense, but Korah's sons did not die.
people.catholic: Korah's rebellion is the classic biblical case of rejecting divinely instituted authority and grasping at priesthood not given by God; Jude 11 names it among the sins of false teachers, and Sirach 45:18-19 recalls it. The Church has read it as a warning against schism and against claiming sacred office without a call. His surviving descendants became temple singers, and many Psalms are titled 'of the sons of Korah'.
know: Son of Izhar, grandson of Kohath (Exo 6:21).
Led a revolt against Moses and Aaron (Num 16).
The earth swallowed the rebels (Num 16:31-33).
'The sons of Korah didn't die' (Num 26:11).
Cited in Jude 11 ('the rebellion of Korah').

people.name: Lysias
people.summary: A nobleman 'of royal lineage' left by Antiochus IV in charge of the kingdom and of the young Antiochus V. His armies were defeated by Judas (at Beth-zur), he later made Antiochus V king, and negotiated peace with the Jews, but was killed with the boy-king by Demetrius I's army.
people.catholic: In 2 Maccabees he concludes after his defeat that 'the Hebrews could not be overcome, because the Almighty God fought for them' (2 Macc 11:13).
know: Regent from the Euphrates to Egypt (1 Macc 3:32-33).
Defeated by Judas at Beth-zur (1 Macc 4:28-35).
Made Antiochus V king (1 Macc 6:17).
Killed with Antiochus V (1 Macc 7:2-4).

people.name: Og
people.summary: King of Bashan, one of the last of the Rephaim, whose iron bedstead was nine cubits long. He came out against Israel at Edrei and was defeated, and his kingdom was given to the half-tribe of Manasseh.
people.catholic: With Sihon, Og is named in Psalms 135 and 136 among the kings God struck down for his people.
know: King of Bashan (Num 21:33).
Last of the Rephaim; his bed was nine cubits long (Deut 3:11).
Defeated at Edrei (Deut 3:1-3).

people.name: Uriah
people.summary: Uriah the Hittite, one of David's Thirty mighty men, refused to go home to his wife while the Ark and army were in the field. David then sent him back to Joab carrying the letter that arranged his death at Rabbah.
people.catholic: Uriah's loyalty and integrity throw David's sin into sharp relief; Matthew's genealogy keeps his name before the Messiah's ('her who had been Uriah's wife'), a reminder that Christ entered a history marked by sin to redeem it.
know: A Hittite in David's elite guard
Would not go home while the army camped
Carried his own death warrant to Joab
Named in Matthew 1:6

people.name: Abijah
people.summary: Abijah (Abijam) son of Rehoboam reigned three years. Kings judges him as walking in his father's sins, while Chronicles records his speech on Mount Zemaraim defending the Davidic covenant and the true priesthood before defeating Jeroboam.
know: Also called Abijam
Reigned three years
Defeated Jeroboam after appealing to the 'covenant of salt' with David

people.name: Amnon
people.summary: Amnon, David's firstborn, became obsessed with his half-sister Tamar, raped her by a ruse and then hated her. Two years later her brother Absalom had him killed at a sheep-shearing feast.
know: Son of Ahinoam of Jezreel
Violated his half-sister Tamar
Murdered by Absalom's servants

people.name: Bacchides
people.summary: A trusted 'friend of the king' under Demetrius I who installed Alcimus as high priest, defeated and killed Judas at Elasa, fortified Judea, and after failing to destroy Jonathan made peace with him.
know: Killed Judas (1 Macc 9:1-18).
Made peace with Jonathan (1 Macc 9:70-72).

people.name: Hazael
people.summary: God told Elijah at Horeb to anoint Hazael king over Syria. Sent by the sick Ben-hadad to Elisha, Hazael watched the prophet weep at the evil he would do to Israel; the next day he smothered Ben-hadad and reigned. He cruelly oppressed Israel under Jehu and Jehoahaz and threatened Jerusalem until Joash paid him off.
know: Named to Elijah at Horeb
Elisha wept foreseeing his cruelty
Seized the throne of Damascus
Oppressed Israel for decades

people.name: Ishmael son of Nethaniah
people.summary: Ishmael, of the royal line, was sent by Baalis king of Ammon to kill Gedaliah, the governor Babylon set over Judah. He murdered Gedaliah at Mizpah, massacred pilgrims, and took the remnant captive, but fled to Ammon when Johanan son of Kareah pursued him.
know: Of royal Davidic descent
Murdered Gedaliah
Murdered Gedaliah despite Johanan's warning (Jer 40:13-41:3).
His crime drove the remnant to flee to Egypt.
The fast of the seventh month (Zech 7:5; 8:19) is traditionally linked to Gedaliah's murder.

people.name: Jehoiada (father of Benaiah)
people.summary: Jehoiada of Kabzeel, called 'the chief priest' in 1 Chr 27:5, was the father of David's warrior Benaiah.
know: Not the later priest who crowned Joash

people.name: Naomi
people.summary: Wife of Elimelech of Bethlehem. Widowed in Moab and bereaved of both sons, she returned home calling herself Mara ('bitter'), accompanied by her Moabite daughter-in-law Ruth. She guided Ruth to Boaz, and when Obed was born the women said, 'A son is born to Naomi.'
people.catholic: Naomi's journey from emptiness to fullness is read as a parable of God's hidden providence. The Church's tradition has seen in the bond of Naomi and Ruth a picture of Israel welcoming the Gentiles, and Naomi nursing Obed, the grandfather of David, as the hidden preparation for the Messiah.
know: Wife of Elimelech, mother of Mahlon and Chilion (Ruth 1:2).
Asked to be called Mara, 'bitter' (Ruth 1:20).
Arranged Ruth's approach to Boaz (Ruth 3:1-4).
Nursed her grandson Obed (Ruth 4:16-17).

people.name: Tryphon
people.summary: A former officer of Alexander Balas who championed the boy Antiochus VI, then plotted to seize the kingdom himself. He captured Jonathan at Ptolemais by treachery, extorted ransom from Simon, killed Jonathan and later Antiochus VI, and was finally besieged at Dor and driven out by Antiochus VII.
know: Killed Jonathan at Bascama (1 Macc 13:23).
Murdered the young Antiochus VI (1 Macc 13:31).
Fled to Orthosia (1 Macc 15:37).

people.name: Adam
people.summary: The first man, formed by God from the dust of the ground and given the breath of life, placed in the garden of Eden to till and keep it. With Eve he disobeyed God's command by eating from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, and they were driven from the garden. He fathered Cain, Abel and Seth, and lived 930 years.
people.catholic: St Paul calls Adam 'a type of him who was to come' (Rom 5:14): as sin and death entered through the first Adam's disobedience, grace and life come through Christ, the New Adam (1 Cor 15:22, 45). The Catechism treats man's creation in God's image, original justice, and the Fall at length (CCC 355-379, 385-421), teaching that Adam's sin is transmitted to all humanity as original sin (CCC 404) and that Christ is the new Adam (CCC 359, 504). The Exsultet at the Easter Vigil sings of the 'truly necessary sin of Adam' and the 'happy fault' that won so great a Redeemer. An ancient tradition placed Adam's grave at Golgotha, which is why a skull is often painted at the foot of the crucifix.
know: Formed from the dust and given the breath of life (Gen 2:7)
Named the animals and received Eve as a suitable helper (Gen 2:18-23)
His disobedience brought sin and death into the world (Rom 5:12)
Christ is called the 'last Adam' (1 Cor 15:45)
Father of Cain, Abel and Seth; lived 930 years (Gen 5:5)

people.name: Ahasuerus
people.summary: The Persian king (usually identified with Xerxes I, 486-465 BC) who ruled 127 provinces from Susa. He deposed Queen Vashti, chose Esther as queen, approved Haman's decree against the Jews, but, after Esther's intercession, hanged Haman, elevated Mordecai and issued a counter-decree permitting the Jews to defend themselves.
people.catholic: In the Greek additions God himself 'changed the spirit of the king to gentleness' when Esther approached (Est 5:1-2 in the additions), and the king's second letter acknowledges the Jews as 'sons of the living God, the most high and mighty' (Est 8:13 addition). Traditional Marian readings see in the king who extends his golden sceptre to Esther an image of God who grants Mary's intercession.
know: Usually identified with Xerxes I.
Ruled 127 provinces 'from India' (Est 1:1).
Extended the golden sceptre to Esther (Est 5:2).
An accusation against Judah was written in his reign (Ezra 4:6).

people.name: Ahikam
people.summary: Ahikam son of Shaphan was among Josiah's delegation to Huldah, and later protected Jeremiah from being put to death.
know: Protected Jeremiah
Father of Gedaliah

people.name: Cyrus
people.summary: Cyrus the Great, founder of the Persian Empire, conquered Babylon in 539 BC and issued the decree allowing the Jews to return home and rebuild the Temple, sending back the sacred vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken. Isaiah names him as the Lord's 'shepherd' and 'anointed' long in advance.
people.catholic: Cyrus is the only Gentile ruler whom Scripture calls the LORD's 'anointed' (Hebrew mashiach, Isa 45:1). The Church reads him as an instrument of Providence: God uses even a pagan king to fulfil his word through Jeremiah (2 Chr 36:22) and free his people, a figure of Christ the Anointed who frees humanity from the captivity of sin. His decree closes the Hebrew Bible (2 Chr 36:23) and opens Ezra.
know: Conquered Babylon in 539 BC.
His decree (Ezra 1:1-4) allowed the return and the rebuilding of the Temple.
Called God's 'anointed' and 'shepherd' in Isaiah 44:28-45:1.
Daniel served into his reign (Dan 1:21; 6:28).

people.name: Demetrius I Soter
people.summary: Son of Seleucus IV, held hostage in Rome, who escaped, seized the throne by killing Antiochus V and Lysias (161 BC), installed Alcimus as high priest and sent Bacchides and Nicanor against Judas. He later lost the throne to Alexander Balas despite lavish offers to Jonathan.
know: 'Demetrius the son of Seleucus came out of Rome' (1 Macc 7:1).
Appointed Alcimus high priest (1 Macc 7:9).
Killed in battle with Alexander Balas (1 Macc 10:48-50).

people.name: Ithamar
people.summary: Youngest son of Aaron. He oversaw the accounting of the tabernacle materials and supervised the Gershonite and Merarite Levites in the wilderness. The priestly house of Ithamar continued alongside that of Eleazar.
know: Fourth son of Aaron.
Supervised the tabernacle records (Exo 38:21).
Directed the Gershonites and Merarites (Num 4:28, 33).
Later priestly courses were divided between Eleazar's and Ithamar's houses (1 Chr 24:3-4).

people.name: Joram (Jehoram) of Israel
people.summary: Joram (Jehoram) son of Ahab reigned twelve years. He campaigned with Jehoshaphat against Mesha of Moab, when Elisha provided water; the king of Israel in the stories of Naaman and the siege of Samaria is probably he. Wounded at Ramoth-gilead, he was killed by Jehu at Naboth's plot in Jezreel, ending Ahab's dynasty.
know: Son of Ahab and brother of Ahaziah
Fought Mesha of Moab
Killed by Jehu's arrow on Naboth's land

people.name: Meshach (Mishael)
people.summary: Mishael, renamed Meshach in Babylon, was one of Daniel's three companions. He refused to worship the golden image and was delivered from the fiery furnace with Hananiah and Azariah.
people.catholic: The three young men who would not worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image and were preserved in the furnace are honoured as models of fidelity unto martyrdom; Mattathias cites them (1 Mac 2:59) and the Fathers saw the 'fourth man' in the fire as a figure of the Son of God. Their hymn in the Greek text, the Song of the Three (Dan 3:52-90, the 'Benedicite'), is the Old Testament canticle of Sunday Morning Prayer in the Liturgy of the Hours (Dan 3:57-88, 56 in Weeks I and III; Dan 3:52-57 in Weeks II and IV), and it is traditionally prayed in thanksgiving after Mass.
know: Hebrew name Mishael; Babylonian name Meshach (Dan 1:7).
Survived the fiery furnace (Dan 3).
Named with his companions in the closing verse of the Benedicite (Dan 3:88).

people.name: Micaiah son of Imlah
people.summary: Micaiah son of Imlah was the one prophet Ahab hated 'because he never prophesies good concerning me'. Before the battle of Ramoth-gilead he first mocked the court prophets' message, then foretold Ahab's death and revealed a lying spirit in their mouths; struck by Zedekiah son of Chenaanah, he was imprisoned on bread and water.
people.catholic: Micaiah - 'what the LORD says to me, that I will speak' - is a model of prophetic integrity against the pressure of a court consensus, foreshadowing Christ struck before the high priest.
know: Stood alone against 400 prophets
Foretold Ahab's death
Saw the LORD on his throne with the host of heaven
Imprisoned for his message

people.name: Raguel
people.summary: Tobit's kinsman living at Ecbatana in Media, father of Sarah. He welcomed Tobias, gave him Sarah in marriage 'according to the law of Moses', secretly dug a grave expecting him to die, and then celebrated a fourteen-day wedding feast when he survived.
know: Calls Tobit 'my cousin' (Tob 7:2).
Dug a grave for Tobias on the wedding night (Tob 8:9-12).
Gave half his property to Tobias (Tob 8:21).

people.name: Reuben
people.summary: Jacob's firstborn, by Leah. He lay with his father's concubine Bilhah, and so lost the pre-eminence of the firstborn. When his brothers plotted against Joseph he persuaded them to throw him into a pit instead of killing him, meaning to rescue him, and later offered his own sons as surety for Benjamin.
people.catholic: Reuben's instability ('boiling over like water', Gen 49:4) costs him the birthright, which 1 Chronicles says passed to Joseph's sons while leadership went to Judah (1 Ch 5:1-2) — a recurring biblical pattern in which God's choice does not follow birth order.
know: Firstborn of Jacob and Leah (Gen 29:32)
Lay with Bilhah and lost his birthright (Gen 35:22; 49:3-4)
Tried to save Joseph from the pit (Gen 37:21-22, 29)
Pledged his sons for Benjamin's safety (Gen 42:37)

people.name: Shadrach (Hananiah)
people.summary: Hananiah, renamed Shadrach in Babylon, was one of Daniel's three companions from Judah. With Mishael and Azariah he refused to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden statue, was thrown bound into the fiery furnace, and walked unharmed in the flames with a fourth figure 'like a son of the gods'.
people.catholic: The three young men who would not worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image and were preserved in the furnace are honoured as models of fidelity unto martyrdom; Mattathias cites them (1 Mac 2:59) and the Fathers saw the 'fourth man' in the fire as a figure of the Son of God. Their hymn in the Greek text, the Song of the Three (Dan 3:52-90, the 'Benedicite'), is the Old Testament canticle of Sunday Morning Prayer in the Liturgy of the Hours (Dan 3:57-88, 56 in Weeks I and III; Dan 3:52-57 in Weeks II and IV), and it is traditionally prayed in thanksgiving after Mass.
know: Hebrew name Hananiah; Babylonian name Shadrach (Dan 1:7).
Shared Daniel's vegetable diet and was found ten times wiser than the magicians (Dan 1).
Survived the fiery furnace (Dan 3) and sang the Benedicite.
Promoted by Nebuchadnezzar afterwards (Dan 3:97).

people.name: Jezebel
people.summary: Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, married Ahab and zealously promoted the worship of Baal, killing the LORD's prophets and maintaining 850 prophets of Baal and Asherah. She vowed to kill Elijah after Carmel and arranged Naboth's judicial murder with false witnesses. At Jehu's revolt she painted her eyes and taunted him from a window, and was thrown down and eaten by dogs as Elijah had foretold.
people.catholic: Jezebel became a byword for seductive idolatry - Revelation calls a false prophetess at Thyatira 'Jezebel' (Rev 2:20). Her persecution of Elijah is a type of the world's hostility to God's prophets, as Herodias's hostility to John the Baptist, the 'Elijah who was to come', has long been compared to it.
know: Phoenician princess, wife of Ahab
Killed the LORD's prophets
Threatened Elijah's life
Had Naboth killed by false witness
Thrown from a window at Jehu's command

people.name: Jotham
people.summary: Jotham son of Uzziah governed during his father's leprosy and then reigned sixteen years. He did right, built the upper gate of the Temple and subdued the Ammonites, 'because he ordered his ways before the LORD', though the people still sacrificed on the high places.
know: Regent during Uzziah's leprosy
Built the upper gate of the Temple
Isaiah, Hosea and Micah prophesied in his time

people.name: Micah (of Ephraim)
people.summary: Man of the hill country of Ephraim who returned stolen silver to his mother, set up a household shrine with images, an ephod and teraphim, and hired a wandering Levite as his priest. The migrating Danites stole his images and his priest, and he could not resist them.
people.catholic: Micah's shrine illustrates the confusion of the period when 'there was no king in Israel; everyone did that which was right in his own eyes' (Jdg 17:6): worship invented by private initiative rather than received from God. The Church reads it as a contrast with true, ordered worship.
know: Lived in the hill country of Ephraim (Jdg 17:1).
Made a shrine with images and an ephod (Jdg 17:5).
Hired a Levite as priest (Jdg 17:10-13).
Robbed by the Danites (Jdg 18:14-26).

people.name: Tobit
people.summary: An Israelite of the tribe of Naphtali deported to Nineveh, Tobit remained faithful to the Law, gave generous alms and risked his life to bury executed fellow Jews. Blinded by bird droppings, he prayed for death; God answered by sending the angel Raphael, who guided his son Tobias on a journey that brought back Tobit's money, a bride for Tobias and the cure of Tobit's eyes. He died in old age after a hymn of praise and a prophecy of Jerusalem's glory.
people.catholic: This book is one of the deuterocanonical books — part of the Greek Old Testament (Septuagint) used by the apostolic Church, listed in the canon by the councils of Rome (382), Hippo (393) and Carthage (397), reaffirmed at Florence and defined at Trent (1546) — which Protestant Bibles place among the 'Apocrypha'. Tobit is a model of the corporal works of mercy, especially burying the dead, and of almsgiving: 'alms delivers from death, and it purges away all sin' (Tob 12:9). His patient endurance under trial and his canticle (Tob 13) are prayed in the Liturgy of the Hours. The Church reads the book as a lesson in divine Providence, in which God's care works quietly through ordinary family life and the ministry of angels.
know: Tribe of Naphtali, exiled to Nineveh under 'Enemessar' (Shalmaneser).
Buried executed Israelites at the risk of his life (Tob 1:17-19; 2:3-8).
Blinded and then healed by the fish's gall at Raphael's instruction (Tob 11:7-15).
His instruction to Tobias (Tob 4) is a classic of Old Testament moral teaching ('what you yourself hate, do to no man', Tob 4:15).
Died aged 158 (Tob 14:11).

people.name: Achish
people.summary: Achish king of Gath twice received David as a fugitive - first David feigned madness before him, later he gave David the town of Ziklag - but the Philistine lords refused to let David fight against Israel.
know: David feigned madness before him
Gave David Ziklag

people.name: Hadadezer
people.summary: Hadadezer son of Rehob, king of Zobah in Syria, was defeated by David, who took his golden shields to Jerusalem; he later aided the Ammonites against David.
know: Defeated by David in Syria

people.name: Ishmael
people.summary: Abraham's son by Hagar, named by the angel because 'the LORD has heard your affliction'. Circumcised at thirteen, he was sent away with his mother after Isaac's birth, grew up in the wilderness as an archer, and married an Egyptian. God blessed him to become a great nation with twelve princes; he and Isaac buried Abraham, and he died at 137.
people.catholic: God's promise to bless Ishmael (Gen 17:20; 21:13, 18) shows his care beyond the chosen line. Many Muslims regard Ishmael as their forefather; the Church regards with esteem Muslims, who 'profess to hold the faith of Abraham' (CCC 841, quoting Lumen Gentium 16).
know: Name means 'God hears' (Gen 16:11)
Circumcised at 13 with Abraham (Gen 17:25-26)
Became an archer in the wilderness of Paran (Gen 21:20-21)
Father of twelve princes (Gen 25:13-16)
Buried Abraham with Isaac (Gen 25:9)

people.name: Nabal
people.summary: Nabal ('fool'), a rich and surly man of Maon with flocks at Carmel, insulted David's men; after Abigail's intercession he was struck by the LORD and died.
know: His name means 'fool'
Died ten days after hearing what Abigail had done

people.name: Naboth
people.summary: Naboth of Jezreel refused to sell Ahab his ancestral vineyard: 'The LORD forbid that I should give the inheritance of my fathers to you.' Jezebel had him falsely accused of cursing God and the king, and he was stoned outside the city; Elijah then pronounced doom on Ahab and Jezebel.
people.catholic: St. Ambrose's treatise 'On Naboth' made him a classic figure in Catholic social teaching against the greed of the powerful, and the Fathers saw in him a type of Christ: an innocent man condemned by false witnesses on a charge of blasphemy and executed outside the city.
know: Refused to sell his ancestral inheritance
Condemned by two false witnesses
Stoned outside the city
His blood was avenged on Ahab's house

people.name: Phinehas
people.summary: Son of Eleazar and grandson of Aaron. When an Israelite brought a Midianite woman into the camp during the apostasy at Peor, Phinehas killed them both, the plague stopped, and God gave him 'a covenant of an everlasting priesthood'. He later led the delegation to the tribes east of the Jordan and served as priest at Bethel in the days of the judges.
people.catholic: Phinehas is Scripture's emblem of zeal for God's honour: Psalm 106:30-31 says it was 'credited to him for righteousness', and Sirach 45:23-24 calls him 'third in glory' after Moses and Aaron. Mattathias explicitly modelled his zeal on Phinehas (1 Mac 2:26, 54). The covenant of perpetual priesthood granted to him (Num 25:13) is read by the Church as finding its fulfilment in the eternal priesthood of Christ.
know: Son of Eleazar, grandson of Aaron (Exo 6:25).
Stopped the plague at Peor (Num 25:7-8).
Received 'the covenant of an everlasting priesthood' (Num 25:13).
Ministered before the ark in Judges 20:28.

people.name: Sennacherib
people.summary: Sennacherib king of Assyria invaded Judah in Hezekiah's fourteenth year, took its fortified cities and sent the Rabshakeh to demand Jerusalem's surrender, mocking the LORD. After Hezekiah's prayer, the angel of the LORD struck the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib returned to Nineveh, where his sons killed him while he worshipped in the temple of Nisroch.
know: Besieged Jerusalem in 701 BC
Mocked the God of Israel
His army was struck by the angel of the LORD
Killed by his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer

people.name: Shem
people.summary: The eldest son of Noah, who with Japheth covered their father's nakedness respectfully. Noah blessed 'the LORD, the God of Shem'. From him descend Eber, Terah and Abraham; he is the eponymous ancestor of the 'Semitic' peoples.
people.catholic: Noah's blessing of the God of Shem points to the line through which God's promise passes to Abraham, Israel and Christ, whom Luke lists as 'son of Shem' (Lk 3:36). Sirach 49:16 says 'Shem and Seth were honoured among men'.
know: Eldest son of Noah (Gen 10:21)
Covered his father's nakedness with Japheth (Gen 9:23)
Blessed by Noah (Gen 9:26)
Ancestor of Abraham and of Jesus (Lk 3:36)

people.name: Timotheus
people.summary: A commander of the Ammonites and of Gentile forces in Gilead repeatedly defeated by Judas; 2 Maccabees reports a Timotheus killed hiding in a cistern at Gazara.
know: Defeated across the Jordan (1 Macc 5:6-8; 5:37-44).
The Timotheus of 2 Maccabees may be one or more men.

people.name: Ahithophel
people.summary: Ahithophel the Gilonite was David's counsellor, whose advice was regarded 'as if a man inquired at the word of God'. He joined Absalom's revolt; when Absalom preferred Hushai's counsel, Ahithophel went home, set his house in order and hanged himself.
people.catholic: Ahithophel - the trusted friend who betrays the king and then hangs himself - is widely read by the Fathers as a type of Judas (cf. Ps 41:9, Jn 13:18). David's prayer 'turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness' is answered through Hushai.

people.name: Araunah
people.summary: Araunah (Ornan) the Jebusite owned the threshing floor where the destroying angel stopped. He offered it free, but David insisted on paying, built an altar there, and the plague ended; Solomon's Temple was built on that spot.
people.catholic: David's words 'I will not offer to the LORD burnt offerings that cost me nothing' are a classic text on true sacrifice. The Chronicler identifies the site with Mount Moriah (2 Chr 3:1), linking Abraham's offering of Isaac, David's altar and the Temple - a typological thread Christian readers carry to Calvary.
know: Sold his threshing floor to David
Site of the future Temple
Called Ornan in Chronicles

people.name: Ben-hadad
people.summary: Ben-hadad king of Syria besieged Samaria under Ahab and was twice defeated; Ahab spared him, against the LORD's will. In Elisha's day he again besieged Samaria, sought Elisha's capture at Dothan, and when sick sent Hazael to ask Elisha whether he would recover; Hazael smothered him and seized the throne.

Besieged Samaria to famine
Murdered by Hazael

people.name: Gershon
people.summary: Eldest son of Levi. His descendants, the Gershonites, carried the curtains and coverings of the tabernacle in the wilderness.

people.name: Hilkiah
people.summary: Hilkiah, high priest under King Josiah, found 'the book of the law' in the Temple during its repair and gave it to Shaphan the scribe. He led the delegation to the prophetess Huldah and carried out Josiah's purge of idolatrous objects from the Temple.
people.catholic: The finding of the book of the law under Hilkiah - widely identified with Deuteronomy - sparked Josiah's reform and covenant renewal, a biblical example of renewal of the Church through rediscovery of the Word of God.
know: Found the book of the law in the Temple
Consulted Huldah for Josiah
Removed Baal's vessels from the Temple
Ancestor of Ezra

people.name: Machir
people.summary: Firstborn son of Manasseh, born in Egypt and raised on Joseph's knees. His descendants, the Machirites, conquered Gilead east of the Jordan, which Moses gave them.
know: His children were born on Joseph's knees (Gen 50:23)
Father of Gilead (Num 26:29)
Not Machir son of Ammiel of David's time
Son of Manasseh; his children were born on Joseph's knees (Gen 50:23).
Father of Gilead (Num 26:29).

people.name: Menelaus
people.summary: Brother of Simon the Benjamite, sent to Antiochus IV by Jason, who outbid him for the high priesthood. He stole Temple vessels, arranged the murder of Onias III, bribed his way out of trials, guided Antiochus when he plundered the Temple, and was finally executed by being thrown into a tower of ashes at Beroea.
know: Not of the high-priestly family (2 Macc 4:23-25).
Had Onias murdered (2 Macc 4:34).
Executed in the ashes at Beroea (2 Macc 13:3-8).

people.name: Simeon
people.summary: Second son of Jacob and Leah. With Levi he avenged the violation of their sister Dinah by massacring the men of Shechem, which Jacob condemned. Joseph later kept him bound in Egypt as a hostage until the brothers returned with Benjamin.
people.catholic: Jacob's deathbed words curse the anger of Simeon and Levi (Gen 49:5-7), while Judith later prays to 'the Lord God of my father Simeon' and recalls his zeal (Jdt 9:2) — two readings within Scripture of the same violent act.
know: Second son of Jacob and Leah (Gen 29:33)
With Levi, killed the men of Shechem (Gen 34:25)
Held as hostage in Egypt (Gen 42:24)
Jacob rebuked his violence (Gen 49:5-7)

people.name: Sisera
people.summary: Commander of the army of Jabin king of Canaan, with nine hundred chariots of iron. Routed by Barak at the Kishon, he fled on foot to the tent of Heber the Kenite, where Jael gave him milk and then drove a tent peg through his temple while he slept.
people.catholic: Sisera's fall at the hand of a woman is celebrated in the Song of Deborah; the Fathers saw in it how God brings down the proud through the lowly, a theme echoed in Mary's Magnificat (Lk 1:52).
know: Commander of Jabin's army (Jdg 4:2).
Defeated at the Kishon (Jdg 4:15).
Killed by Jael with a tent peg (Jdg 4:21).
His mother waits at the window in the Song of Deborah (Jdg 5:28).

people.name: The Rabshakeh
people.summary: The Rabshakeh (a high Assyrian title, 'chief cupbearer') stood by the conduit of the upper pool and, speaking Hebrew so the people on the wall would hear, mocked Hezekiah's trust in the LORD and demanded surrender.
know: Refused to speak in Aramaic
Mocked trust in the LORD

people.name: Cain
people.summary: The firstborn son of Adam and Eve, a tiller of the ground. When God accepted Abel's offering but not his, Cain in anger killed his brother in the field, then asked, 'Am I my brother's keeper?' God sent him away as a wanderer but put a mark on him so no one would kill him; he settled in the land of Nod and founded a city named after his son Enoch.
people.catholic: The Catechism presents Cain's murder of Abel as the first fruit of sin spreading after the Fall (CCC 401) and as Scripture's revelation of anger and envy at the root of violence against human life (CCC 2259). The New Testament holds him up as a warning: 1 John 3:12 says he 'was of the evil one', and Jude 11 warns against 'the way of Cain'. St Augustine's City of God makes Cain the founder of the earthly city built on self-love, in contrast to Abel the pilgrim of the city of God. God's protection of Cain is often cited as a sign that even the guilty keep their dignity.
know: Firstborn of Adam and Eve, a farmer (Gen 4:1-2)
Killed his brother Abel out of envy (Gen 4:8)
'Am I my brother's keeper?' (Gen 4:9)
God marked him so that no one would kill him (Gen 4:15)
Father of Enoch; built the first city (Gen 4:17)

people.name: Darius I the Persian
people.summary: Darius I (522-486 BC), the Persian king in whose reign Haggai and Zechariah prophesied. When local officials questioned the rebuilding of the Temple, he searched the archives, found Cyrus' decree, confirmed it and paid for the work, and the Temple was completed in his sixth year.
people.catholic: Darius is remembered as another Gentile ruler whom Providence used to restore true worship in Jerusalem. He should not be confused with 'Darius the Mede' of the book of Daniel.
know: Confirmed Cyrus' decree after finding it at Ecbatana (Ezra 6:1-12).
The Second Temple was finished in his sixth year (Ezra 6:15).
Haggai and Zechariah date their prophecies by his reign.
Distinct from 'Darius the Mede' in Daniel.

people.name: James, 'brother of the Lord'
people.role: Kinsman of Jesus; leader of the Jerusalem Church
people.summary: Named first among Jesus' 'brothers' at Nazareth (Mt 13:55; Mk 6:3), James is 'James the less' whose mother Mary watched at the cross (Mk 15:40). The risen Christ appeared to him (1 Cor 15:7), and he became a leader of the church in Jerusalem, speaking decisively at the Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15:13-21). Paul calls him 'the Lord's brother' and one of the pillars of the Church (Gal 1:19; 2:9).
people.catholic: Following St Jerome, the Church understands 'brother' here in the broad biblical sense of kinsman: James and Joses are sons of another Mary, not of the Virgin Mary (CCC 500). Catholic tradition generally identifies him with the apostle James son of Alphaeus ('St James the Less') and as author of the Letter of James, whose instruction on anointing the sick is the scriptural basis of that sacrament (Jas 5:14-15; CCC 1510). Tradition (Hegesippus) and the historian Josephus record his death by stoning in Jerusalem around AD 62.
know: Called 'the Lord's brother' (Gal 1:19) - a kinsman, not a son of Mary (CCC 500).
His mother was 'Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses' (Mk 15:40).
Saw the risen Lord (1 Cor 15:7) and, after Peter spoke, gave the decisive judgment at the Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15:7-21).
Catholic tradition generally identifies him with James son of Alphaeus and with the author of the Letter of James.
people.feast: May 3 (as St James the Less, with St Philip)

people.name: Jephunneh
people.summary: The Kenizzite father of Caleb.
know: Father of Caleb (Num 13:6).
Called a Kenizzite (Num 32:12).

people.name: Michal
people.role: Daughter of Saul, wife of David
people.summary: Michal, Saul's younger daughter, loved David and became his wife; she saved him by letting him down through a window and deceiving Saul's men with an idol in the bed. Saul gave her to Paltiel, but David reclaimed her when he became king. When she despised David for dancing before the Ark, Scripture notes she had no child to the day of her death.
people.catholic: Michal's contempt for David's joyful, humble dancing before the Ark contrasts with the joy that greets the new Ark in Luke 1, where John leaps in Elizabeth's womb before Mary. Spiritual writers use her as an image of pride that cannot rejoice in God's presence.
know: Loved David and saved his life
Given to Paltiel, then returned to David
Despised David's dancing before the Ark
Had no children

people.name: Nahor (brother of Abraham)
people.summary: A son of Terah and brother of Abraham who stayed in Mesopotamia. He married his niece Milcah and had eight sons by her, including Bethuel, father of Rebekah, and four by his concubine Reumah. His household became the source of wives for Isaac and Jacob.
know: Married his niece Milcah (Gen 11:29)
Grandfather of Rebekah and great-grandfather of Leah and Rachel
Laban swore by 'the God of Nahor' (Gen 31:53)
His city was Haran in Aram Naharaim (Gen 24:10)

people.name: Nethaniah son of Elishama
people.summary: Nethaniah son of Elishama, of the royal line, was the father of Ishmael who assassinated Gedaliah.

people.name: Silas
people.summary: Silas, a leading man and prophet of the Jerusalem church, was sent with Judas Barsabbas to bring the Council's letter to Antioch, and then chosen by Paul as companion on the second missionary journey. Beaten and imprisoned with Paul at Philippi, he sang hymns at midnight before an earthquake opened the prison. As Silvanus he co-sends 1 and 2 Thessalonians, and Peter says he wrote 1 Peter 'through Silvanus'.
people.catholic: At the Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15) the apostles and elders, after Peter and James had spoken, settled the question of circumcision for Gentile converts with a letter beginning 'it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us' (Acts 15:28), the model of later Church councils and of the Magisterium's authority to interpret the faith (CCC 85). Silas links the ministries of Paul and Peter, serving both apostles. He is honored as a saint.
know: Called Silvanus in the letters.
Paul's companion on the second missionary journey (Acts 15:40).
Sang hymns with Paul in the Philippian prison (Acts 16:25).
Like Paul, a Roman citizen (Acts 16:37).
1 Peter was written 'through Silvanus' (1 Pet 5:12).

people.name: Alcimus
people.summary: A priest of Aaron's line who led the Hellenizing party and was made high priest by Demetrius I. He treacherously had sixty pious Hasideans killed, brought Bacchides and Nicanor against Judas, and died of a stroke while tearing down the wall of the inner Temple court.
know: Appointed by Demetrius I (1 Macc 7:9).
Killed sixty Hasideans (1 Macc 7:12-16).
Died struck by palsy (1 Macc 9:54-56).

people.name: Amon
people.summary: Amon son of Manasseh continued his father's idolatry for two years until his servants killed him in his house; the people of the land executed the conspirators and made his son Josiah king.
know: Reigned two years
Assassinated by his servants
Father of Josiah

people.name: Athaliah
people.summary: Athaliah, daughter of Ahab (granddaughter of Omri), married Jehoram of Judah and was queen mother of Ahaziah. When Jehu killed her son, she seized the throne and massacred the royal family, but the infant Joash was hidden by Jehosheba. After six years the priest Jehoiada crowned Joash in the Temple, and Athaliah, crying 'Treason!', was put to death.
people.catholic: Athaliah's attempt to wipe out the seed of David nearly broke God's promise to David; its preservation in one hidden child is a striking instance of God's fidelity to the Davidic covenant, which Catholic readers trace on to Christ. She is the only woman to rule Judah as sovereign.
know: Daughter of Ahab
Wife of Jehoram, mother of Ahaziah
Usurped the throne for six years
Killed at Jehoiada's command

people.name: Hezron
people.summary: Son of Perez and grandson of Judah, who went down to Egypt with Jacob. He heads the genealogy of Ruth 4 that leads to David, and is the ancestor of the Hezronite clan.
people.catholic: Matthew and Luke include him in the genealogy of Jesus, so he is one of the links through which the promise to Judah ('the scepter will not depart from Judah', Gen 49:10) passes to David and to Christ.
know: Son of Perez (Gen 46:12)
Father of Ram, ancestor of David (Ru 4:19)
Listed in Jesus' genealogy (Mt 1:3)
Not Hezron son of Reuben
Son of Perez (Gen 46:12).
Went down to Egypt with Jacob.
Father of Ram (Ruth 4:19).
Named in Mt 1:3 and Lk 3:33.

people.name: Johanan son of Kareah
people.summary: Johanan, a captain of the forces left in Judah, warned Gedaliah of Ishmael's plot, rescued the captives Ishmael had seized, and then led the remnant — with Jeremiah and Baruch — to Egypt, despite God's word through Jeremiah that they should stay in the land.
know: Warned Gedaliah
Led the flight to Egypt
Warned Gedaliah but was not believed (Jer 40:13-16).
Asked Jeremiah to seek God's will, then rejected the answer (Jer 42-43).
Took Jeremiah and Baruch to Tahpanhes in Egypt.

people.name: Joseph, husband of Mary
people.summary: A righteous man of the house of David, Joseph was betrothed to Mary. When she was found with child by the Holy Spirit, an angel told him in a dream to take her as his wife and to name the child Jesus. He brought the family to Bethlehem for the census, fled with them into Egypt from Herod, and settled in Nazareth, where Jesus was known as 'the carpenter's son'.
people.catholic: St Joseph is honoured as the chaste spouse of the Virgin Mary and the legal and foster father of Jesus, through whom Jesus is legally 'son of David' (Mt 1:16, 20); the Church teaches he was not Jesus' natural father (CCC 496-497). Pius IX declared him Patron of the Universal Church in 1870, and Pope Francis opened a Year of St Joseph (2020-2021) with the letter Patris Corde. Because tradition holds that he died with Jesus and Mary beside him, he is invoked as patron of a happy death (CCC 1014), as well as of workers and families. Like Joseph son of Jacob, he is a dreamer who goes down to Egypt to save his family.
know: Called 'a righteous man' (Mt 1:19); no word of his is recorded in Scripture.
Guided by four dreams in Matthew 1-2, three of them through an angel (Mt 1:20; 2:13, 19, 22).
Matthew names his father Jacob (Mt 1:16); Luke's genealogy reads 'son of Heli' (Lk 3:23).
A tekton - carpenter or builder (Mt 13:55).
Feasts March 19 (Solemnity) and May 1 (St Joseph the Worker).
people.feast: March 19 (St Joseph, Spouse of the Blessed Virgin Mary); May 1 (St Joseph the Worker)
