people.name: Nebuzaradan
people.summary: Nebuzaradan, captain of Nebuchadnezzar's guard, burned the Temple, the palace and the houses of Jerusalem, broke down its walls and led the people into exile; by the king's order he freed Jeremiah and let him choose where to live.
know: Burned the Temple in 587/586 BC
Freed Jeremiah
Burned the Temple in 587 BC (Jer 52:12-14).
Released Jeremiah and entrusted him to Gedaliah (Jer 40:1-6).

people.name: Nehemiah
people.summary: Nehemiah son of Hacaliah was cupbearer to Artaxerxes I at Susa. Hearing of Jerusalem's ruin, he prayed and fasted, then obtained the king's leave to return as governor (445 BC), rebuilding the city walls in fifty-two days despite the threats of Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem. He reformed social injustice, restored the Sabbath and, with Ezra, renewed the covenant.
people.catholic: Nehemiah is a model of the layman who unites prayer and action: he prays before every decision (Neh 1:4-11; 2:4) and builds the wall 'with one of his hands' while 'with the other' he holds a weapon (Neh 4:17). Sirach praises him for raising up the fallen walls (Sir 49:13), and 2 Maccabees credits him with recovering the sacred fire and founding a library of the sacred books (2 Macc 1:18-36; 2:13). His rebuilding of the walls has long been read spiritually as the rebuilding of the soul and of the Church.
know: Cupbearer to Artaxerxes I (Neh 1:11).
Rebuilt Jerusalem's walls in 52 days (Neh 6:15).
Opposed by Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem.
Praised in Sirach 49:13 and 2 Maccabees 1-2.

people.name: Perez
people.role: Son of Judah; ancestor of David
people.summary: Twin son of Judah and Tamar who 'broke through' ahead of his brother Zerah at birth; father of Hezron and Hamul. Through him runs the line of David and of Christ.
people.catholic: The elders' blessing on Boaz, 'let your house be like the house of Perez' (Ru 4:12), and the genealogy of Ruth 4:18-22 show Perez as the root of David's family; Matthew and Luke list him among Jesus' ancestors (Mt 1:3; Lk 3:33).
know: Name means 'breach' or 'breaking out' (Gen 38:29)
Twin of Zerah, son of Judah and Tamar
Father of Hezron and Hamul (Gen 46:12)
Ancestor of David and of Jesus

people.name: Philip
people.summary: Philip of Bethsaida was called by Jesus with the words 'Follow me' and at once brought Nathanael, saying 'Come and see'. Jesus tested him before feeding the five thousand; Greeks seeking Jesus came to him; and at the Last Supper he asked, 'Lord, show us the Father'.
people.catholic: Jesus' reply to Philip, 'He who has seen me has seen the Father' (Jn 14:9), is a key text for the unity of the Son with the Father. Tradition holds he preached in Asia Minor and was martyred at Hierapolis. He shares a feast with St James the Less, whose relics with his rest in the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles in Rome. He is distinct from Philip the deacon and evangelist of Acts.
know: From Bethsaida, the town of Andrew and Peter (Jn 1:44).
Brought Nathanael to Jesus (Jn 1:45-46).
'Lord, show us the Father' (Jn 14:8).
Feast May 3, with St James the Less.

people.name: Philip the Evangelist
people.summary: Philip was one of the Seven. Scattered by the persecution after Stephen's death, he preached Christ in Samaria with great signs, baptizing many, including Simon the sorcerer. An angel then sent him to the desert road to Gaza, where he explained Isaiah 53 to an Ethiopian court official and baptized him. He later lived in Caesarea, where he hosted Paul, and had four virgin daughters who prophesied.
people.catholic: Distinct from Philip the Apostle. His mission in Samaria shows the Church's sacramental order: Philip baptized, but Peter and John came and laid hands on the baptized so they would receive the Holy Spirit, a passage the Church reads as a witness to Confirmation (Acts 8:14-17; CCC 1288). His encounter with the Ethiopian, who asks 'how can I understand unless someone guides me?' (Acts 8:31), is a classic text for reading Scripture within the Church and for the link between catechesis and Baptism. The choice of the Seven, on whom the apostles laid hands after prayer (Acts 6:6), is traditionally read as the institution of the diaconate, the first degree of Holy Orders, ordained 'not unto the priesthood but unto the ministry' (CCC 1569-1571).
know: One of the Seven (Acts 6:5); distinct from the apostle Philip.
Evangelized Samaria (Acts 8:5-13).
Baptized the Ethiopian eunuch on the Gaza road (Acts 8:26-40).
Called 'the evangelist'; hosted Paul at Caesarea (Acts 21:8).
Father of four prophesying daughters (Acts 21:9).

people.name: Shimei son of Gera
people.summary: Shimei, a Benjaminite of Saul's clan, cursed and stoned David as he fled Absalom; David stopped Abishai from killing him, saying the LORD may have bidden him. Pardoned on David's return, he was later confined to Jerusalem by Solomon and executed when he broke the terms.
people.catholic: David's meek acceptance of Shimei's curses is read as a figure of Christ who, 'when he was cursed, did not curse back' (1 Pt 2:23).
know: Cursed David at Bahurim
Spared by David
Executed by Solomon for leaving Jerusalem

people.name: Abigail
people.summary: Abigail, the intelligent and beautiful wife of the churlish Nabal of Carmel, rode out with gifts to meet David when he was coming to take revenge on her household, and by her humble, wise words kept him from bloodguilt. After Nabal died, David married her; she was captured at Ziklag and rescued, and bore David's son Chileab (Daniel).
people.catholic: Abigail's intercession - she takes the blame upon herself and turns away the anger of the future king - has led spiritual writers to see in her a figure of Mary the intercessor and a model of peacemaking. Her speech confesses David's 'sure house' before Nathan's oracle (1 Sam 25:28).
know: Wife of Nabal, then of David
Turned David from vengeance
Called 'the Carmelitess'
Mother of Chileab (Daniel)

people.name: Artaxerxes
people.summary: Artaxerxes I (465-424 BC) was the Persian king who first halted the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls after hostile letters, then commissioned the priest-scribe Ezra to teach and enforce the Law, and later sent his cupbearer Nehemiah to rebuild Jerusalem's walls as governor.
people.catholic: Like Cyrus and Darius, Artaxerxes shows God turning the hearts of kings (Prov 21:1) for the good of his people; Nehemiah's silent prayer before answering the king (Neh 2:4) is a classic example of short, trusting prayer in the midst of work.
know: Stopped work on the walls after Rehum's letter (Ezra 4:7-23).
Sent Ezra with a royal decree (Ezra 7:11-26).
Nehemiah was his cupbearer (Neh 1:11; 2:1-8).

people.name: Asahel
people.summary: Asahel son of Zeruiah, 'as light of foot as a wild gazelle', pursued Abner after the battle of Gibeon and was killed by him, which Joab later avenged.
know: Famed for speed
One of David's Thirty

people.name: Ephraim
people.summary: Joseph's younger son by Asenath, named because 'God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction'. Jacob blessed him above his elder brother Manasseh, and his tribe became the leading tribe of the northern kingdom, so that 'Ephraim' later stands for all Israel in the prophets.
people.catholic: Jacob's crossed hands giving the younger the greater blessing echo the Bible's pattern of God's free choice (Abel, Isaac, Jacob, David); Tertullian saw in them a figure of the Cross. Hebrews cites the blessing of Joseph's sons as an act of faith (Heb 11:21).
know: Name means 'fruitful' (Gen 41:52)
Blessed above Manasseh by Jacob (Gen 48:14-20)
Ancestor of Joshua (1 Ch 7:20-27)
Later a name for the northern kingdom

people.name: Gad
people.summary: Gad the prophet advised David during his flight from Saul to go into Judah. After David's sinful census he offered him a choice of three punishments and then told him to build an altar on the threshing floor of Araunah, the future Temple site.
know: David's seer
Brought the choice of punishments after the census
Directed the altar on Araunah's threshing floor
Helped organise the Temple music

people.name: Jeduthun
people.summary: Jeduthun was one of David's three chief Levite musicians with Asaph and Heman, whose sons prophesied with the harp in giving thanks to the LORD.
people.catholic: Psalms 39, 62 and 77 carry his name in their titles.
know: Chief musician under David
Possibly the same as Ethan.
His sons prophesied with harps (1 Chr 25:3).

people.name: Kareah
people.summary: Kareah was the father of the captains Johanan and Jonathan.

people.name: Manoah
people.summary: Danite of Zorah whose barren wife was told by the angel of the LORD that she would bear a son to be a Nazirite from the womb. Manoah prayed for the angel to return, asked his name (it is 'incomprehensible'), and offered a sacrifice; the angel ascended in the altar's flame.
people.catholic: The annunciation of Samson's birth to a barren mother, with a heavenly messenger and a consecrated child, belongs to the pattern the Church sees culminating in the annunciations to Zechariah and to Mary (Lk 1). The angel's answer that his name is 'incomprehensible' (Jdg 13:18; the Hebrew word is related to 'wonderful') is often linked by Christian readers with the messianic title 'Wonderful Counselor' (Isa 9:6).
know: Danite from Zorah (Jdg 13:2).
Prayed for the angel to return (Jdg 13:8).
Saw the angel ascend in the altar flame (Jdg 13:20).
Father of Samson.

people.name: Mary Magdalene
people.summary: Mary of Magdala, from whom Jesus cast out seven demons, followed him from Galilee and supported him from her means. She stood by the cross, saw where he was buried, and came to the tomb early on Easter morning. The risen Jesus appeared first to her, calling her by name, and sent her to tell the disciples, 'I have seen the Lord'.
people.catholic: Because she was sent to announce the Resurrection to the apostles, Christian tradition - St Hippolytus called the myrrh-bearing women 'apostles to the apostles', and St Thomas Aquinas uses the title - honours her as 'Apostle of the Apostles', and in 2016 Pope Francis raised her memorial to a feast. She is honoured among the holy women who were the first witnesses of the Resurrection (CCC 641). Western tradition since St Gregory the Great identified her with the sinful woman of Luke 7 and with Mary of Bethany; the reformed Roman calendar (1969) treats them as distinct.
know: Seven demons were cast out of her (Lk 8:2; Mk 16:9).
Present at the crucifixion, the burial and the empty tomb.
First to see the risen Lord (Jn 20:11-18; Mk 16:9).
Feast July 22.

relations.type: brought news of the empty tomb to

people.name: Onias III
people.summary: The godly high priest at the start of 2 Maccabees under whom Jerusalem lived 'in unbroken peace'. He defended the Temple deposits against Heliodorus and prayed for him, was supplanted by his brother Jason, and was murdered at Daphne near Antioch by Andronicus at Menelaus' instigation. Later Judas saw him in a vision, praying for the whole Jewish people.
people.catholic: 1 and 2 Maccabees are deuterocanonical books, received in the Church's canon (Rome 382, Hippo 393, Carthage 397, Florence, and defined at Trent in 1546) though not in the Hebrew Bible or Protestant Old Testament. The vision of the dead Onias and the prophet Jeremiah interceding for the people (2 Macc 15:12-14) is a key Old Testament witness to the intercession of the righteous departed for those on earth, a basis for the Church's teaching on the communion of saints.
know: High priest under Seleucus IV (2 Macc 3:1-3).
Prayed for the stricken Heliodorus (2 Macc 3:31-33).
Murdered at Daphne (2 Macc 4:33-35).
Seen in vision praying for Israel (2 Macc 15:12).
Josephus calls him son of Simon II; Scripture does not name his father.

relations.type: son of (per Josephus; not in Scripture)

people.name: Achior
people.summary: The leader of the Ammonites in Holofernes' army who warned him that Israel could not be defeated unless it sinned against its God, recounting Israel's history from Abraham onward. Holofernes handed him over to Bethulia to share its fate; after seeing Holofernes' head he believed, was circumcised and joined the house of Israel.
people.catholic: Achior is a remarkable picture of a Gentile who comes to faith through hearing the story of salvation and seeing God's deeds — a foreshadowing of the Church's call to the nations. His conversion is striking since Deut 23:3 had excluded Ammonites from the assembly.
know: Leader of the children of Ammon (Jdt 5:5).
Recited Israel's salvation history to Holofernes (Jdt 5:5-21).
Converted and was circumcised (Jdt 14:10).

people.name: Ahijah the Shilonite
people.summary: Ahijah, a prophet of Shiloh, met Jeroboam outside Jerusalem, tore his new cloak into twelve pieces and gave him ten, announcing that God would give him ten tribes because of Solomon's idolatry. Years later, old and blind, he recognised Jeroboam's disguised wife and foretold the death of her son and the destruction of Jeroboam's house.
know: Tore his cloak into twelve pieces
Foretold the division of the kingdom
Condemned Jeroboam's idolatry
His prophecy is cited as a source for Solomon's history

people.name: Ahimaaz
people.summary: Ahimaaz son of Zadok carried secret news to David during Absalom's revolt and outran the Cushite to bring word of the victory, tactfully withholding the news of Absalom's death.
know: David called him 'a good man' with good news
Hid in a well at Bahurim

people.name: Amoz
people.summary: Amoz is named only as the father of the prophet Isaiah.
know: Not to be confused with the prophet Amos — the names differ in Hebrew.

people.name: Barak
people.summary: Son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali, called by Deborah to lead ten thousand men against Sisera. He would go only if Deborah went with him, and so the honour of killing Sisera went to a woman; he routed Sisera's chariots at the Kishon and sang with Deborah.
people.catholic: Hebrews 11:32 lists Barak among the heroes of faith 'who through faith subdued kingdoms'. His dependence on the prophetic word spoken through Deborah is read as an example of obedience to God's voice in the community.
know: Son of Abinoam of Naphtali (Jdg 4:6).
Insisted Deborah go with him (Jdg 4:8).
Defeated Sisera's chariots (Jdg 4:14-16).
Named among the faithful in Heb 11:32.

people.name: Hamor
people.summary: The Hivite prince of the land at Shechem, from whose sons Jacob bought a field. When his son Shechem violated Dinah, Hamor sought a marriage alliance; the city's men agreed to be circumcised, and Simeon and Levi killed them, Hamor among them.
know: Sold Jacob land near Shechem for a hundred pieces of money (Gen 33:19)
Killed with his son by Simeon and Levi (Gen 34:26)
Joseph's bones were buried in the plot bought from his sons (Jos 24:32)

people.name: Heliodorus
people.summary: Chancellor of Seleucus IV, sent to seize the deposits in the Jerusalem Temple. As he entered the treasury a terrifying horseman and two young men appeared and scourged him; he survived only through the high priest Onias' prayer and returned confessing the power of God.
people.catholic: The scene inspired Raphael's famous Vatican fresco 'The Expulsion of Heliodorus from the Temple', commissioned by Pope Julius II as an image of God defending his Church's patrimony.
know: Sent by King Seleucus (2 Macc 3:7).
Struck down by heavenly riders (2 Macc 3:24-28).
Saved by Onias' sacrifice (2 Macc 3:31-34).

people.name: Heman
people.summary: Heman son of Joel, grandson of the prophet Samuel, of the Korahite clan of Kohath, was one of David's three chief Temple musicians and 'the king's seer'. Psalm 88, the darkest lament of the Psalter, is ascribed to 'Heman the Ezrahite', and 1 Kings names a Heman among the wise men surpassed by Solomon (whether these are the same man is debated).
people.catholic: Psalm 88 ('my soul is full of troubles, my life draws near to Sheol') is prayed at Night Prayer (Compline) on Fridays in the Liturgy of the Hours, the day of the Passion, and has been read as the prayer of Christ in the darkness of death.
know: Grandson of Samuel through Joel
Chief Kohathite singer under David
His fourteen sons served in the music
Grandson of Samuel (1 Chr 6:33).
Fourteen sons and three daughters (1 Chr 25:5).
Psalm 88 bears his name.
Named among the wise in 1 Kgs 4:31.

people.name: Hushai the Archite
people.summary: Hushai the Archite, 'David's friend', met David on the Mount of Olives during Absalom's revolt and went back as a double agent. His advice to Absalom overturned Ahithophel's sound counsel and gave David time to escape.
know: Called 'the king's friend'
Defeated Ahithophel's counsel
Sent intelligence to David through the priests' sons

people.name: Ishbosheth
people.summary: Ishbosheth, a son of Saul, was made king over Israel at Mahanaim by Abner and reigned two years while David ruled Judah at Hebron. After he accused Abner over Saul's concubine Rizpah, Abner defected; Ishbosheth was then murdered in his bed by Rechab and Baanah, whom David executed.
know: Reigned two years over the northern tribes
Called Eshbaal in Chronicles
Murdered by two of his own captains
Possibly the Ishvi of 1 Sam 14:49

people.name: Jehozadak
people.summary: Jehozadak son of Seraiah went into captivity when Nebuchadnezzar took Jerusalem; his son Joshua (Jeshua) became high priest of the returned exiles beside Zerubbabel.
know: Also spelled Jozadak
Father of Joshua the high priest of the restoration
Father of Jeshua the high priest.
Spelled Jehozadak in Haggai/Zechariah and Josedek in Sirach.

people.name: Mephibosheth
people.summary: Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, was lamed at five when his nurse fled with him at news of Gilboa. David, keeping his covenant with Jonathan, restored Saul's land to him and had him eat at the king's table always. During Absalom's revolt his servant Ziba accused him of disloyalty; on David's return he came out unwashed in mourning, and David divided the land between them.
people.catholic: Mephibosheth at the king's table is a favourite image of grace: a lame, powerless heir of a fallen house invited, for another's sake, to eat always with the king - an image of the sinner welcomed to the Eucharistic table for Christ's sake. His story shows David's hesed (covenant kindness).
know: Lame in both feet from childhood
Ate at David's table for Jonathan's sake
Slandered by Ziba
Called Merib-baal in Chronicles
Father of Mica

people.name: Ner
people.summary: Ner son of Abiel was Saul's uncle and the father of Abner, Saul's army commander.
know: Saul's uncle
Father of Abner

people.name: Omri
people.summary: Omri, army commander, was made king after Zimri's coup, overcame Tibni and reigned twelve years. He bought the hill of Samaria and built it as Israel's new capital, founding a powerful dynasty, but did more evil than all before him.
know: Founded Samaria as the capital
Founder of the dynasty of Ahab
Known in Assyrian records ('house of Omri')

people.name: Ozias (Uzziah) of Bethulia
people.summary: Ozias son of Micah, of the tribe of Simeon, chief magistrate of Bethulia. Under the siege he promised to surrender in five days if God did not help, for which Judith rebuked him; afterwards he blessed her 'above all the women upon the earth'.
people.catholic: Ozias' blessing of Judith (Jdt 13:18) anticipates Elizabeth's greeting to Mary (Luke 1:42) and is used in the Church's Marian liturgy.
know: Called Ozias in this translation (Uzziah in others).
Set a five-day limit for God's help (Jdt 7:30-31).
Blessed Judith (Jdt 13:18-20).

people.name: Porcius Festus
people.summary: Porcius Festus succeeded Felix as governor. When he proposed sending Paul to Jerusalem for trial, Paul, a Roman citizen, appealed to Caesar. Festus laid the case before King Agrippa and, hearing Paul speak of the resurrection, exclaimed, 'Paul, you are crazy!'
people.catholic: Paul's appeal before Festus is the providential means by which he reaches Rome, fulfilling the Lord's word that he would bear witness there (Acts 23:11).
know: Successor of Felix (Acts 24:27).
Paul appealed to Caesar before him (Acts 25:11-12).
Consulted King Agrippa about the charges.

people.name: Raphael
people.summary: The angel sent by God to answer the prayers of Tobit and Sarah. Disguised as a kinsman named Azarias son of Ananias, he guided Tobias to Media, taught him to use the fish to drive away Asmodaeus and heal Tobit, and bound the demon. At the end he revealed himself: 'I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels which present the prayers of the saints.'
people.catholic: Raphael ('God heals') is one of only three angels named in the Catholic Bible, with Michael and Gabriel, and is venerated with them on September 29, the feast of the Archangels. Tobit 12 grounds the Church's teaching on angels who present our prayers before God (cf. Rev 8:3-4) and accompany us on the way; the Catechism teaches that 'from its beginning until death human life is surrounded by their watchful care and intercession' (CCC 336). He is patron of travelers, the sick and healers, and of young people seeking a spouse.
know: Name means 'God heals'.
Used the name Azarias son of Ananias (Tob 5:12).
Bound the demon Asmodaeus (Tob 8:3).
'One of the seven holy angels' (Tob 12:15).
Feast: Sept 29 with Michael and Gabriel (October 24 before the 1969 calendar reform).

people.name: Ruth
people.summary: Moabite widow of Mahlon who refused to leave her mother-in-law Naomi: 'Where you go, I will go... your people will be my people, and your God my God.' Gleaning in the fields of Boaz at Bethlehem, she won his kindness, sought him as redeemer at the threshing floor, and became his wife. Their son Obed was the grandfather of King David.
people.catholic: Ruth is one of the four women named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus (Mt 1:5), a Gentile who by faith and loving-kindness (hesed) enters the people of God and becomes an ancestress of the Messiah - a sign of the universal reach of salvation. Her words to Naomi are a classic expression of covenant fidelity and are often used at weddings. Boaz as her kinsman-redeemer has long been read as a figure of Christ, who takes the Gentile Church as his bride.
know: Moabite widow of Mahlon (Ruth 4:10).
'Your people will be my people, and your God my God' (Ruth 1:16).
Gleaned in Boaz's field (Ruth 2).
Married Boaz; mother of Obed (Ruth 4:13).
Great-grandmother of David; named in Mt 1:5.

people.name: Tamar
people.summary: Tamar, David's beautiful daughter and Absalom's full sister, was raped by her half-brother Amnon and then cast out; she lived desolate in Absalom's house, and his revenge set off the tragedies of David's later reign.
people.catholic: Tamar's protest - 'Don't do this folly!' - gives voice to the dignity of the victim, and the narrative honestly exposes the consequences of sin in David's house that Nathan foretold (2 Sam 12:10).
know: Sister of Absalom
Wore a robe of many colours as a king's daughter
Violated by Amnon

people.name: The two elders
people.summary: Two elders appointed as judges in Babylon lusted after Susanna, tried to force her, and when she refused accused her of adultery with a young man. Daniel separated them; one named a mastic tree, the other an evergreen oak, and they were put to death under the law of false witness.
know: A group entry for two unnamed men.
Exposed by separate cross-examination (Dan 13:51-59).
Punished as the law of Moses prescribes for false witnesses (Deut 19:18-19).

people.name: Tobiah the Ammonite
people.summary: An Ammonite official ('servant') allied with Sanballat who ridiculed and threatened the wall builders and kept up a network of Jewish allies through marriage. While Nehemiah was away, the priest Eliashib gave him a room in the Temple; Nehemiah threw his furniture out.
know: Mocked: 'if a fox climbed up it, he would break down their stone wall' (Neh 4:3).
Related by marriage to leading Jerusalem families (Neh 6:17-19).
Expelled from the Temple room (Neh 13:4-9).

people.name: Zerah (son of Judah)
people.summary: Twin son of Judah and Tamar, marked with a scarlet thread on his hand at birth though his brother Perez was born first; ancestor of the Zerahite clan, including Achan.
know: The scarlet thread on his hand (Gen 38:28-30)
Ancestor of Achan (Jos 7:1)
Named in Mt 1:3 with Perez

people.name: Ziba
people.summary: Ziba, a servant of Saul's house, told David of Mephibosheth and managed his land; during Absalom's revolt he brought supplies to David and falsely accused his master, winning half the estate.
know: Had fifteen sons and twenty servants
Accused Mephibosheth of treason

people.name: Abihu
people.summary: Second son of Aaron. He ascended Sinai with Moses, Aaron, Nadab and the seventy elders, but was struck down with Nadab for offering strange fire.
people.catholic: As with Nadab, his fate is read as a warning against irreverent or self-willed worship.
know: Second son of Aaron.
Saw the God of Israel on Sinai (Exo 24:9-10).
Consumed by fire with Nadab (Lev 10:2).
Died without sons (Num 3:4).

people.name: Andrew
people.summary: A fisherman of Bethsaida and first a disciple of John the Baptist, Andrew followed Jesus when John called him the Lamb of God, and at once brought his brother Simon to Jesus. He pointed out the boy with five loaves and two fish at the feeding of the five thousand, and with Philip brought the Greeks who wished to see Jesus.
people.catholic: The Eastern Church calls him Protokletos, 'the First-Called' (Jn 1:40). Tradition holds he preached around the Black Sea and Greece and was crucified at Patras on an X-shaped cross, the 'St Andrew's cross'. He is patron of Scotland, Russia and Greece, and of the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople, so his feast is a sign of Catholic-Orthodox friendship.
know: Brother of Simon Peter; son of John/Jonah.
First a disciple of John the Baptist (Jn 1:35-40).
Brought Peter to Jesus (Jn 1:41-42).
Feast November 30.

relations.type: brother of; brought him to Jesus

people.name: Bathsheba
people.summary: Bathsheba, daughter of Eliam and wife of Uriah the Hittite, was taken by David, who then arranged Uriah's death; their first child died. She bore Solomon and other sons, and with Nathan secured Solomon's succession against Adonijah. As queen mother she sat on a throne at King Solomon's right hand, who rose and bowed to her when she came to intercede.
people.catholic: Bathsheba is the clearest biblical example of the gebirah, the queen mother of the Davidic kingdom: the king rises to meet her, bows, and sets a throne for her at his right hand (1 Kgs 2:19). Catholic theology sees here a type of Mary's queenship: the mother of the Son of David reigns beside her Son and intercedes with him, as Mary is 'exalted by the Lord as Queen over all things' (CCC 966) and Christ's kingdom is the fulfilment of David's. Matthew's genealogy names her discreetly as 'her who had been Uriah's wife' (Mt 1:6), one of the four women before Mary.
know: Wife of Uriah, then of David
Mother of Solomon (and of Shimea, Shobab and Nathan)
Called Bathshua in 1 Chronicles
Sat at the king's right hand as queen mother
Named in Jesus' genealogy

people.name: Eber
people.summary: Son of Shelah and father of Peleg and Joktan. Shem is called 'the father of all the children of Eber', and the name is often linked with the word 'Hebrew'.
know: Shem is 'father of all the children of Eber' (Gen 10:21)
Name traditionally associated with 'Hebrew'
Listed in Luke 3:35

people.name: Enoch
people.summary: Son of Jared in the line of Seth and father of Methuselah. He 'walked with God, and he was not found, for God took him' after 365 years, so that he did not see death.
people.catholic: Hebrews says Enoch was taken up 'so that he wouldn't see death' because he pleased God by faith (Heb 11:5), and Sirach calls him 'an example of repentance to all generations' (Sir 44:16; 49:14). The Catechism cites his 'walk with God' as a model of prayer (CCC 2569). Several Church Fathers expected Enoch, with Elijah, to return before the end as the two witnesses of Revelation 11, though this is not defined teaching. Jude 14-15 quotes a prophecy attributed to him.
know: Walked with God and was taken by God (Gen 5:24)
Lived 365 years on earth
Father of Methuselah
Praised in Heb 11:5 and Sir 44:16; 49:14
Different from Enoch son of Cain

people.name: Gehazi
people.summary: Gehazi, Elisha's servant, suggested the Shunammite's reward and carried the prophet's staff to her son. After Elisha refused Naaman's gifts, Gehazi ran after him, lied to obtain silver and clothing, and was struck with Naaman's leprosy. Later he told the king of Elisha's great deeds.
people.catholic: Gehazi's attempt to profit from a gift of God is often paired with Simon Magus (Acts 8) as the archetype of simony, the sin of trading in spiritual things.
know: Elisha's servant
Took silver from Naaman by deceit
Struck with leprosy
Recounted Elisha's miracles to the king

people.name: Hagar
people.summary: Sarah's Egyptian servant, given to Abraham as a wife so that Sarah might have children through her. Mistreated after she conceived, she fled, and the angel of the LORD met her in the wilderness; she named God 'El Roi', the God who sees. After Isaac's birth she and her son Ishmael were sent away, and God saved them in the wilderness of Beersheba by opening her eyes to a well.
people.catholic: St Paul uses Hagar allegorically for the covenant from Mount Sinai that bears children for slavery, contrasted with Sarah the free woman (Gal 4:21-31). Yet Genesis shows God's tender care for her: she is the first person in Scripture visited by the angel of the LORD and the only one to give God a name, 'the God who sees' (Gen 16:13).
know: Egyptian servant of Sarah (Gen 16:1)
Named God 'El Roi' — 'the God who sees' (Gen 16:13)
Mother of Ishmael
God heard her son's cry in the wilderness (Gen 21:17)
An allegory of the Sinai covenant in Gal 4

people.name: Herod Agrippa II
people.summary: King Agrippa, son of Herod Agrippa I, visited Festus at Caesarea with his sister Bernice and heard Paul's defense. Paul appealed to his knowledge of the prophets; Agrippa replied, 'With a little persuasion are you trying to make me a Christian?', and judged that Paul could have been released had he not appealed to Caesar.
people.catholic: Paul's speech before Agrippa (Acts 26) is his fullest account of his conversion and commission to open the eyes of the Gentiles. Agrippa's half-hearted response is often preached as the danger of being 'almost persuaded'.
know: Called 'King Agrippa' in Acts 25-26.
Heard Paul's defense with Bernice and Festus.
Said Paul could have been freed if he had not appealed to Caesar (Acts 26:32).

people.name: Heth
people.summary: A son of Canaan, ancestor of the 'children of Heth' (Hittites) from whom Abraham bought the cave of Machpelah.
know: The 'children of Heth' sold Abraham a burial place (Gen 23)

people.name: Kish
people.summary: Kish son of Abiel was a wealthy Benjaminite of Gibeah; Saul met Samuel while searching for his father's lost donkeys.
know: Father of King Saul
Paul recalls him in Acts 13:21
1 Chronicles makes Ner his father

people.name: Martha
people.summary: Martha of Bethany, sister of Mary and Lazarus, welcomed Jesus into her home and was 'distracted with much serving' while Mary listened at his feet. When Lazarus died she went out to meet Jesus and professed, 'I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God'; at the supper in Bethany before the Passion she again served.
people.catholic: Martha's confession of faith at Lazarus's tomb (Jn 11:27) parallels Peter's, and Jesus' words to her, 'I am the resurrection and the life', are read at funerals. With Mary she is classically read as the active life beside the contemplative. In 2021 Pope Francis extended her memorial on July 29 to include her sister Mary and brother Lazarus. She is patron of cooks, servers and hospitality.
know: Sister of Mary and Lazarus of Bethany (Jn 11:1).
'Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things' (Lk 10:41).
Confessed Jesus as the Christ, the Son of God (Jn 11:27).
Feast July 29 (Sts Martha, Mary and Lazarus).

relations.type: confessed the Christ, the Son of God

people.name: Miriam
people.summary: Sister of Moses and Aaron, called a prophetess. She led the women in song and dance after the crossing of the Red Sea. When she and Aaron spoke against Moses she was struck with leprosy and shut out of the camp seven days; she died at Kadesh.
people.catholic: Miriam's song at the sea (Exo 15:20-21) is one of the oldest hymns of Scripture, and the Canticle of Moses is sung at Lauds and proclaimed at the Easter Vigil. Christian writers have long noted that Mary, the Mother of Jesus, bears Miriam's name, and have compared Miriam's song of deliverance with Mary's Magnificat. Micah 6:4 counts her with Moses and Aaron among those God sent before Israel.
know: Called 'the prophetess' (Exo 15:20).
Usually identified with the sister who watched over the infant Moses (Exo 2:4-8).
Struck with leprosy after criticizing Moses (Num 12).
Died at Kadesh (Num 20:1).

people.name: Nadab
people.summary: Eldest son of Aaron. With Abihu and the seventy elders he saw the God of Israel on Sinai, but after his ordination he and Abihu offered 'strange fire' before the LORD, and fire came out and consumed them.
people.catholic: The death of Nadab and Abihu is read as a sober lesson that worship must be offered as God commands, not according to human invention - a theme the Church applies to reverence in the liturgy.
know: Aaron's firstborn (Exo 6:23).
Saw God on Sinai with the elders (Exo 24:9-11).
Died offering unauthorized fire (Lev 10:1-2).
Died childless (Num 3:4).

people.name: Shealtiel
people.summary: The son of the exiled King Jeconiah (Jehoiachin) born in Babylon and the father (or legal father) of Zerubbabel. He appears mainly in genealogies and in the formula 'Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel'.
people.catholic: Shealtiel is a link in the genealogy of Jesus in both Matthew and Luke, a sign that God preserved the house of David through the darkness of the Exile, as he had promised (2 Sam 7:16).
know: Son of Jeconiah, born in captivity.
Father of Zerubbabel in Ezra, Haggai, Matthew and Luke.
Listed in both Gospel genealogies of Jesus.

people.name: Titus
people.summary: Titus was a Greek convert and trusted co-worker of Paul. Paul brought him to Jerusalem, where he was not compelled to be circumcised, a test case for the freedom of Gentile believers. He carried out delicate missions to Corinth, organized the collection for Jerusalem, and was left in Crete to 'appoint elders in every city'; the Letter to Titus is addressed to him.
people.catholic: Saints Timothy and Titus are celebrated together on January 26. Tradition holds that Titus was the first bishop of Crete. Paul's charge to him to appoint presbyters in every town (Titus 1:5) is a key witness to the apostolic ordering of ministry and to apostolic succession: those who received authority from the apostles in turn ordained others. The Letter to Titus gives the Church a classic baptismal text, 'the washing of regeneration and renewal by the Holy Spirit' (Titus 3:5), read at the Christmas liturgy with Titus 2:11-14.
know: A Greek, not circumcised (Gal 2:3).
Paul's 'partner and fellow worker' (2 Cor 8:23).
Left in Crete to appoint elders (Titus 1:5).
Feast with Timothy January 26.

people.name: Amasa
people.summary: Amasa, David's nephew, commanded Absalom's rebel army; David forgave him and made him commander in Joab's place, but Joab treacherously stabbed him while greeting him with a kiss.
know: Son of David's sister Abigail
Murdered by Joab

people.name: Amminadab
people.summary: Man of Judah, son of Ram, father of Nahshon the prince of Judah and of Elisheba, wife of Aaron - so that the royal line of Judah and the priestly line of Aaron meet in his household.
people.catholic: Matthew and Luke include him in the genealogy of Jesus, so he is one of the links through which the promise to Judah ('the scepter will not depart from Judah', Gen 49:10) passes to David and to Christ. Through his daughter Elisheba he is also grandfather of Israel's priests.
know: Son of Ram (Ruth 4:19).
Father of Nahshon and of Elisheba, Aaron's wife (Exo 6:23).
In the genealogies of Mt 1:4 and Lk 3:33.

people.name: Amram
people.summary: Son of Kohath and grandson of Levi. He married his aunt Jochebed, and they became the parents of Aaron, Moses and Miriam.
people.catholic: Amram is honoured in Scripture chiefly through his children. Hebrews 11:23 praises the faith of Moses' parents, who hid the child and 'were not afraid of the king's commandment' - an example the Church holds up of parents protecting the life of a child against an unjust decree.
know: Son of Kohath, grandson of Levi.
Married Jochebed, his father's sister (Exo 6:20).
Father of Aaron, Moses and Miriam.
Lived 137 years.

people.name: Asher
people.summary: Jacob's second son by Zilpah; Leah named him 'happy'. Jacob said his bread would be rich and he would yield royal dainties.
people.catholic: The prophetess Anna, who greeted the infant Jesus in the Temple, was of the tribe of Asher (Lk 2:36).
know: Son of Jacob and Zilpah (Gen 30:12-13)
Father of Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah and Serah (Gen 46:17)
Anna the prophetess was of his tribe (Lk 2:36)

people.name: Haggai
people.summary: Haggai prophesied in 520 BC, the second year of Darius I, to the returned exiles in Jerusalem. He rebuked them for living in panelled houses while God's house lay in ruins, stirred up the governor Zerubbabel and the high priest Joshua to rebuild the Temple, and promised that the glory of the new house would surpass the old.
people.catholic: Haggai's promise that God would 'shake all nations' and fill the Temple with glory (Hag 2:6-9) was read in the Christian tradition as pointing to Christ's coming into the Temple (cf. Mal 3:1; Lk 2:22-32); the Vulgate's 'the desired of all nations will come' (Hag 2:7) made this verse a classic Advent text. Hebrews 12:26-28 applies his 'once more I will shake the heavens and the earth' to the unshakable Kingdom.
know: Four dated oracles, all in 520 BC (Hag 1:1; 2:1; 2:10; 2:20).
Rebuilding of the Temple resumed at his preaching (Ezra 5:1-2; 6:14).
Called Zerubbabel God's 'signet ring' (Hag 2:23).

people.name: Hannah
people.summary: Hannah, the beloved but childless wife of Elkanah, poured out her soul in silent prayer at the sanctuary of Shiloh and vowed that a son would be given to the LORD. Eli first mistook her for drunk, then blessed her. She bore Samuel, weaned him, and brought him to Eli to serve at Shiloh, singing a song of praise that celebrates God who lifts up the lowly.
people.catholic: Hannah's Song (1 Sam 2:1-10) is the clearest Old Testament model of Mary's Magnificat (Lk 1:46-55): both rejoice in God who humbles the proud, exalts the lowly and fills the hungry, and the Church prays Hannah's canticle in the Liturgy of the Hours. The Catechism names Hannah among the holy women whose mission prepared for Mary's (CCC 489) and says the young Samuel learned from her how to stand before the LORD (CCC 2578). Her persevering, wordless prayer is a classic example of prayer from the heart, and her offering of her child foreshadows the Presentation of Jesus in the Temple.
know: Prayed so fervently at Shiloh that Eli thought she was drunk
Dedicated Samuel to the LORD as a Nazirite-like servant
Her Song (1 Sam 2:1-10) parallels Mary's Magnificat
Later bore three more sons and two daughters

people.name: Japheth
people.summary: A son of Noah who, with Shem, covered their father's nakedness. Noah prayed, 'May God enlarge Japheth; let him dwell in the tents of Shem.' His sons are listed as ancestors of the 'islands of the nations'.
people.catholic: Many Fathers read 'let him dwell in the tents of Shem' as foreshadowing the Gentiles' entry into the inheritance of Israel through the Church.
know: Son of Noah (Gen 5:32)
Blessed: 'May God enlarge Japheth' (Gen 9:27)
Father of Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras (Gen 10:2)

people.name: Jason the high priest
people.summary: Brother of Onias III, Jason bought the high priesthood from Antiochus IV, built a gymnasium in Jerusalem and led the people into the Greek way of life. Outbid by Menelaus, he fled to Ammon; his later violent attempt to retake Jerusalem failed, and he died a fugitive among the Spartans with no one to mourn him.
know: Originally named Joshua/Jesus according to Josephus.
Bought the high priesthood (2 Macc 4:7-10).
Built a gymnasium under the citadel (2 Macc 4:12).
Died in exile at Sparta (2 Macc 5:8-10).

people.name: Jehoahaz of Israel
people.summary: Jehoahaz son of Jehu reigned seventeen years, during which Hazael and Ben-hadad of Syria crushed Israel's army; he sought the LORD, who gave Israel a deliverer.
know: Israel reduced to 50 horsemen and 10 chariots

people.name: Jethro
people.summary: Priest of Midian and father-in-law of Moses, also called Reuel. He sheltered Moses for forty years, gave him his daughter Zipporah, and later came to Sinai, praised the LORD for the deliverance from Egypt, offered sacrifice, and advised Moses to appoint judges to share the burden of governing the people.
people.catholic: Jethro is a Gentile who blesses the God of Israel and offers sacrifice (Exo 18:10-12), and so is read as a figure of the nations coming to faith. His counsel that Moses delegate authority to capable men (Exo 18:13-26) has been cited by Church writers as a model of shared, ordered governance.
know: Also called Reuel (Exo 2:18; compare 3:1).
Father of Zipporah and of Hobab.
Confessed 'Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods' (Exo 18:11).
Advised Moses to appoint judges over thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens.

people.name: Lazarus of Bethany
people.role: Friend of Jesus, raised from the dead
people.summary: Lazarus of Bethany, brother of Martha and Mary, was a friend whom Jesus loved. When he fell ill and died, Jesus came after four days, wept, and called him from the tomb: 'Lazarus, come out!' Many believed, and the chief priests plotted to kill both Jesus and Lazarus.
people.catholic: The raising of Lazarus, the greatest of Jesus' signs in John, reveals him as 'the resurrection and the life' and anticipates his own Resurrection, though Lazarus returned to an ordinary, mortal life (CCC 646). It is the Gospel of the Fifth Sunday of Lent in Year A, used for the third scrutiny of those preparing for Baptism. Eastern tradition holds he later became bishop of Kition in Cyprus. Since 2021 he is honoured with his sisters on July 29.
know: Brother of Martha and Mary (Jn 11:1-2).
'Jesus wept' at his tomb (Jn 11:35).
Raised after four days in the tomb (Jn 11:39-44).
Feast July 29 (Sts Martha, Mary and Lazarus).

people.name: Mary of Bethany
people.summary: Mary, sister of Martha and Lazarus, sat at Jesus' feet listening to his word, and Jesus said she had 'chosen the good part'. When Lazarus died she fell at Jesus' feet weeping. Six days before the Passover she anointed Jesus' feet with costly nard and wiped them with her hair, an act Jesus linked to his burial.
people.catholic: Mary is the model of contemplative listening to the Word. John identifies her with the woman who anointed Jesus at Bethany (Jn 11:2; 12:3; compare Mt 26:6-13; Mk 14:3-9), of whom Jesus said that what she did would be told wherever the Gospel is preached. Western tradition long identified her with Mary Magdalene; since 2021 she is celebrated with Martha and Lazarus on July 29.
know: Sister of Martha and Lazarus (Jn 11:1).
'Mary has chosen the good part' (Lk 10:42).
Anointed Jesus' feet with nard (Jn 12:3).
Feast July 29 (Sts Martha, Mary and Lazarus).

people.name: Mattathias
people.summary: A priest of the line of Joarib living at Modin, Mattathias refused the king's order to sacrifice to idols, killed the apostate Jew and the royal officer at the altar, and fled to the hills with his five sons crying, 'Whoever is zealous for the law... let him follow me!' He began the Maccabean revolt and, dying, charged his sons to remember the faith of their fathers.
people.catholic: 1 and 2 Maccabees are deuterocanonical books, received in the Church's canon (Rome 382, Hippo 393, Carthage 397, Florence, and defined at Trent in 1546) though not in the Hebrew Bible or Protestant Old Testament. Mattathias is presented as a new Phinehas, zealous for the covenant (1 Macc 2:26, 54). His deathbed speech (1 Macc 2:49-68) recalls the faithful from Abraham to Daniel, a 'cloud of witnesses' like Hebrews 11. The Church honors his fidelity to God's law under persecution, though it reads the Maccabean use of arms in light of the Gospel's fuller revelation.
know: Son of John, son of Simeon, of the priests of Joarib (1 Macc 2:1).
Killed an apostate and the king's officer at Modin (1 Macc 2:23-25).
Allowed fighting on the Sabbath for self-defense (1 Macc 2:39-41).
Died in the 146th year (166 BC) (1 Macc 2:70).

people.name: Melchizedek
people.role: King of Salem; priest of God Most High
people.summary: The king of Salem and 'priest of God Most High' who met Abram after his victory over the four kings, brought out bread and wine, and blessed him; Abram gave him a tenth of everything. Psalm 110 speaks of a priest forever 'after the order of Melchizedek'.
people.catholic: Hebrews presents Christ as high priest 'after the order of Melchizedek', a priesthood greater than Levi's (Heb 5-7; Ps 110:4). The Catechism teaches that Christian tradition sees Melchizedek as a prefiguration of Christ's priesthood (CCC 1544) and his offering of bread and wine as a prefiguring of the Church's own offering in the Eucharist (CCC 1333); it also lists him among the figures of Christ outside Israel (CCC 58). The Roman Canon asks God to accept the Eucharistic sacrifice as he accepted 'the offering of your high priest Melchizedek, a holy sacrifice, a spotless victim'. Psalm 110:4 is traditionally sung at priestly ordinations.
know: King of Salem (traditionally Jerusalem) and priest of God Most High (Gen 14:18)
Brought out bread and wine and blessed Abram
Abram gave him a tithe of everything (Gen 14:20)
Christ is priest 'after the order of Melchizedek' (Ps 110:4; Heb 7)
Named in the Roman Canon

people.name: Naaman
people.summary: Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Syria, was a mighty man but a leper. A captive Israelite girl told his wife about the prophet in Samaria; Elisha sent word to wash seven times in the Jordan. After angry resistance he obeyed, and his flesh became like a little child's. He confessed that there is no God in all the earth but in Israel, and took two mule-loads of earth to worship the LORD at home.
people.catholic: Naaman's cleansing in the Jordan is a classic Old Testament figure of Baptism, read in the Fathers (Ambrose, 'On the Mysteries') and in the liturgy: the humble washing restores him like a newborn child. Jesus cites him as a Gentile healed when many in Israel were not (Lk 4:27, read on the Monday of the 3rd week of Lent), and his story is paired with the healed Samaritan leper (28th Sunday, Year C). His conversion shows God's salvation offered to all nations.
know: Commander of the Syrian army
Learned of Elisha from a captive Israelite girl
Washed seven times in the Jordan
Confessed the God of Israel
Cited by Jesus in Luke 4:27

people.name: Nahshon
people.summary: Son of Amminadab and prince of the tribe of Judah in the wilderness. He helped Moses take the census, led the camp of Judah at the head of Israel's march, and was the first leader to present his tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar. He was brother-in-law of Aaron and grandfather of Boaz.
people.catholic: Matthew and Luke include him in the genealogy of Jesus, so he is one of the links through which the promise to Judah ('the scepter will not depart from Judah', Gen 49:10) passes to David and to Christ. Jewish tradition (not Scripture) remembers him as the first to step into the Red Sea.
know: Son of Amminadab, prince of Judah (Num 1:7; 2:3).
First to bring his offering for the altar (Num 7:12).
Brother of Elisheba, Aaron's wife (Exo 6:23).
Father of Salmon (Ruth 4:20).

people.name: Pekah
people.summary: Pekah son of Remaliah killed Pekahiah and reigned in Samaria. Allied with Rezin of Damascus he attacked Ahaz of Judah - the crisis of Isaiah's Immanuel prophecy - but Tiglath-pileser took Galilee and much of Israel, and Hoshea assassinated him.
people.catholic: Isaiah dismisses Rezin and 'the son of Remaliah' as 'two tails of smoking firebrands' (Isa 7:4), the setting of the Immanuel sign.
know: Called 'the son of Remaliah' by Isaiah
Attacked Judah with Rezin
Lost Galilee to Assyria

people.name: Ptolemy VI Philometor
people.summary: King of Egypt defeated by Antiochus IV, who later gave his daughter Cleopatra to Alexander Balas, then took her back, gave her to Demetrius II, crowned himself king of Asia at Antioch and died three days after defeating Alexander.
know: Defeated by Antiochus IV (1 Macc 1:16-19).
Wore the crowns of Egypt and Asia (1 Macc 11:13).
Died in 145 BC (1 Macc 11:18).

people.name: Sarah (wife of Tobias)
people.summary: The only daughter of Raguel and Edna at Ecbatana. Seven husbands had died on their wedding night, killed by the demon Asmodaeus, and, mocked by her father's maid, she prayed for death or relief on the same day Tobit prayed. God sent Raphael, and she was married to her kinsman Tobias, who drove the demon away.
people.catholic: Sarah's prayer in her distress (Tob 3:11-15) and her 'Amen' to Tobias' wedding prayer (Tob 8:8) make her a model of faith in suffering and of a marriage founded on prayer. Her deliverance shows that God hears the prayers of the afflicted at the same moment, weaving separate lives into one providential plan (Tob 3:16-17).
know: Only daughter of Raguel and Edna (Tob 3:10).
Seven husbands died on the wedding night (Tob 3:8).
Her prayer and Tobit's were heard together (Tob 3:16).
Married Tobias (Tob 7:13).

people.name: Thomas (Didymus)
people.summary: Thomas, called Didymus ('Twin'), urged the disciples to go with Jesus to Judea 'that we may die with him', and asked at the Last Supper how they could know the way. Absent when the risen Jesus first appeared, he refused to believe without touching the wounds; a week later Jesus invited him to do so, and he confessed, 'My Lord and my God!'
people.catholic: Thomas's confession is one of the clearest New Testament professions of Christ's divinity (CCC 448), and Jesus' reply - 'Blessed are those who have not seen, and have believed' - is addressed to every later believer. Tradition holds he evangelized India, where the 'St Thomas Christians' trace their origin to him, and was martyred near Chennai.
know: Called Didymus, 'the Twin' (Jn 11:16).
Asked 'How can we know the way?' - 'I am the way, the truth, and the life' (Jn 14:5-6).
Confessed 'My Lord and my God!' (Jn 20:28).
Feast July 3.

people.name: Zebedee
people.role: Fisherman; father of James and John
people.summary: Zebedee was a Galilean fisherman with hired servants, mending nets in the boat with his sons James and John when Jesus called them; they left him and followed Jesus.
know: Father of the apostles James and John (Mt 4:21).
Ran a fishing business with hired men (Mk 1:20).
His wife is generally identified with Salome (compare Mt 27:56 with Mk 15:40).

people.name: Ahimelech
people.summary: Ahimelech son of Ahitub, priest at Nob, gave the fleeing David the holy showbread and Goliath's sword. Doeg the Edomite reported it, and Saul had Ahimelech and eighty-five priests of Nob slaughtered; only his son Abiathar escaped to David.
people.catholic: Jesus cites this episode (Mt 12:3-4; Mk 2:25-26) to show that mercy and human need come before ritual law and that he, Son of David, is Lord of the Sabbath. Mark's account names the high priest of that time as Abiathar, Ahimelech's son. The holy bread given to David is often read by the Fathers as a figure of the Eucharistic bread.
know: Gave David the consecrated bread (showbread)
Gave him Goliath's sword
Murdered with the priests of Nob on Saul's order
Father of Abiathar

people.name: Apollos
people.summary: Apollos, a Jew of Alexandria, was eloquent and mighty in the Scriptures and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John. Priscilla and Aquila explained the way of God more accurately to him, and he went on to Corinth, where he powerfully refuted the Jews from the Scriptures. Some Corinthians formed a faction around him, but Paul insists, 'I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase.'
people.catholic: Apollos shows the need for the apostolic faith to be received whole, and Paul's treatment of the Corinthian factions ('I follow Paul... I follow Apollos', 1 Cor 1:12) is a classic plea for unity in the one Body of Christ.
know: An eloquent Alexandrian Jew (Acts 18:24).
Instructed by Priscilla and Aquila.
Watered what Paul planted at Corinth (1 Cor 3:6).
Sent on with Zenas (Titus 3:13).

people.name: Arpachshad
people.summary: A son of Shem, born two years after the Flood, and father of Shelah in the line leading to Abraham.
know: Born two years after the Flood (Gen 11:10)
Called 'Arphaxad' in Luke 3:36
Luke inserts a 'Cainan' between him and Shelah, following the Greek Septuagint

people.name: Barabbas
people.summary: Barabbas was a notorious prisoner, held for insurrection and murder, whom Pilate offered to release at the Passover alongside Jesus. Stirred up by the chief priests, the crowd chose Barabbas and demanded that Jesus be crucified.
people.catholic: The Fathers noted that his name means 'son of the father': the guilty 'son of the father' goes free while the innocent Son of the Father dies in his place, an image of Christ's substitutionary sacrifice for sinners.
know: A 'notable prisoner' (Mt 27:16).
Imprisoned for insurrection and murder (Mk 15:7; Lk 23:19).
Released by Pilate at the crowd's demand (Mk 15:15).

people.name: Bartholomew (Nathanael)
people.summary: Bartholomew appears in every list of the Twelve, usually beside Philip. Catholic tradition identifies him with Nathanael of Cana, whom Philip brought to Jesus: Jesus called him 'an Israelite indeed, in whom is no deceit', and he confessed, 'Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are King of Israel!'
people.catholic: The name Bartholomew is a patronymic ('son of Tolmai'), which is why he can also bear the personal name Nathanael; the identification is traditional rather than certain. Jesus' promise to him of 'angels ascending and descending on the Son of Man' (Jn 1:51) presents Christ as Jacob's ladder. Tradition holds he preached in India and Armenia and was flayed alive.
know: Paired with Philip in the lists of the Twelve (Mt 10:3).
Traditionally identified with Nathanael of Cana (Jn 1:45-51; 21:2).
Confessed Jesus as Son of God and King of Israel (Jn 1:49).
Feast August 24.

people.name: Belshazzar
people.summary: Belshazzar held a great feast using the gold and silver vessels taken from the Jerusalem Temple. A hand wrote MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN on the wall; Daniel interpreted it as God's judgment, and that night Belshazzar was killed and the kingdom passed to Darius the Mede.
people.catholic: His profanation of the Temple vessels is a classic warning against sacrilege and pride; 'weighed in the balances and found wanting' (Dan 5:27) has become proverbial.
know: Daniel 5 calls Nebuchadnezzar his 'father' (i.e., predecessor/ancestor); historically he was the son of Nabonidus.
Profaned the Temple vessels at his feast (Dan 5:2-4).
Slain the night of the writing on the wall (Dan 5:30).
Called 'Baltasar' in Baruch 1:11-12.

people.name: Bilhah
people.role: Servant of Rachel; concubine of Jacob
people.summary: Rachel's servant, given to her by Laban, whom Rachel gave to Jacob as a wife; she bore Dan and Naphtali. Reuben later lay with her, an act that cost him his birthright.
know: Mother of Dan and Naphtali (Gen 30:3-8)
Reuben's sin with her cost him the firstborn's rights (Gen 35:22; 49:4)

people.name: Ephron the Hittite
people.summary: Son of Zohar, a Hittite of Hebron who sold Abraham the field and cave of Machpelah for four hundred shekels of silver as a burial place for Sarah.
know: Sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah for 400 shekels (Gen 23:16)
Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, Leah and Jacob were buried there (Gen 49:29-32)

people.name: Gorgias
people.summary: A general sent by Lysias to destroy Judah who tried to surprise Judas' camp by night at Emmaus and was outmaneuvered; later governor of Idumea, he fought Judas again.
people.catholic: It was after the battle with Gorgias that the bodies of fallen Jews were found wearing idol amulets, leading Judas to offer prayer and sacrifice for the dead (2 Macc 12:32-45).
know: Defeated at Emmaus (1 Macc 4:1-25).
Governor of Idumea (2 Macc 12:32).

people.name: Ham
people.summary: A son of Noah who saw his father's nakedness and told his brothers; in response Noah cursed Ham's son Canaan. His sons Cush, Mizraim, Put and Canaan are the ancestors of peoples of Africa and Canaan in the Table of Nations.
people.catholic: The curse in Gen 9:25 falls on Canaan, not on Ham, and says nothing about race; its modern misuse to justify enslaving Africans is a grave distortion. The Church teaches that all people share 'the same nature and the same origin' and equal dignity (CCC 1934-1935).
know: Son of Noah, father of Canaan (Gen 9:18)
Dishonoured his drunken father (Gen 9:22)
Noah's curse falls on Canaan, not Ham (Gen 9:25)
Father of Cush, Mizraim, Put and Canaan (Gen 10:6)

people.name: Herod the Great
people.summary: Herod, an Idumean made king of Judea by Rome, ruled from 37 to 4 BC and rebuilt the Jerusalem Temple on a grand scale. Troubled by the Magi's news of a newborn King of the Jews, he ordered the killing of the boys of Bethlehem; Joseph fled with Jesus and Mary into Egypt until Herod died.
people.catholic: The Holy Innocents he massacred are honoured as martyrs on December 28, having died in place of Christ. His hostility to the newborn King recalls Pharaoh's slaughter of Hebrew infants and casts Jesus as the new Moses (Mt 2:15-18). The Temple he expanded is the one Jesus knew (Jn 2:20).
know: King of Judea when Jesus and John the Baptist were born (Mt 2:1; Lk 1:5).
Ordered the massacre of the Innocents (Mt 2:16).
Father of Archelaus, Antipas and Philip; grandfather of Herodias and Herod Agrippa I (Josephus).

people.name: Issachar
people.summary: Fifth son of Jacob and Leah, born after Leah hired Jacob's night with Rachel's mandrakes; his name is linked with 'hire' or 'reward'. Jacob called him a strong donkey couching between the sheepfolds.
know: Son of Jacob and Leah (Gen 30:14-18)
Father of Tola, Puvah, Iob and Shimron (Gen 46:13)

people.name: Neriah
people.summary: Neriah son of Mahseiah was the father of Baruch the scribe and of Seraiah the quartermaster.
know: Called 'Nerias' in the Book of Baruch.

people.name: Obed-Edom
people.summary: Obed-Edom the Gittite sheltered the Ark in his house for three months after Uzzah's death, and the LORD blessed his whole household; hearing this, David brought the Ark up to Jerusalem with joy.
people.catholic: Luke's Visitation narrative closely parallels 2 Samuel 6: as the Ark stayed three months in the house of Obed-Edom bringing blessing, Mary - the new Ark carrying the Word made flesh - stays about three months in Zechariah's house (Lk 1:56). The Catechism calls Mary 'the ark of the covenant, the place where the glory of the Lord dwells' (CCC 2676).
know: Kept the Ark three months
His house was blessed because of the Ark
Parallels Mary's three-month stay with Elizabeth

relations.type: type of (three months with the Ark)

people.name: Queen of Sheba
people.summary: The Queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame and came to Jerusalem with camels bearing spices, gold and precious stones to test him with hard questions. Overwhelmed by his wisdom and the order of his house and worship, she blessed the LORD and exchanged rich gifts with the king.
people.catholic: Jesus says 'the Queen of the South' will rise at the judgement to condemn his generation, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon, 'and behold, something greater than Solomon is here' (Mt 12:42). The Fathers saw in her the Gentile Church coming to Christ, and her gifts of gold and spices are linked with Psalm 72 and Isaiah 60 and the Magi's gifts at the Epiphany.
know: Came to test Solomon with riddles
Brought gold, spices and precious stones
Blessed the God of Israel
Called 'Queen of the South' by Jesus

people.name: Sanballat the Horonite
people.summary: The chief opponent of Nehemiah's rebuilding: he mocked the Jews, plotted an armed attack and tried to lure Nehemiah into a trap and to discredit him through hired prophets. One of the high priest's grandsons married his daughter.
know: Mocked the 'feeble Jews' (Neh 4:2).
Tried to lure Nehemiah to the plain of Ono (Neh 6:2).
Became father-in-law to a grandson of Eliashib (Neh 13:28).

people.name: Seth
people.summary: The third son of Adam and Eve, born after Abel's death; Eve said God had given him 'instead of Abel'. Adam fathered him 'in his own likeness, after his image' at 130 years. He was the father of Enosh and lived 912 years; the line leading to Noah, Abraham and David runs through him.
people.catholic: Seth's line carries the promise after the tragedy of Cain and Abel, and Luke traces Jesus' genealogy back through Seth to Adam (Lk 3:38). St Augustine's City of God follows the 'city of God' through Seth's descendants, in contrast with Cain's line. Sirach 49:16 honours him with Shem.
know: Given 'instead of Abel' (Gen 4:25)
Born in Adam's likeness and image (Gen 5:3)
Father of Enosh; lived 912 years
Ancestor of Noah and of Jesus (Lk 3:38)

people.name: Shechem (son of Hamor)
people.summary: Son of Hamor who took and violated Dinah, then loved her and asked to marry her. He and the men of his city accepted circumcision, but Simeon and Levi attacked while they were in pain and killed them all.
know: Violated Dinah, then sought to marry her (Gen 34:2-4)
Killed by Simeon and Levi (Gen 34:26)
Bears the same name as the city of Shechem

people.name: Susanna
people.summary: Susanna, the beautiful and God-fearing wife of Joakim in Babylon, was propositioned by two lustful elders while bathing in her garden. She refused, choosing death over sin, and they falsely accused her of adultery; as she was led to execution God stirred up the young Daniel, who questioned the elders separately and exposed their lie.
people.catholic: Susanna is honoured as a model of chastity, trust in God and courage under false accusation; her prayer 'O everlasting God, you know the secrets' (Dan 13:42) is a classic of innocent suffering. The Church reads her story (Dan 13) on Monday of the Fifth Week of Lent, pairing it with Jesus and the woman caught in adultery, and early Christians painted her in the catacombs as a figure of the soul saved by God. Her story is part of the Catholic (Greek) text of Daniel.
know: Daughter of Helkias and wife of Joakim (Dan 13:1-2).
Said: 'It is better for me to fall into your hands than to sin' (Dan 13:23).
Saved when Daniel asked each elder under which tree he saw her (mastic vs. evergreen oak).

people.name: Terah
people.summary: Son of Nahor and father of Abram, Nahor and Haran. He left Ur of the Chaldees with Abram, Sarai and Lot, intending to go to Canaan, but settled in Haran, where he died at 205.
people.catholic: Joshua recalls that Terah and his fathers 'served other gods' beyond the River (Jos 24:2), which highlights the gratuitous character of God's call to Abraham. He appears in Luke's genealogy of Jesus (Lk 3:34).
know: Father of Abram, Nahor and Haran (Gen 11:26)
Left Ur of the Chaldees and settled in Haran (Gen 11:31)
Served other gods (Jos 24:2)
Died in Haran aged 205

people.name: Abel
people.summary: The second son of Adam and Eve, a keeper of sheep. He offered God the firstborn of his flock and their fat portions, and God looked with favour on his offering. His jealous brother Cain killed him, and his blood cried out to God from the ground.
people.catholic: Jesus calls him 'righteous Abel' (Mt 23:35), and Hebrews praises his faith-filled sacrifice and says Christ's blood 'speaks better than that of Abel' (Heb 11:4; 12:24). In the Roman Canon (Eucharistic Prayer I) the Church asks God to accept the Eucharistic offering as he accepted 'the gifts of your servant Abel the just', together with Abraham's sacrifice and Melchizedek's offering. He is seen as a type of Christ the innocent shepherd slain by his brother, and as the first martyr. The Catechism points to his offering of the firstborn of his flock as an early form of prayer (CCC 2569) and to his murder as revealing the evil of homicide (CCC 2259).
know: A shepherd who offered the firstborn of his flock (Gen 4:2-4)
Killed by his brother Cain (Gen 4:8)
Called 'righteous' by Jesus (Mt 23:35)
Named in the Roman Canon of the Mass
Hebrews 11:4 lists him first among the heroes of faith

people.name: Abiram
people.summary: Reubenite, son of Eliab and brother of Dathan, who joined Korah's revolt against Moses and Aaron and was swallowed by the earth with his household.
people.catholic: Like Dathan, he stands in Scripture as a warning against contempt for God-given authority (Ps 106:17).
know: Son of Eliab, brother of Dathan.
Joined Korah's rebellion (Num 16).
Swallowed by the earth (Ps 106:17).

people.name: Beor
people.summary: Father of the diviner Balaam.
know: Father of Balaam (Num 22:5).

people.name: Bethuel
people.summary: Youngest son of Nahor and Milcah, an Aramean of Paddan Aram, father of Rebekah and Laban. He consented with Laban to Rebekah's marriage to Isaac: 'The thing proceeds from the LORD.'
know: Father of Rebekah and Laban (Gen 22:23; 24:29)
Called 'the Syrian (Aramean) of Paddan Aram' (Gen 25:20)
Jacob was sent to his house to find a wife (Gen 28:2)

people.name: Caiaphas
people.summary: Joseph Caiaphas, son-in-law of Annas, was high priest (c. AD 18-36). He counselled the Sanhedrin that it was better for one man to die for the people than for the whole nation to perish, presided over Jesus' night trial, tore his robes at Jesus' claim to be the Christ, and sent him to Pilate. He later interrogated Peter and John.
people.catholic: John notes that Caiaphas unwittingly prophesied that Jesus would die 'for the nation, and not for the nation only, but ... to gather together into one the children of God who are scattered abroad' (Jn 11:51-52; CCC 596). An ossuary inscribed 'Joseph son of Caiaphas', found in Jerusalem in 1990, is widely thought to be his family's.
know: High priest 'that year' (Jn 11:49).
Son-in-law of Annas (Jn 18:13).
Presided at Jesus' trial before the council (Mt 26:57-66).
Questioned Peter and John (Acts 4:6).

people.name: Canaan
people.summary: The youngest son of Ham, cursed by Noah after Ham's disrespect. He is the eponymous ancestor of the Canaanite peoples, beginning with Sidon his firstborn and Heth.
people.catholic: The curse on Canaan explains in story form Israel's later relation to the Canaanites; it has nothing to do with race (see CCC 1934).
know: Cursed by Noah: 'a servant of servants' (Gen 9:25)
Ancestor of the Canaanites, Hittites, Jebusites, Amorites and others (Gen 10:15-18)

people.name: Cornelius
people.summary: Cornelius was a centurion of the Italian Regiment at Caesarea, a devout God-fearer who gave alms and prayed. An angel told him to send for Peter; while Peter preached in his house, the Holy Spirit fell on all who heard, and Peter commanded that these Gentiles be baptized.
people.catholic: Cornelius is the first Gentile convert, whose household received the Spirit before Baptism and was then baptized at Peter's command. The Church sees here Peter, as head of the apostles, opening the door of the Church to the nations, a decision Peter later invokes at the Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15:7-11). His prayers and alms 'went up for a memorial before God' (Acts 10:4).
know: A centurion of the Italian Regiment stationed at Caesarea.
A God-fearer who prayed and gave alms.
First Gentile convert received by Peter; the Spirit fell on his household (Acts 10:44).
Peter retold the event to defend it (Acts 11:1-18).

people.name: Dathan
people.summary: Reubenite, son of Eliab, who with his brother Abiram joined Korah's rebellion. Refusing Moses' summons, they accused him of bringing them out of a land flowing with milk and honey to die in the wilderness; the earth opened and swallowed them with their households.
people.catholic: Dathan and Abiram are remembered in the Psalms and Sirach as an example of rebellion against God's chosen leaders and of the judgement that follows (Ps 106:16-18; Sir 45:18).
know: Son of Eliab, of Reuben (Num 16:1).
Refused to come up at Moses' call (Num 16:12-14).
Swallowed by the earth (Num 16:31-33; Deut 11:6).

people.name: Deborah
people.summary: Prophetess, wife of Lappidoth, who judged Israel under the palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel. She summoned Barak to fight Sisera, went with him into battle, and foretold that the LORD would deliver Sisera into the hand of a woman. With Barak she sang the victory song of Judges 5, and the land had rest forty years.
people.catholic: Deborah, 'a mother in Israel' (Jdg 5:7), is honoured as one of the great women of the Old Testament - a prophetess who speaks God's word and calls others to courageous action. Christian tradition has seen in the valiant women of Israel, such as Deborah, Jael and Judith, foreshadowings of Mary, whose fiat and victory over the enemy are celebrated in the Church's liturgy.
know: Prophetess and judge (Jdg 4:4-5).
Judged under 'the palm tree of Deborah'.
Commanded Barak to fight Sisera (Jdg 4:6-7).
'A mother in Israel' (Jdg 5:7).
Sang the Song of Deborah (Jdg 5).

people.name: Eliakim son of Hilkiah
people.summary: Eliakim son of Hilkiah, 'over the household' of King Hezekiah, led the delegation that met the Rabshakeh outside Jerusalem's wall and carried the Assyrian threats to Hezekiah and Isaiah. Isaiah prophesied that he would replace Shebna and receive 'the key of the house of David'.
people.catholic: Isaiah's oracle - 'I will lay the key of David's house on his shoulder; he will open and no one will shut' (Isa 22:22) - lies behind Jesus' gift of the keys of the kingdom to Peter (Mt 16:19) and is applied to Christ himself in Revelation 3:7. Catholic interpreters see in Eliakim's office of royal steward, with father-like authority over the household, a type of the Petrine office (Isa 22:20-24 is read with Mt 16:13-20 on the 21st Sunday, Year A).
know: Royal steward ('over the household') under Hezekiah
Negotiated with the Rabshakeh
Received 'the key of the house of David' in Isaiah's oracle
Replaced Shebna as master of the palace (Isa 22:15-23).
Received 'the key of David's house' — opens and none shall shut.
Negotiated with the Rabshakeh in Hebrew/Aramaic (Isa 36).
Also in 2 Kings 18-19.

people.name: Eliashib the high priest
people.summary: High priest in Nehemiah's day who, with his fellow priests, rebuilt the Sheep Gate of Jerusalem. Later, while Nehemiah was away, he gave Tobiah the Ammonite a room in the Temple courts, which Nehemiah angrily cleared out.
know: Rebuilt the Sheep Gate (Neh 3:1).
Allied with Tobiah and housed him in the Temple (Neh 13:4-7).
A grandson married Sanballat's daughter (Neh 13:28).

people.name: Gaal
people.summary: Son of Ebed, who won the trust of Shechem and boasted against Abimelech; Zebul warned Abimelech, who defeated Gaal and drove him out of the city.
know: Son of Ebed (Jdg 9:26).
Incited Shechem against Abimelech (Jdg 9:28-29).
Defeated and expelled (Jdg 9:39-41).

people.name: Gilead (father of Jephthah)
people.summary: Gileadite father of Jephthah by a prostitute; his legitimate sons later drove Jephthah out of the family inheritance.
know: Father of Jephthah (Jdg 11:1).
His other sons expelled Jephthah (Jdg 11:2).

people.name: Izhar
people.summary: Son of Kohath and brother of Amram; father of Korah, who led the rebellion against Moses and Aaron.
know: Son of Kohath (Exo 6:18).
Father of Korah, Nepheg and Zichri (Exo 6:21).

people.name: Jehonadab son of Rechab
people.summary: Jehonadab son of Rechab joined Jehu in his chariot to witness his 'zeal for the LORD' against Baal. Generations later his descendants, the Rechabites, still kept his command to drink no wine and live in tents, and Jeremiah held up their fidelity as a rebuke to Judah.
people.catholic: The Rechabites' fidelity to their ancestor's rule (Jer 35) has been seen by spiritual writers as an Old Testament anticipation of religious rules of life; the Carmelites, who claim Elijah as their father, have also appealed to them.
know: Rode with Jehu
Ancestor of the Rechabites
His descendants' obedience is praised in Jeremiah 35

people.name: Jonadab son of Rechab
people.summary: Jonadab (Jehonadab) son of Rechab rode with Jehu against the worship of Baal and commanded his descendants to drink no wine, build no houses and sow no fields but live in tents. Centuries later Jeremiah tested the Rechabites with wine; their fidelity to their ancestor's command became a rebuke to unfaithful Judah, and God promised Jonadab would never lack a man to stand before him.
people.catholic: The Rechabites' obedience is held up as a model of fidelity to a received rule of life, and is sometimes cited in the tradition of religious life and of temperance.
know: Ally of Jehu against Baal worship (2 Kings 10:15-23).
His descendants kept his rule for some 250 years (Jer 35).
God promised: 'Jonadab will not lack a man to stand before me forever' (Jer 35:19).

people.name: Jude Thaddeus
people.summary: The apostle is called 'Judas the son of James' in Luke and Acts and 'Thaddaeus' (Matthew also 'Lebbaeus') in Matthew and Mark. At the Last Supper 'Judas (not Iscariot)' asked why Jesus would reveal himself to the disciples and not to the world, and Jesus answered that he and the Father would make their home with whoever loves him.
people.catholic: Catholic tradition often identifies him with Jude, 'brother of James', author of the Letter of Jude, reading Luke's Greek 'Judas of James' as 'brother of James' (as the Douay-Rheims does). Tradition holds he preached with Simon the Zealot in Persia, where both were martyred, so they share a feast. He is widely invoked as patron of desperate and lost causes.
know: Called Thaddaeus (Mk 3:18) and 'Judas the son of James' (Lk 6:16).
'Judas (not Iscariot)' of John 14:22.
Patron of hopeless causes.
Feast October 28, with St Simon.

people.name: Maacah
people.summary: Maacah, granddaughter of Absalom (called 'daughter of Abishalom'), was Rehoboam's favourite wife and the mother of Abijah. She remained queen mother into the reign of Asa, who deposed her for making an abominable image for Asherah.
people.catholic: Maacah shows the real power of the gebirah (queen mother) in Judah - a power Asa could remove when it was used for idolatry. Her story is the negative counterpart to Bathsheba's role as intercessor.
know: Rehoboam's favourite wife
Mother of Abijah
Removed as queen mother by Asa for idolatry
Called Micaiah daughter of Uriel in 2 Chr 13:2

people.name: Nahor (father of Terah)
people.summary: Son of Serug and father of Terah; grandfather of Abraham.
know: Not the same as Abraham's brother Nahor
Listed in Luke 3:34

people.name: Naphtali
people.summary: Jacob's second son by Bilhah, named by Rachel from her 'wrestlings' with her sister. Jacob calls him 'a doe set free'.
people.catholic: Isaiah promises that the land of Zebulun and Naphtali, once humbled, will see a great light; Matthew sees this fulfilled when Jesus begins preaching in Capernaum (Isa 9:1-2; Mt 4:13-16).
know: Son of Jacob and Bilhah (Gen 30:7-8)
Father of Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer and Shillem (Gen 46:24)
His territory in Galilee saw the start of Jesus' preaching (Mt 4:13-16)

people.name: Pharaoh of the Oppression
people.summary: The 'new king who did not know Joseph', who enslaved the Israelites, ordered the midwives to kill Hebrew boys, and then commanded that every newborn son be thrown into the Nile. Moses fled from him to Midian; he died while Israel still groaned in slavery.
people.catholic: The Fathers set this Pharaoh's slaughter of the Hebrew infants beside Herod's massacre of the Innocents (Mt 2:16), seeing in Moses' rescue a figure of the Christ Child's escape.
know: 'A new king arose over Egypt, who didn't know Joseph' (Exo 1:8).
Ordered Hebrew baby boys killed (Exo 1:16, 22).
Sought to kill Moses (Exo 2:15).
His death is noted in Exo 2:23; Scripture does not name him.

people.name: Ram
people.summary: Son of Hezron of the tribe of Judah and father of Amminadab, known only from the genealogies leading to David and to Jesus. Luke calls him Aram.
people.catholic: Matthew and Luke include him in the genealogy of Jesus, so he is one of the links through which the promise to Judah ('the scepter will not depart from Judah', Gen 49:10) passes to David and to Christ.
know: Son of Hezron, father of Amminadab (Ru 4:19)
Called 'Aram' in Luke 3:33
Grandfather of Nahshon, prince of Judah
Son of Hezron (Ruth 4:19).
Father of Amminadab.
Called Aram in Lk 3:33.

people.name: Rezin
people.summary: Rezin king of Damascus allied with Pekah of Israel to attack Ahaz of Judah, the crisis behind Isaiah's Immanuel prophecy. Ahaz called in Tiglath-pileser, who took Damascus and killed Rezin.
know: Last king of Aram-Damascus
Killed by Tiglath-pileser

people.name: Uzziel
people.summary: Son of Kohath and uncle of Aaron; his sons Mishael and Elzaphan carried the bodies of Nadab and Abihu out of the camp.
know: Son of Kohath, uncle of Moses and Aaron (Lev 10:4).
Father of Mishael, Elzaphan and Sithri.

people.name: Zalmunna
people.summary: One of the two kings of Midian pursued by Gideon across the Jordan. Captured at Karkor, they admitted killing Gideon's brothers at Tabor, and Gideon killed them himself.
know: King of Midian (Jdg 8:5).
Killed Gideon's brothers at Tabor (Jdg 8:18-19).
Slain by Gideon (Jdg 8:21).

people.name: Zebah
people.summary: One of the two kings of Midian pursued by Gideon across the Jordan. Captured at Karkor, they admitted killing Gideon's brothers at Tabor, and Gideon killed them himself.
know: King of Midian (Jdg 8:5).
Killed Gideon's brothers at Tabor (Jdg 8:18-19).
Slain by Gideon (Jdg 8:21).

people.name: Zechariah (Zacharias)
people.role: Priest; father of John the Baptist
people.summary: Zechariah was a priest of the division of Abijah. While he offered incense in the Temple, the angel Gabriel announced that his barren wife Elizabeth would bear a son to be named John; because he doubted, he was struck mute. When he wrote 'His name is John', his speech returned and he prophesied the Benedictus.
people.catholic: Zechariah's canticle, the Benedictus (Lk 1:68-79), is prayed every day at Morning Prayer in the Liturgy of the Hours, blessing God for the dawn of salvation and for John's mission as prophet of the Most High. His muteness and restored speech are often contrasted with Mary's faith-filled question at the Annunciation. He and Elizabeth are commemorated together as saints.
know: Priest of the division of Abijah (Lk 1:5).
Struck mute for doubting Gabriel (Lk 1:20).
Wrote 'His name is John' (Lk 1:63).
Spoke the Benedictus (Lk 1:68-79).
people.feast: September 23 (Sts Zechariah and Elizabeth, Roman Martyrology)

people.name: Zelophehad
people.summary: Son of Hepher of the tribe of Manasseh, who died in the wilderness without sons. His five daughters asked for his inheritance, leading to the law that daughters inherit when there is no son.
know: Died in the wilderness, not in Korah's rebellion (Num 27:3).
Had five daughters and no sons.
