His case set Israel's inheritance law (Num 27:8-11).

people.name: Ahitub
people.summary: Ahitub son of Amariah, of the line of Eleazar son of Aaron, was the father of Zadok the priest.
know: Zadok's descent from Eleazar is traced through him

people.name: Amos
people.summary: Amos, a herdsman and dresser of sycamore figs from Tekoa in Judah, was sent to prophesy in the northern kingdom under Jeroboam II (8th century BC). He denounced oppression of the poor, corrupt worship and complacent luxury, saw visions of locusts, fire, a plumb line and summer fruit, and was expelled from Bethel by the priest Amaziah. The book ends with the promise to raise up David's fallen tent.
people.catholic: Amos is the great prophetic voice of social justice: 'let justice roll on like rivers' (Amos 5:24) informs the Church's social teaching on worship that is inseparable from care for the poor. At the Council of Jerusalem St James quoted Amos 9:11-12 to show that the Gentiles' entry into the Church fulfils God's plan to rebuild David's tent (Acts 15:16-17). Tobit recalls Amos' prophecy that feasts would be turned to mourning (Tob 2:6).
know: 'I was no prophet, nor a prophet's son, but a herdsman' (Amos 7:14).
Expelled from Bethel by Amaziah the priest.
Five visions: locusts, fire, plumb line, summer fruit, the Lord by the altar.
Promise of David's restored tent quoted in Acts 15.

people.name: Anak
people.summary: Ancestor of the Anakim, the giant clan of Hebron whose size terrified the ten spies.
know: Son of Arba (Jos 15:13).
The spies felt 'like grasshoppers' beside his descendants (Num 13:33).
Father of Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai.

people.name: Anna (wife of Tobit)
people.summary: Tobit's wife, of his own kindred, who supported the household by weaving when he was blind. Her sharp reply when Tobit doubted her honesty, and her daily vigil watching the road for her son, make her one of the most human figures in the book.
people.catholic: Anna's anxious love for Tobias and her joy at his return (Tob 11:9) show the Old Testament's tender portrait of motherhood; Tobit charges his son to honor her all her days (Tob 4:3-4).
know: Worked as a weaver to support the family (Tob 2:11-12).
Watched the road daily for Tobias (Tob 10:7).
Buried with Tobit by their son (Tob 14:12).

people.name: Azariah son of Hilkiah
people.summary: Azariah son of Hilkiah is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

people.name: Bezalel
people.summary: Son of Uri, of the tribe of Judah, whom God called by name and filled with the Spirit of God in wisdom and skill. He led the work of making the tabernacle, the ark of the covenant, the mercy seat, the lampstand and the priestly vessels.
people.catholic: Bezalel is the first person in Scripture said to be 'filled with the Spirit of God' (Exo 31:3), and his gift is artistic: the Church sees in him a patron-figure for sacred art and architecture placed at the service of worship. The ark he made, overshadowed by the cherubim, is in Catholic tradition a type of Mary, the Ark of the New Covenant.
know: Called by name and filled with God's Spirit (Exo 31:1-5).
Made the ark of the covenant (Exo 37:1-9).
Worked with Oholiab and other skilled workers.
His bronze altar still stood at Gibeon in Solomon's day (2 Chr 1:5).

people.name: Caleb (Chelubai)
people.summary: Caleb (Chelubai) son of Hezron, brother of Jerahmeel and Ram, heads a large clan list of Judah; Jewish and Christian interpreters traditionally distinguish him from Caleb son of Jephunneh (1 Chr 2:9, 18-24, 42-50).

people.name: Dan
people.summary: Jacob's son by Rachel's servant Bilhah; Rachel named him saying 'God has judged me'. Jacob's blessing calls him a judge of his people and a serpent by the way.
people.catholic: Jacob interrupts his blessing of Dan with the prayer 'I have waited for your salvation, LORD' (Gen 49:18). Dan is the one tribe missing from the list of the sealed in Rev 7:5-8, which some Fathers connected with Gen 49:17; this is speculation, not Church teaching.
know: Son of Jacob and Bilhah; name means 'he judged' (Gen 30:6)
Father of Hushim (Gen 46:23)
'Dan will judge his people' (Gen 49:16)

people.name: Darius the Mede
people.summary: Darius the Mede received Belshazzar's kingdom and set Daniel over his governors. Tricked by jealous officials into signing an irrevocable decree against prayer to anyone but the king, he reluctantly had Daniel thrown to the lions, rejoiced at his deliverance, and decreed reverence for Daniel's God.
know: Called 'son of Ahasuerus, of the offspring of the Medes' (Dan 9:1).
His historical identity is debated.
Distinct from Darius I of Persia in Haggai, Zechariah and Ezra.

relations.type: threw to the lions and then honoured

people.name: Dinah
people.summary: Daughter of Jacob and Leah. When she went out to visit the women of the land, Shechem son of Hamor took and violated her and then sought to marry her; her brothers Simeon and Levi deceived the Shechemites and killed them.
know: Only daughter of Jacob named in Genesis (Gen 30:21)
Violated by Shechem (Gen 34:2)
Avenged by Simeon and Levi (Gen 34:25-26)

people.name: Ehud
people.summary: Left-handed Benjamite, son of Gera, raised up by the LORD when Israel had served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years. Bringing tribute, he gained a private audience, killed the obese king with a hidden double-edged sword, escaped, and led Israel to victory; the land had rest eighty years.
people.catholic: Ehud's 'secret message from God' (Jdg 3:20) has been read allegorically by the Fathers of the two-edged word of God (Heb 4:12) that pierces to the heart. More broadly he shows God choosing the unlikely - a left-handed man of the smallest tribe - to save his people.
know: Left-handed Benjamite (Jdg 3:15).
Killed Eglon of Moab with a hidden sword (Jdg 3:21-22).
Rallied Israel at the fords of the Jordan.
Eighty years of rest followed (Jdg 3:30).

people.name: Eliphaz (son of Esau)
people.summary: Firstborn son of Esau by Adah; father of Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam and Kenaz, and of Amalek by his concubine Timna.
know: Father of Amalek (Gen 36:12)
Not the same as Eliphaz the Temanite, Job's friend, though that name echoes his son Teman

people.name: Elizabeth
people.summary: Elizabeth, of the priestly line of Aaron and wife of the priest Zechariah, was righteous but barren and advanced in years. She conceived John in her old age, and when her relative Mary visited, the child leapt in her womb and, filled with the Holy Spirit, she greeted Mary as 'the mother of my Lord'. At John's circumcision she insisted he be named John.
people.catholic: Elizabeth's inspired words 'Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb' form part of the Hail Mary (CCC 2676), and her greeting of Mary as 'the mother of my Lord' is cited by the Church for Mary's divine motherhood (CCC 495). The Visitation (May 31) celebrates her meeting with Mary. Her late, miraculous motherhood echoes Sarah and Hannah and shows that 'nothing is impossible with God' (Lk 1:37).
know: A descendant of Aaron (Lk 1:5).
Relative of the Virgin Mary (Lk 1:36).
First to call Mary 'the mother of my Lord' (Lk 1:43).
Her words are part of the Hail Mary.
people.feast: September 23 (Sts Zechariah and Elizabeth, Roman Martyrology)

relations.type: descendant of ('of the daughters of Aaron')

people.name: Elkanah
people.summary: Elkanah son of Jeroham, a man of Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim, went up yearly to worship at Shiloh. He had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah, and loved the childless Hannah tenderly. After Samuel's birth he let Hannah fulfil her vow and give the boy to the LORD's service.
people.catholic: Elkanah is remembered for his gentle love toward his barren wife ('Am I not better to you than ten sons?') and for his faithful yearly pilgrimage, the setting in which Hannah's prayer was heard. The Chronicler lists him among the Levites, so Samuel's priestly ministry has a family background.
know: Lived at Ramah (Ramathaim-zophim) in Ephraim
Husband of Hannah and Peninnah
Father of Samuel and of three more sons and two daughters by Hannah
1 Chronicles 6 counts him among the Kohathite Levites

people.name: Enosh
people.summary: Son of Seth and father of Kenan. In his days 'men began to call on the LORD's name'. He lived 905 years.
people.catholic: The Catechism notes the invocation of the divine name in the time of Enosh as part of the earliest history of prayer (CCC 2569). Luke lists him (as 'Enos') among Jesus' ancestors.
know: In his time people began to call on the LORD's name (Gen 4:26)
Spelled 'Enos' in Luke 3:38
Lived 905 years

people.name: Felix
people.summary: Antonius Felix was the Roman governor to whom the tribune Lysias sent Paul under guard. He heard Paul's case against the high priest Ananias and Tertullus but postponed judgment; when Paul spoke of righteousness, self-control and the judgment to come, Felix was terrified, yet he kept Paul in custody for two years hoping for a bribe.
people.catholic: Felix is a figure of the soul that hears the truth, trembles, and still delays conversion ('when it is a convenient season, I will summon you', Acts 24:25).
know: Governor of Judea at Caesarea.
Husband of Drusilla.
Kept Paul in prison two years hoping for money (Acts 24:26-27).
Succeeded by Porcius Festus.

people.name: Gabael
people.summary: The kinsman at Rages in Media with whom Tobit left ten talents of silver; Raphael retrieved the money from him and brought him to Tobias' wedding.
know: Called 'brother of Gabrias' (Tob 1:14) and 'son of Gabrias' (Tob 4:20).
Came to the wedding feast and blessed Tobias (Tob 9:5-6).

people.name: Gad
people.summary: Jacob's son by Leah's servant Zilpah; Leah named him saying 'How fortunate!' Jacob foretold that raiders would raid him but he would raid at their heels.
know: Son of Jacob and Zilpah (Gen 30:9-11)
Father of seven sons (Gen 46:16)
Not the prophet Gad of David's time

people.name: Gilead
people.summary: Son of Machir and grandson of Manasseh, ancestor of the Gileadite clans including Hepher.
know: Son of Machir (Num 26:29).
Father of Hepher (Num 26:32).

people.name: Hananiah son of Azzur
people.summary: Hananiah, a prophet from Gibeon, publicly contradicted Jeremiah in the Temple, prophesying that Babylon's yoke would be broken within two years, and broke the wooden yoke from Jeremiah's neck. Jeremiah answered that God would put an iron yoke on the nations and that Hananiah would die that year; he died two months later.
know: The classic example of a false prophet who tells people what they want to hear (Jer 28).
Broke Jeremiah's wooden yoke; God replaced it with an iron one.
Died in the seventh month of that year, as Jeremiah foretold.

people.name: Hanun
people.summary: Hanun son of Nahash humiliated David's envoys of condolence, shaving half their beards, which provoked the Ammonite war in which Uriah later died.
know: Provoked war with David

people.name: Hoshea
people.summary: Hoshea son of Elah killed Pekah and became the last king of Israel. A vassal of Shalmaneser of Assyria, he conspired with Egypt and withheld tribute; Shalmaneser imprisoned him and besieged Samaria for three years, and in 722 BC Samaria fell and Israel was deported to Assyria.
people.catholic: 2 Kings 17 explains the fall of Samaria as the fruit of centuries of idolatry and rejection of the prophets - a sober theological meditation the Church reads as a call to fidelity.
know: Last king of the northern kingdom
Rebelled against Assyria
Samaria fell in his ninth year (722 BC)

people.name: James, son of Alphaeus
people.summary: James son of Alphaeus is the ninth name in the lists of the Twelve (Mt 10:3; Mk 3:18; Lk 6:15; Acts 1:13); nothing else is said of him under that name.
people.catholic: Catholic tradition generally identifies him with 'James the less' (Mk 15:40) and with James 'the brother of the Lord' who led the Jerusalem church, and honours him as St James the Less together with St Philip. The identification is traditional rather than certain.
know: Son of Alphaeus (Mt 10:3).
Traditionally 'St James the Less'.
Catholic tradition generally identifies him with James the brother of the Lord.
Feast May 3, with St Philip.

people.name: Joash the Abiezrite
people.summary: Man of Ophrah of the clan of Abiezer in Manasseh, father of Gideon. When the townsmen demanded Gideon's death for destroying Baal's altar, Joash replied, 'If he is a god, let him contend for himself.'
know: Father of Gideon (Jdg 6:11).
Owned the altar of Baal Gideon tore down.
Defended his son (Jdg 6:31).

people.name: Kenan
people.summary: Son of Enosh and father of Mahalalel; he lived 910 years.
know: Called 'Cainan' in Luke 3:37
Lived 910 years

people.name: Mark
people.summary: John, called Mark, was the son of Mary, in whose Jerusalem house the church gathered. He went with his cousin Barnabas and with Saul on the first missionary journey but turned back at Perga, causing a sharp disagreement that separated Paul and Barnabas. Later reconciled with Paul, he is with him in prison as a fellow worker and is called 'useful to me for service'; Peter calls him 'Mark, my son'.
people.catholic: The Church honors St Mark as the author of the second Gospel; his feast is April 25 and his symbol is the lion. Early tradition (Papias, via Eusebius) holds that he wrote down Peter's preaching as Peter's interpreter, so that his Gospel transmits the apostolic witness of the head of the apostles. Tradition also holds that he founded the Church of Alexandria and died a martyr there; his relics were brought to Venice, whose patron he is. His restoration to Paul's favor after failure is a picture of reconciliation in the Church.
know: Also called John (Acts 12:12, 13:5, 13:13).
Son of Mary of Jerusalem and cousin of Barnabas (Col 4:10).
Left the first missionary journey at Perga (Acts 13:13; 15:38).
Peter calls him 'my son' (1 Pet 5:13).
Traditionally the evangelist of the second Gospel; feast April 25.

people.name: Mary of Clopas
people.summary: Mary 'the wife of Clopas' stood by the cross with the Virgin Mary and Mary Magdalene (Jn 19:25). The Synoptic Gospels name among the women at the cross and tomb 'Mary the mother of James and Joses' (Mt 27:56; Mk 15:40), also called 'the other Mary' (Mt 27:61; 28:1); Catholic tradition generally identifies these as one woman.
people.catholic: The Catechism points to her to explain the 'brothers of Jesus': 'James and Joses, brothers of Jesus, are the sons of another Mary, a disciple of Christ, whom St Matthew significantly calls the other Mary' (CCC 500). Some readers take John 19:25 to call her the sister (kinswoman) of the Virgin Mary. She is honoured among the holy women who followed Jesus from Galilee and were first at the empty tomb.
know: Wife of Clopas (Jn 19:25).
'Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses' (Mk 15:40) - identification with Mary of Clopas is traditional.
Called 'the other Mary' in Matthew (Mt 28:1).
Brought spices to anoint Jesus' body (Mk 16:1).

relations.type: stood at the cross with ('his mother's sister' in some readings)
companion at the cross and tomb

people.name: Matthew (Levi)
people.summary: Matthew, also called Levi son of Alphaeus, was a tax collector at Capernaum. At Jesus' word 'Follow me' he left his tax booth and hosted a banquet for Jesus with tax collectors and sinners, where Jesus said he came to call not the righteous but sinners.
people.catholic: The Church honours him as Apostle and Evangelist, by tradition author of the First Gospel, written to show Jesus as the fulfilment of Israel's Scriptures; his symbol is the man (or angel). His call, painted by Caravaggio, is a classic image of grace meeting a sinner. Tradition holds he died a martyr.
know: Called 'Levi the son of Alphaeus' in Mark 2:14.
A tax collector (Mt 9:9; 10:3).
Traditionally author of the Gospel of Matthew.
Feast September 21.

relations.type: called from the tax office by

people.name: Menahem
people.summary: Menahem son of Gadi killed Shallum, savagely put down resistance at Tiphsah, and reigned ten years, paying Pul (Tiglath-pileser) of Assyria a thousand talents of silver raised from Israel's wealthy men.
know: Paid tribute to Assyria

people.name: Mushi
people.summary: Son of Merari and grandson of Levi, listed in the Levitical genealogies; head of a Levite clan.
know: Grandson of Levi through Merari.
Named in the genealogy of Exodus 6 and the census of Numbers 3.

people.name: Necoh
people.summary: Pharaoh Necoh (Neco) marched north to aid Assyria; Josiah went out against him at Megiddo and was killed. Necoh then deposed Jehoahaz, made Jehoiakim king and laid tribute on Judah, until Nebuchadnezzar defeated him at Carchemish.
know: Killed Josiah at Megiddo
Deposed Jehoahaz and installed Jehoiakim
Defeated at Carchemish (605 BC)

people.name: Obed
people.summary: Son of Boaz and Ruth, born in Bethlehem and nursed by Naomi; the neighbour women named him. He was the father of Jesse and grandfather of King David.
people.catholic: Matthew and Luke include him in the genealogy of Jesus, so he is one of the links through which the promise to Judah ('the scepter will not depart from Judah', Gen 49:10) passes to David and to Christ.
know: Son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:13).
Named by the women of Bethlehem (Ruth 4:17).
Father of Jesse, grandfather of David (Ruth 4:17, 22).

people.name: Peleg
people.summary: Son of Eber, so named because 'in his days the earth was divided'; father of Reu.
know: Name means 'division' (Gen 10:25)
Listed in Luke 3:35

people.name: Rahab
people.summary: Canaanite woman of Jericho, called a prostitute, who hid Joshua's two spies, confessed that 'the LORD your God, he is God in heaven above and on earth beneath', and let them down by a rope from her house on the wall. A scarlet cord in her window marked her household, which was spared when Jericho fell; she lived among Israel and, according to Matthew, married Salmon and became the mother of Boaz.
people.catholic: Rahab is one of the four women named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus (Mt 1:5), a sign that the Messiah came for Gentiles and sinners. Hebrews 11:31 praises her faith and James 2:25 her works, so she is a classic witness that faith and works go together. St. Clement of Rome (1 Clement 12) saw in the scarlet cord a sign of redemption through the blood of the Lord, and the Fathers read her house, the only place of safety in the doomed city, as a figure of the Church.
know: Hid the spies and confessed faith in the LORD (Jos 2:9-11).
Scarlet cord in her window (Jos 2:18-21).
Spared with her family at Jericho (Jos 6:22-25).
Mother of Boaz by Salmon (Mt 1:5).
Praised in Heb 11:31 and Jas 2:25.

people.name: Sheba son of Bichri
people.summary: Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjaminite, raised a revolt of the northern tribes after Absalom's defeat; a wise woman of Abel Beth Maacah persuaded her city to throw his head over the wall to Joab.
know: Cried 'We have no portion in David'
Killed by the people of Abel

people.name: Shelah (son of Arpachshad)
people.summary: Son of Arpachshad and father of Eber.
know: Not the same as Shelah son of Judah
Listed among Jesus' ancestors (Lk 3:35)

people.name: Shelah (son of Judah)
people.summary: Judah's third son by Shua's daughter, whom Judah withheld from Tamar for fear he too would die; ancestor of the Shelanite clan.
know: Born at Chezib (Gen 38:5)
Withheld from Tamar (Gen 38:11, 14, 26)
Ancestor of the Shelanites (Num 26:20; 1 Ch 4:21)

people.name: Uzzah
people.summary: Uzzah, son of Abinadab, drove the new cart carrying the Ark toward Jerusalem; when the oxen stumbled he put out his hand to steady the Ark and was struck dead.
people.catholic: Uzzah's death is a classic lesson in reverence for the holy: the Ark was to be carried on poles by Levites, not handled. It sets up David's fear - 'How can the Ark of the LORD come to me?' - which Elizabeth echoes before Mary (Lk 1:43).
know: Touched the Ark and died
David named the place Perez-uzzah
Called Uzza in Chronicles

people.name: Zimri
people.summary: Zimri, commander of half the chariots, killed Elah and reigned seven days at Tirzah; when the army made Omri king and besieged the city, Zimri burned the palace over himself.
know: Reigned seven days
Died in the burning palace
'Zimri, murderer of his master' became a taunt (2 Kgs 9:31)

people.name: Achan
people.summary: Judahite, son of Carmi, who at the fall of Jericho secretly took a mantle, silver and a wedge of gold that had been devoted to the LORD. Israel was then defeated at Ai; Achan was identified by lot, confessed, and was stoned with his household in the Valley of Achor.
people.catholic: Achan's hidden sin bringing defeat on all Israel is a scriptural image of the communal dimension of sin, which the Catechism describes: every sin harms the communion of the Church. His confession before Joshua ('give glory to the LORD... and make confession') is often cited in teaching on the confession of sins.
know: Took devoted spoil from Jericho (Jos 7:1, 21).
His sin caused the defeat at Ai.
Identified by lot; confessed (Jos 7:16-21).
Stoned in the Valley of Achor (Jos 7:24-26).
Called Achar, 'the troubler of Israel' (1 Chr 2:7).

people.name: Ahaziah of Israel
people.summary: Ahaziah son of Ahab reigned two years. After falling through a lattice he sent to inquire of Baal-zebub, god of Ekron; Elijah intercepted the messengers, called down fire on two companies of soldiers, and foretold the king's death. He died without a son.
know: Consulted Baal-zebub of Ekron
Elijah announced his death
Succeeded by his brother Joram

people.name: Anah
people.summary: A Horite, son of Zibeon, who found the hot springs in the wilderness while feeding his father's donkeys; father of Dishon and Esau's wife Oholibamah.
know: Found hot springs in the wilderness (Gen 36:24)
Gen 36:20 also lists an Anah among the sons of Seir

people.name: Barzillai the Gileadite
people.summary: Barzillai, a very old and wealthy Gileadite of Rogelim, provided food for David at Mahanaim during Absalom's revolt. He declined David's invitation to live at court because of his age, sending his son Chimham instead.
know: Eighty years old
Fed David's people in the wilderness
David commended his sons to Solomon

people.name: Bela (son of Benjamin)
people.summary: A son of Benjamin who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)
Benjamin's firstborn (1 Ch 8:1)

people.name: Edna
people.summary: Raguel's wife and Sarah's mother, who prepared the bridal chamber and comforted her daughter, and blessed Tobias as her own son.
know: Mother of Sarah.
Called Tobias 'dear brother' and entrusted Sarah to him (Tob 10:12).

people.name: Elihu son of Barachel
people.summary: A young Buzite who, angry at Job for justifying himself and at the friends for having no answer, delivered four speeches stressing that God teaches through suffering and is beyond human judgment. He is neither answered by Job nor rebuked by God.
people.catholic: Elihu's insight that suffering can be a discipline that instructs and saves (Job 33:14-30; 36:15) prepares for the Christian understanding of the medicinal and purifying value of trials.
know: Son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram (Job 32:2).
Speaks in Job 32-37.

people.name: Goliath
people.summary: Goliath of Gath, a giant Philistine champion, defied the armies of Israel for forty days until the shepherd boy David, trusting in the LORD, felled him with a stone from his sling and cut off his head with the giant's own sword.
people.catholic: The Fathers read David's victory over Goliath as a figure of Christ's victory over Satan: the humble shepherd from Bethlehem defeats the proud enemy with the weakest means, 'that all the earth may know there is a God in Israel'. Augustine and Caesarius of Arles preached on this typology.
know: About six cubits and a span tall
Defied Israel for forty days
Killed by David's sling stone
His sword was later kept at Nob

people.name: Habakkuk
people.summary: Habakkuk prophesied as Babylon rose to power (late 7th century BC), boldly asking God why he tolerates injustice and why he would use the ruthless Chaldeans. God answers that the vision will come in its time and that 'the righteous will live by his faith'; the book ends with a psalm of trust. In the Greek story of Bel and the Dragon, an angel carries 'the prophet Habakkuk' to Babylon to bring food to Daniel in the lions' den.
people.catholic: Hab 2:4, 'the righteous will live by his faith', is quoted three times in the New Testament (Rom 1:17; Gal 3:11; Heb 10:38) and is central to the Church's teaching on faith as the beginning of salvation. His canticle (Hab 3) is used at Morning Prayer in the Liturgy of the Hours, and his final confession, 'though the fig tree does not flourish... yet I will rejoice in the LORD' (Hab 3:17-18), is a classic of hope in desolation.
know: Dialogues with God about evil (Hab 1-2).
'The righteous will live by his faith' (Hab 2:4).
Carried by an angel to feed Daniel in the lions' den (Dan 14:33-39).

people.name: Hur (grandfather of Bezalel)
people.summary: Man of Judah, grandfather of the craftsman Bezalel through his son Uri. 1 Chronicles makes him a son of Caleb son of Hezron and Ephrath.
know: Father of Uri and grandfather of Bezalel (Exo 31:2).
Of the tribe of Judah.
Possibly the same as Moses' companion Hur; Scripture does not say.

people.name: Jared
people.summary: Son of Mahalalel and father of Enoch; he lived 962 years.
know: Second-longest lifespan in Genesis after Methuselah
Father of Enoch who 'walked with God'

people.name: Joel son of Samuel
people.summary: Joel, Samuel's firstborn, judged at Beersheba but took bribes and perverted justice, prompting the elders to demand a king. Through his son Heman the singer, Samuel's line served in the Temple music.
know: Corrupt judge at Beersheba
Father of Heman the singer

people.name: John Hyrcanus
people.summary: Simon's son John, made commander of the army at Gazara, who with his brother Judas defeated Cendebaeus. When his father and brothers were murdered he escaped the assassins sent against him and succeeded Simon as high priest and ruler (134-104 BC); 1 Maccabees ends by referring to the chronicles of his high priesthood.
know: Called simply 'John' in 1 Maccabees; 'Hyrcanus' is known from Josephus.
Defeated Cendebaeus (1 Macc 16:1-10).
Succeeded his father as high priest (1 Macc 16:24).
Not the Hyrcanus son of Tobias of 2 Macc 3:11.

people.name: Joseph of Arimathea
people.summary: Joseph of Arimathea was a rich and respected member of the council, a good and righteous man looking for the Kingdom of God, who had not consented to the council's decision. A secret disciple, he boldly asked Pilate for Jesus' body, wrapped it in clean linen and laid it in his own new tomb cut in the rock.
people.catholic: Joseph fulfils the prophecy that the Servant would be 'with a rich man in his death' (Is 53:9) and is cited with Nicodemus as a secret disciple among the leaders (CCC 595). His care for Jesus' body is honoured in the Fourteenth Station of the Cross and in the corporal work of mercy of burying the dead. Medieval legends link him with Glastonbury and the Holy Grail, but these are not historical tradition.
know: A rich council member from Arimathaea (Mt 27:57; Lk 23:50-51).
Asked Pilate for Jesus' body (Mk 15:43).
Laid Jesus in his own new tomb (Mt 27:60).
Commemorated with Nicodemus on August 31.
people.feast: August 31 (Sts Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus, Roman Martyrology)

people.name: Lamech (father of Noah)
people.summary: Son of Methuselah in the line of Seth. At Noah's birth he prophesied that the child would bring comfort from the toil caused by the cursed ground. He lived 777 years.
people.catholic: His hope that Noah would bring 'comfort' (Gen 5:29) expresses the longing for relief from the curse that runs through the primeval story. Luke lists him among Jesus' ancestors (Lk 3:36).
know: Father of Noah (Gen 5:28-29)
Named Noah hoping he would bring comfort
Lived 777 years
Different from Lamech son of Methushael

people.name: Mahalalel
people.summary: Son of Kenan and father of Jared; he lived 895 years.
know: Called 'Mahalaleel' in Luke 3:37
Lived 895 years

people.name: Methuselah
people.summary: Son of Enoch and grandfather of Noah. At 969 years he is the longest-lived person in the Bible.
people.catholic: Luke lists him among Jesus' ancestors (Lk 3:37). His proverbial age illustrates the long lifespans of the generations before the Flood, which Genesis shows shrinking as sin spreads.
know: Lived 969 years, the longest recorded life (Gen 5:27)
Son of Enoch, father of Lamech, grandfather of Noah
Not the same as Methushael of Cain's line

people.name: Pharaoh's daughter
people.summary: Daughter of the Pharaoh who ordered the Hebrew boys drowned. She found the infant Moses in a basket among the reeds, had compassion on him, hired his own mother as nurse, and raised him as her son, giving him his name.
people.catholic: Pharaoh's daughter shows mercy that defies her father's death-decree, and God uses a Gentile woman's compassion to preserve Israel's deliverer. Stephen recalls her in his speech (Acts 7:21), and Hebrews 11:24 notes that Moses by faith refused to be called her son.
know: Found Moses in the Nile (Exo 2:5-6).
Named him Moses, 'because I drew him out of the water' (Exo 2:10).
Unnamed in Exodus.

people.name: Phinehas
people.summary: Phinehas, son of Eli (not the zealous grandson of Aaron), was a corrupt priest at Shiloh who died with his brother Hophni when the Ark was captured. On hearing the news his wife went into labour and named their son Ichabod, 'the glory has departed from Israel'.
know: Son of Eli; brother of Hophni
Abused the sacrifices and the women serving at the sanctuary
Father of Ichabod and Ahitub

people.name: Rechab
people.summary: Rechab was the father of Jonadab and gave his name to the Rechabite clan.
know: The Rechabites are connected with the Kenites in 1 Chronicles 2:55.

people.name: Shammah son of Jesse
people.summary: Shammah (also Shimea, Shimeah or Shimei), Jesse's third son, was passed over by Samuel and fought in Saul's army; his sons Jonadab and Jonathan appear in David's story.
know: Called Shimea in Chronicles
Father of Jonadab and Jonathan

people.name: Shebna
people.summary: Shebna was the royal treasurer 'over the house' under Hezekiah, whom Isaiah rebuked for carving himself a grand tomb and told he would be deposed in favour of Eliakim. He appears later as the scribe in Hezekiah's delegation to the Assyrians.
know: Rebuked by Isaiah for his pride
Part of the delegation to the Rabshakeh
Rebuked for pride in building his own tomb (Isa 22:16).
Deposed in favour of Eliakim.
Appears as 'the scribe' in Isa 36-37 and 2 Kings 18-19.

people.name: Simon the Benjamite
people.summary: The Temple official who quarrelled with Onias III and betrayed the Temple treasury to the Seleucids, prompting Heliodorus' mission; he went on slandering Onias.
know: Told Apollonius of the Temple's wealth (2 Macc 3:4-6).
Brother of Menelaus (2 Macc 4:23).

people.name: Sons of Korah
people.summary: The Levite descendants of Korah, who survived their ancestor's rebellion and served as Temple gatekeepers and singers. Eleven psalms bear their name (Ps 42-49 and 84, 85, 87, 88), among them 'As the deer pants for the water brooks' and 'How lovely are your dwellings'.
people.catholic: The Korahite psalms are beloved in Catholic liturgy: Psalm 43 (42 in the Vulgate, a continuation of the Korahite Psalm 42) opened the traditional prayers at the foot of the altar ('I will go to the altar of God'), and Psalm 84 expresses longing for God's house. That the sons of a rebel became singers of praise is a sign of God's mercy across generations.
know: Group entry.
Survived Korah's rebellion (Num 26:11).
Gatekeepers of the tent (1 Chr 9:19).
Psalms 42-49, 84-85, 87-88 bear their name.
Heman the singer was of this family.

people.name: Stephen
people.summary: Stephen, 'a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit', was first among the Seven chosen to serve the Jerusalem church. He worked great signs and debated with members of the Synagogue of the Freedmen, who brought him before the council on charges of blasphemy against the Temple and the Law. After a long speech retelling Israel's history, he saw the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at God's right hand; he was stoned outside the city while praying for his killers, with young Saul approving.
people.catholic: St Stephen is the Protomartyr, the first to give his life for Christ; his feast on December 26, the day after Christmas, joins the birth of Christ to the 'birth into heaven' of his first witness. His death closely echoes Christ's Passion: he commends his spirit to the Lord Jesus and forgives his persecutors (Acts 7:59-60). The choice of the Seven, on whom the apostles laid hands after prayer (Acts 6:6), is traditionally read as the institution of the diaconate, the first degree of Holy Orders, ordained 'not unto the priesthood but unto the ministry' (CCC 1569-1571). The Fathers (e.g. St Augustine) saw Paul's conversion as fruit of Stephen's prayer. His relics were discovered in 415 and spread his cult widely.
know: One of the Seven chosen in Acts 6 and the first named.
Gave the longest speech in Acts (Acts 7).
Saw 'the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God' (Acts 7:56).
First Christian martyr; feast December 26.
His death began a persecution that scattered the Church beyond Jerusalem (Acts 8:1-4, 11:19).

relations.type: saw in glory at God's right hand

people.name: Tamar
people.summary: Wife of Judah's son Er and then, by levirate duty, of Onan; both died. When Judah failed to give her his son Shelah, she disguised herself and conceived by Judah himself, keeping his seal, cord and staff as proof. Judah confessed 'She is more righteous than I,' and she bore the twins Perez and Zerah.
people.catholic: Tamar is the first of four women named in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus (Mt 1:3), with Rahab, Ruth and 'the wife of Uriah'; Church Fathers such as St John Chrysostom saw in them a sign that Christ came to save sinners and Gentiles and was not ashamed of his ancestry. Her determination secured the line of Judah through which David and the Messiah came.
know: Widow of Er and Onan (Gen 38:6-10)
Kept Judah's signet, cord and staff (Gen 38:18)
'She is more righteous than I' (Gen 38:26)
Mother of the twins Perez and Zerah
Named in Jesus' genealogy (Mt 1:3)

people.name: Vashti
people.summary: Ahasuerus' queen who refused to appear at his feast when summoned; on Memucan's advice she was deposed, opening the way for Esther.
know: Refused the king's summons (Est 1:12).
Deposed by royal decree (Est 1:19-21).

people.name: Zebulun
people.summary: Sixth son of Jacob and Leah, whose name Leah linked to her hope that Jacob would 'honour' (dwell with) her. Jacob foretold he would dwell at the shore of the sea.
people.catholic: With Naphtali, his land is the 'Galilee of the nations' where Isaiah's great light dawns, fulfilled in Jesus' ministry (Isa 9:1-2; Mt 4:13-16).
know: Son of Jacob and Leah (Gen 30:19-20)
Father of Sered, Elon and Jahleel (Gen 46:14)
'Zebulun will dwell at the haven of the sea' (Gen 49:13)

people.name: Zibeon
people.summary: A son of Seir the Horite and chief in the land of Edom; father of Aiah and Anah.
know: Called 'the Hivite' in Gen 36:2
Grandfather of Oholibamah

people.name: Zilpah
people.role: Servant of Leah; concubine of Jacob
people.summary: Leah's servant, given her by Laban, whom Leah gave to Jacob as a wife; she bore Gad and Asher.
know: Mother of Gad and Asher (Gen 30:9-13)

people.name: Zippor
people.summary: Father of Balak, king of Moab.
know: Father of Balak (Num 22:2).

people.name: Ahinoam of Jezreel
people.summary: Ahinoam of Jezreel married David during his fugitive years, was captured and rescued at Ziklag, and bore his firstborn son Amnon at Hebron.
know: Mother of Amnon, David's firstborn

people.name: Antiochus VI
people.summary: The young son of Alexander Balas whom Tryphon set on the throne against Demetrius II; he confirmed Jonathan's high priesthood but was soon murdered by Tryphon.
know: Raised by Imalcue the Arabian (1 Macc 11:39).
Confirmed Jonathan (1 Macc 11:57).
Killed by Tryphon (1 Macc 13:31).

people.name: Antiochus VII Sidetes
people.summary: 'Antiochus son of Demetrius the king', who wrote to Simon confirming his privileges and granting him coinage, besieged Tryphon at Dor, then turned against Simon and sent Cendebaeus to invade Judea.
know: Granted Simon the right to mint coins (1 Macc 15:6).
Broke his agreement (1 Macc 15:27).

people.name: Aquila
people.summary: Aquila, a Jew from Pontus, came to Corinth with his wife Priscilla after Claudius expelled the Jews from Rome. Paul stayed and worked with them as a fellow tentmaker; they travelled with him to Ephesus, where they took Apollos aside and explained the way of God more accurately.
people.catholic: Priscilla and Aquila are the New Testament's great missionary couple: tentmakers who worked with Paul, risked their lives for him, hosted a church in their home, and taught the faith. They show marriage as a partnership in the apostolate and the home as a 'domestic church' (cf. CCC 1655-1657). They are commemorated together in the Roman Martyrology (July 8).
know: A Jew of Pontus and a tentmaker.
Always named with his wife Priscilla (Prisca).
Instructed Apollos at Ephesus (Acts 18:26).
Hosted a church in their house (1 Cor 16:19; Rom 16:5).

people.name: Azariah son of Ahimaaz
people.summary: Azariah son of Ahimaaz is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6. 1 Kings 4:2 lists an 'Azariah the son of Zadok' as Solomon's priest, probably the same man (grandson of Zadok).
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

people.name: Azariah son of Johanan
people.summary: Azariah son of Johanan is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6. He is noted as the one 'who executed the priest's office in the house that Solomon built'.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

people.name: Bagoas
people.summary: The eunuch in charge of Holofernes' household, who invited Judith to the fatal banquet and next morning discovered his master's headless body.
know: Shut the tent the night Holofernes died (Jdt 13:1).
Found the body and raised the alarm (Jdt 14:14-18).

people.name: Basemath (daughter of Ishmael)
people.summary: Daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth whom Esau married to please his father; mother of Reuel. Gen 28:9 calls her Mahalath.
know: Called Mahalath in Gen 28:9 and Basemath in Gen 36:3
Mother of Reuel (Gen 36:4)
Esau married her after seeing that Canaanite wives displeased Isaac (Gen 28:8-9)

people.name: Beriah (son of Asher)
people.summary: A son of Asher who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)
Father of Heber and Malchiel (Gen 46:17)

people.name: Cendebaeus
people.summary: Commander of the coast under Antiochus VII who invaded Judea and was routed by John Hyrcanus and Judas, sons of Simon.
know: Fortified Kidron (1 Macc 15:39).
Defeated near Modin (1 Macc 16:4-10).

people.name: Cush
people.summary: Firstborn son of Ham, ancestor of the Cushites (the peoples south of Egypt) and father of Nimrod.
know: Cush is the biblical name for the region of the upper Nile ('Ethiopia')
Father of Nimrod (Gen 10:8)

people.name: Delilah
people.summary: Woman of the valley of Sorek whom Samson loved. Bribed by the Philistine lords with eleven hundred pieces of silver each, she pressed him until he revealed that his strength lay in his uncut hair, then had it shaved while he slept and handed him to the Philistines.
people.catholic: Delilah's betrayal of Samson for silver has been compared by Christian writers to Judas' betrayal of Christ. Her persistent pressure is also a classic image of temptation that wears down resistance.
know: From the valley of Sorek (Jdg 16:4).
Paid by the Philistine lords (Jdg 16:5).
Had Samson's hair cut (Jdg 16:19).

people.name: Ebed-melech the Ethiopian
people.summary: Ebed-melech, an Ethiopian eunuch in Zedekiah's palace, pleaded with the king when Jeremiah was left to die in a muddy cistern, then drew him out with ropes and padded rags. Jeremiah gave him God's promise that he would be spared when the city fell, 'because you have put your trust in me'.
people.catholic: A Gentile who shows mercy to God's prophet when Israel's own leaders do not, Ebed-melech is often read alongside the Ethiopian eunuch of Acts 8 as a sign that salvation is offered to all nations through faith.
know: His name means 'servant of the king'.
Rescued Jeremiah from the cistern with thirty men (Jer 38:7-13).
Promised deliverance because he trusted in the Lord (Jer 39:15-18).

people.name: Elimelech
people.summary: Man of Bethlehem in Judah who, during a famine in the days of the judges, took his wife Naomi and sons Mahlon and Chilion to Moab, where he died. Boaz redeemed his land and raised up his name through Ruth.
know: From Bethlehem, an Ephrathite (Ruth 1:2).
Died in Moab (Ruth 1:3).
Boaz was his kinsman (Ruth 2:1).
Name means 'my God is king'.

people.name: Eliphaz the Temanite
people.summary: The first and senior of Job's three friends, from Teman in Edom. He argued that the innocent never perish and that Job must have sinned, appealing to a mysterious night vision. God told him that he and his friends had not spoken rightly of him, and they were forgiven only through Job's prayer.
people.catholic: The friends illustrate a too-simple theology of retribution that the book corrects; their pardon through Job's intercession and sacrifice (Job 42:8-9) has been read as a figure of Christ's priestly intercession.
know: Speaks in Job 4-5, 15, 22.
Rebuked by God (Job 42:7).
Not to be confused with Esau's son Eliphaz.

people.name: Elishama
people.summary: Son of Ammihud and leader of the tribe of Ephraim in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Ephraim's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar. According to 1 Chronicles 7:26-27 he was the grandfather of Joshua.
know: Son of Ammihud, prince of Ephraim (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Ephraim's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:48).
1 Chronicles 7:26-27 lists Elishama son of Ammihud as father of Nun and grandfather of Joshua.

people.name: Er
people.summary: Judah's firstborn by Shua's daughter, husband of Tamar; he was wicked in the LORD's sight, and the LORD put him to death.
know: First husband of Tamar (Gen 38:6)
Died childless (Gen 38:7)
Not the Er in Luke 3:28

people.name: Gershom
people.summary: Firstborn son of Moses and Zipporah, born in Midian; Moses named him Gershom, saying, 'I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign land.' Judges 18:30 names his son Jonathan as priest to the Danites' idol.
know: Name linked to 'a sojourner there' (Exo 2:22).
Firstborn of Moses and Zipporah.
Ancestor of Jonathan, the Danites' priest (Jdg 18:30), and of Shebuel (1 Chr 23:16).

people.name: Haran (brother of Abraham)
people.summary: Youngest son of Terah, who died in Ur of the Chaldees while his father was alive. He was the father of Lot, Milcah and Iscah.
know: Father of Lot (Gen 11:27)
Died before his father in Ur (Gen 11:28)
Not to be confused with the city of Haran where Terah settled

people.name: Herod Agrippa I
people.summary: Herod Agrippa I, grandson of Herod the Great, is called simply 'Herod the king' in Acts 12. To please the Jewish leaders he had James the brother of John killed with the sword and imprisoned Peter, who was freed by an angel. At Caesarea, when the crowd hailed his speech as 'the voice of a god', an angel of the Lord struck him because he did not give God the glory, and he died eaten by worms.
people.catholic: He is the first ruler to make an apostle a martyr (St James, Acts 12:2). The Church's unceasing prayer for the imprisoned Peter (Acts 12:5) is a classic image of the Church praying for the Pope. His death illustrates the downfall of pride that claims divine honor.
know: Called 'Herod' in Acts 12; identified by the historian Josephus as Agrippa I.
Executed James son of Zebedee and imprisoned Peter.
Struck down by an angel at Caesarea (Acts 12:23).
According to Josephus, father of Agrippa II, Bernice and Drusilla.

people.name: Herodias
people.summary: Herodias, granddaughter of Herod the Great, left her husband Philip to marry his brother Herod Antipas. When John the Baptist declared the marriage unlawful, she nursed a grudge against him, and at Herod's birthday feast she prompted her daughter to ask for John's head on a platter.
people.catholic: Herodias is often compared with Jezebel, who persecuted Elijah, since Jesus identifies John with Elijah. John's death for rebuking her marriage makes him a martyr for the indissolubility and holiness of marriage.
know: Wife first of Philip, then of his brother Herod Antipas (Mk 6:17).
Held a grudge against John the Baptist (Mk 6:19).
Prompted her daughter to request John's head (Mt 14:8).

people.name: Hezron (son of Reuben)
people.summary: A son of Reuben who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)
Not Hezron son of Perez

people.name: Ittai the Gittite
people.summary: Ittai, a Philistine of Gath newly come to David with six hundred men, refused to turn back when David fled Absalom: 'wherever my lord the king is, in death or in life, there your servant will be'. He commanded a third of David's army.
people.catholic: Ittai, a foreigner, pledges loyalty to the rejected king in words close to Ruth's and to Peter's 'Lord, I will go with you to death' - an image of Gentiles cleaving to the rejected Messiah.
know: A Philistine from Gath
Swore loyalty to David in exile
Commanded a third of the army

people.name: Jabin (in Judges)
people.summary: King of Canaan reigning in Hazor who oppressed Israel cruelly for twenty years with nine hundred iron chariots under his commander Sisera, until the victory of Deborah and Barak; Israel then pressed on until they destroyed him.
know: Reigned in Hazor (Jdg 4:2).
Sisera was his army commander.
Oppressed Israel twenty years (Jdg 4:3).
Remembered in Ps 83:9.

people.name: Jael
people.summary: Wife of Heber the Kenite, who welcomed the fleeing Sisera into her tent, gave him milk, covered him, and while he slept drove a tent peg through his temple, fulfilling Deborah's word that the LORD would sell Sisera into a woman's hand.
people.catholic: The Song of Deborah calls Jael 'blessed above women' (Jdg 5:24), words echoed of Judith (Jdt 13:18) and of Mary by Elizabeth (Lk 1:42). Patristic and medieval writers read her, like Judith, as a type of Mary, through whom the enemy's head is crushed (cf. Gen 3:15).
know: Wife of Heber the Kenite (Jdg 4:17).
Killed Sisera with a tent peg (Jdg 4:21).
'Blessed above women' (Jdg 5:24).

people.name: Jair (son of Manasseh)
people.summary: Descendant of Manasseh who captured the villages of Gilead and Argob and named them Havvoth Jair, 'the villages of Jair'.
know: Called 'son of Manasseh' (Num 32:41), i.e. a descendant.
Took villages east of the Jordan and named them Havvoth Jair.
Not the judge Jair of Judges 10.

people.name: Jehoahaz of Judah
people.summary: Jehoahaz (Shallum), son of Josiah, was made king by the people after Megiddo but reigned only three months before Pharaoh Necoh deposed him and took him to Egypt, where he died.
know: Also called Shallum (Jer 22:11)
Reigned three months
Died captive in Egypt

people.name: Jehohanan son of Eliashib
people.summary: Son of the priest Eliashib in whose Temple room Ezra fasted and mourned over the people's unfaithfulness; later lists name a Johanan in the high-priestly succession.
know: Ezra mourned in his chamber (Ezra 10:6).
Probably the 'Johanan son of Eliashib' of Neh 12:22-23.

people.name: Joah son of Asaph
people.summary: Joah son of Asaph was Hezekiah's recorder and one of the three officials who met the Rabshakeh.
know: Royal recorder

people.name: Joakim
people.summary: Joakim was a wealthy and honoured Jew in Babylon whose house and garden were the gathering place of the community and its judges; his wife Susanna was falsely accused there.
know: Not King Jehoiakim of Judah.
Praised God with Susanna's family when she was vindicated (Dan 13:63).

people.name: Joktan
people.summary: Son of Eber and brother of Peleg; father of thirteen sons who settled in Arabia, among them Sheba, Ophir and Havilah.
know: Father of thirteen Arabian peoples (Gen 10:26-29)

people.name: Jonathan son of Abiathar
people.summary: Jonathan, son of Abiathar the priest, ran messages to David during Absalom's revolt and later brought Adonijah the news that Solomon had been made king.
know: Hid in a well at Bahurim with Ahimaaz
Announced Solomon's anointing to Adonijah's feast

people.name: Jonathan son of Shimei
people.summary: Jonathan, son of David's brother Shimei (Shimea), killed a six-fingered giant of Gath.
know: Killed a giant at Gath

people.name: Kenaz
people.summary: Father of the judge Othniel. Joshua 15:17 and Judges 1:13 call Othniel 'son of Kenaz, Caleb's (younger) brother'.
know: Father of Othniel (Jos 15:17).
Related to Caleb; whether Kenaz or Othniel is meant as Caleb's brother is debated.

people.name: Manasses (husband of Judith)
people.summary: Judith's husband, of her own tribe and family, who died of sunstroke during the barley harvest, leaving her wealthy; she was buried beside him.
know: Died during the barley harvest (Jdt 8:2-3).
Spelled 'Manasses' in this translation.

people.name: Mica
people.summary: Mica, young son of Mephibosheth, carried on the line of Saul and Jonathan.
know: Called Micah in 1 Chronicles

people.name: Milcah (wife of Nahor)
people.summary: Daughter of Haran who married her uncle Nahor and bore him eight sons, including Bethuel; grandmother of Rebekah.
know: Daughter of Haran and sister of Lot (Gen 11:29)
Grandmother of Rebekah (Gen 24:24)

people.name: Nahash
people.summary: Nahash the Ammonite besieged Jabesh-gilead, demanding to gouge out every right eye; Saul's rescue of the city confirmed his kingship. Nahash later showed kindness to David.
know: His threat launched Saul's reign
Father of Hanun

people.name: Obadiah
people.summary: Obadiah, who 'feared the LORD greatly', was in charge of Ahab's household; when Jezebel was killing the prophets he hid a hundred of them in two caves and fed them. He arranged Elijah's meeting with Ahab before Carmel.
people.catholic: Some Jewish tradition identified him with the prophet Obadiah, but Scripture does not. He is a model of the believer who serves faithfully and courageously within a hostile court.
know: Hid 100 prophets in caves
Brought Ahab to meet Elijah

people.name: Oholibamah
people.summary: Wife of Esau, daughter of Anah and granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite (Horite); mother of Jeush, Jalam and Korah.
know: Mother of Jeush, Jalam and Korah (Gen 36:5)
Some interpreters identify her with Judith of Gen 26:34

people.name: Onan
people.summary: Judah's second son, told to raise offspring for his dead brother Er by Tamar (the levirate duty). Knowing the child would not count as his, he spilled his seed on the ground, and the LORD put him to death.
people.catholic: Catholic moral tradition has cited Onan's act in teaching on the integrity of the marital act; Pius XI's encyclical Casti Connubii (1930), quoting St Augustine, refers to it. The text also stresses his refusal of the duty to his dead brother.
know: Second son of Judah (Gen 38:4)
Refused to raise offspring for Er (Gen 38:9)
The LORD put him to death (Gen 38:10)

people.name: Othniel
people.summary: Son of Kenaz, of Caleb's family, who captured Kiriath Sepher (Debir) and won Caleb's daughter Achsah as wife. When Israel served Cushan Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia for eight years, the Spirit of the LORD came upon him; he delivered Israel and the land had rest forty years. He is the first of the judges.
people.catholic: Othniel is the model judge in whom the pattern of the book is laid out plainly: sin, oppression, crying out, a Spirit-filled deliverer, and rest. The Church reads the judges' Spirit-given deliverance as a foreshadowing of Christ, on whom the Spirit rests fully (Isa 11:2; Lk 4:18).
know: First judge of Israel (Jdg 3:9).
Took Kiriath Sepher and married Achsah (Jos 15:17).
Defeated Cushan Rishathaim (Jdg 3:10).
The land had rest forty years (Jdg 3:11).

people.name: Philip (regent of Antiochus IV)
people.summary: One of Antiochus IV's friends whom the dying king set over his kingdom and entrusted with his son; Lysias drove him from Antioch. He carried the king's body home and, fearing Antiochus V, withdrew to Egypt.
know: Called the king's 'foster brother' (2 Macc 9:29).
Seized Antioch from Lysias (1 Macc 6:55-63).
Distinct from Philip the Phrygian, governor of Jerusalem (2 Macc 5:22).

people.name: Priscilla
people.summary: Priscilla (Prisca) was the wife of Aquila and, with him, a co-worker of Paul at Corinth, Ephesus and Rome. Paul thanks them for risking their necks for his life, and the churches of the Gentiles give thanks for them.
people.catholic: Priscilla and Aquila are the New Testament's great missionary couple: tentmakers who worked with Paul, risked their lives for him, hosted a church in their home, and taught the faith. They show marriage as a partnership in the apostolate and the home as a 'domestic church' (cf. CCC 1655-1657). They are commemorated together in the Roman Martyrology (July 8). That she is often named before her husband suggests her prominence in the community.
know: Called Prisca by Paul.
Explained the way of God to Apollos with Aquila (Acts 18:26).
Paul's 'fellow worker in Christ Jesus' (Rom 16:3).

people.name: Ptolemy son of Dorymenes
people.summary: One of the generals Lysias chose against Judah and governor of Coelesyria and Phoenicia; Menelaus bribed him to sway Antiochus IV, and he promoted the decree forcing Greek cities to persecute the Jews.
know: Chosen with Nicanor and Gorgias (1 Macc 3:38).
Bribed by Menelaus (2 Macc 4:45-47).
Urged the persecution decree (2 Macc 6:8).

people.name: Reu
people.summary: Son of Peleg and father of Serug.
know: Listed in Luke 3:35

people.name: Reuel (son of Esau)
people.summary: Son of Esau by Basemath, Ishmael's daughter; father of the Edomite chiefs Nahath, Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah.
know: Not Reuel (Jethro), Moses' father-in-law
Father of four Edomite chiefs (Gen 36:13)

people.name: Serug
people.summary: Son of Reu and father of Nahor, the grandfather of Abraham.
know: Listed in Luke 3:35

people.name: Shalmaneser
people.summary: Shalmaneser (V) of Assyria made Hoshea his vassal, imprisoned him for treachery and besieged Samaria for three years until it fell. Tobit calls him Enemessar.
know: Besieged Samaria 725-722 BC
Called Enemessar in Tobit

people.name: Shishak
people.summary: Shishak king of Egypt sheltered the fugitive Jeroboam and, in Rehoboam's fifth year, invaded Judah and carried off the treasures of the Temple and palace, including Solomon's golden shields.
know: Usually identified with Pharaoh Shoshenq I
Plundered Jerusalem under Rehoboam

people.name: Tiglath-pileser
people.summary: Tiglath-pileser (III) of Assyria, called Pul in 2 Kings 15:19, received tribute from Menahem, conquered Galilee and Gilead under Pekah and deported their people, and answered Ahaz's appeal by taking Damascus.
know: Called Pul (his Babylonian throne-name)
Began the deportations of Israel
Chronicles spells him Tilgath-pilneser

people.name: Timna
people.summary: Concubine of Eliphaz son of Esau and mother of Amalek; she is also called the sister of the Horite chief Lotan.
know: Mother of Amalek (Gen 36:12)
Sister of Lotan the Horite (Gen 36:22)

people.name: Zechariah
people.summary: Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, began to prophesy in 520 BC alongside Haggai, encouraging the returned exiles to rebuild the Temple. His night visions include the high priest Joshua clothed in clean garments, the golden lampstand and the two olive trees ('not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit'), and his later oracles speak of a humble king riding on a donkey, a shepherd valued at thirty pieces of silver, and one 'whom they have pierced'.
people.catholic: The Gospels read Zechariah's oracles as fulfilled in the Passion: Jesus enters Jerusalem on Palm Sunday as the king 'humble, and riding on a donkey' (Zech 9:9; Mt 21:4-5; Jn 12:15; CCC 559); he is betrayed for thirty pieces of silver (Zech 11:12-13; Mt 27:9); the shepherd is struck and the sheep scattered (Zech 13:7; Mt 26:31); and they look on him whom they have pierced (Zech 12:10; Jn 19:37), a text the Church contemplates in devotion to the pierced Heart of Jesus. The crowning of Joshua (Jeshua) as 'the Branch' (Zech 6:11-13) was read by the Fathers as a figure of Christ, priest and king — whose Hebrew name is the same as Joshua's.
know: Son of Berechiah, grandson of Iddo (Zech 1:1); Ezra calls him 'son of Iddo'.
Eight night visions (Zech 1-6).
King riding on a donkey (Zech 9:9) — Palm Sunday.
'They will look on me whom they have pierced' (Zech 12:10).

people.name: Zephaniah son of Maaseiah
people.summary: Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, the second priest, was twice sent by Zedekiah to ask Jeremiah's prayers and read to Jeremiah the letter of Shemaiah demanding that he be silenced. After Jerusalem fell he was taken to Riblah and executed.
know: Not the prophet Zephaniah.
Executed at Riblah with Seraiah the chief priest (Jer 52:24-27).

people.name: Abidan
people.summary: Son of Gideoni and leader of the tribe of Benjamin in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Benjamin's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Gideoni, prince of Benjamin (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Benjamin's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:60).

people.name: Abishag the Shunammite
people.summary: Abishag, a beautiful young woman of Shunem, was brought to nurse and warm the aged David. After David's death Adonijah's request to marry her cost him his life.
know: Attended David in his old age
Adonijah's request for her was seen as a claim to the throne

people.name: Achiacharus (Ahikar)
people.summary: Tobit's nephew, son of his brother Anael, who rose to be cupbearer, keeper of the signet and chief administrator under the Assyrian king Esarhaddon ('Sarchedonus'). He interceded to bring Tobit back to Nineveh and supported him during his blindness. He is the hero of the ancient Near Eastern 'Story of Ahikar', in which his adopted nephew betrays him.
people.catholic: Tobit appeals to Ahikar's story as proof that almsgiving delivers from death while treachery falls into its own snare (Tob 14:10-11). The cameo shows the inspired author drawing on wider wisdom traditions.
know: Known outside the Bible as Ahikar.
Cupbearer and keeper of the signet under Sarchedonus (Esarhaddon).
Supported blind Tobit (Tob 2:10).
Attended Tobias' wedding feast with Nasbas (Tob 11:18).

people.name: Achsah
people.summary: Daughter of Caleb, promised to whoever captured Kiriath Sepher and given to Othniel. She urged her husband to ask for a field and herself asked her father for springs of water, receiving the upper and lower springs.
people.catholic: Achsah's bold, successful petition to her father has been used by spiritual writers as an image of confident prayer to God the Father.
know: Daughter of Caleb (Jos 15:16).
Wife of Othniel.
Asked for and received springs of water (Jos 15:18-19).

people.name: Adah (wife of Esau)
people.summary: Wife of Esau, daughter of Elon the Hittite, and mother of his firstborn Eliphaz.
know: Mother of Eliphaz (Gen 36:4)
Probably the same woman called Basemath daughter of Elon in Gen 26:34

people.name: Agag
people.summary: Agag king of the Amalekites was spared by Saul against God's command; Samuel himself put him to death at Gilgal.
know: His sparing cost Saul the kingdom
Haman in Esther is called an Agagite

people.name: Ahiezer
people.summary: Son of Ammishaddai and leader of the tribe of Dan in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Dan's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Ammishaddai, prince of Dan (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Dan's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:66).

people.name: Ahira
people.summary: Son of Enan and leader of the tribe of Naphtali in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Naphtali's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Enan, prince of Naphtali (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Naphtali's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:78).

people.name: Ahitub
people.summary: Ahitub, son of Phinehas and grandson of Eli, was the father of the priests Ahijah and Ahimelech of Nob.
know: Brother of Ichabod
Father of Ahimelech, the priest of Nob

people.name: Ahitub son of Amariah
people.summary: Ahitub son of Amariah is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

people.name: Ananias of Damascus
people.summary: Ananias was a devout disciple in Damascus. In a vision the Lord sent him to Saul, who had been blinded on the road; despite his fear of the persecutor, he went, laid his hands on him, and Saul regained his sight and was baptized.
people.catholic: Ananias is honored as the man who welcomed the Church's fiercest enemy as 'Brother Saul' and baptized him (Acts 9:17-18; 22:16). The Lord's words to him, that Saul is 'my chosen vessel', express the Church's understanding of Paul's vocation.
know: Sent by the Lord in a vision to the house of Judah on Straight Street (Acts 9:10-11).
Called Saul 'Brother' and laid hands on him.
Baptized Saul (Acts 9:18; 22:16).
Paul describes him as devout and respected by the Jews (Acts 22:12).

people.name: Antiochus V Eupator
people.summary: The boy-king son of Antiochus IV, raised by Lysias and made king at his father's death. With Lysias he invaded Judea and besieged Beth-zur and Mount Zion, then made peace when Philip seized Antioch. He and Lysias were killed by the army when Demetrius I came from Rome.
know: Named Eupator by Lysias (1 Macc 6:17).
Battle of Beth-zechariah (1 Macc 6:28-47).
Killed at Demetrius' order (1 Macc 7:2-4).

people.name: Aristarchus
people.summary: Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was seized in the Ephesian riot, travelled with Paul toward Jerusalem, and sailed with him on the voyage to Rome. Paul calls him 'my fellow prisoner'.
know: From Thessalonica (Acts 20:4; 27:2).
Shared Paul's voyage and imprisonment (Acts 27:2; Col 4:10).
Sends greetings in Colossians and Philemon.

people.name: Bildad the Shuhite
people.summary: The second of Job's friends, who defended the tradition of the ancients and insisted that God does not reject the blameless, implying Job's children died for their sins.
know: Speaks in Job 8, 18, 25.
Rebuked by God (Job 42:7-9).

people.name: Chedorlaomer
people.summary: Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, was one of the four eastern kings who warred against the cities of the plain and carried off Lot; Abram defeated them.
know: One of the 'four kings against the five' (Gen 14:9)
Leader of the coalition; the cities had served him twelve years (Gen 14:4)

people.name: Doeg
people.summary: Doeg the Edomite, Saul's chief herdsman, saw Ahimelech help David at Nob, informed Saul, and when Saul's guards refused, himself slaughtered the priests of Nob and the town.
know: Informer and executioner of the priests
Psalm 52 is traditionally linked to him

people.name: Ebed
people.summary: Father of Gaal, who rebelled against Abimelech.
know: Father of Gaal (Jdg 9:26).

people.name: Eliab
people.summary: Eliab, Jesse's firstborn, was so impressive that Samuel thought him the LORD's anointed, but God 'looks at the heart'. At the Valley of Elah he scolded David for coming to the battle.
know: Rejected despite his stature
Served in Saul's army

people.name: Eliab
people.summary: Son of Helon and leader of the tribe of Zebulun in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Zebulun's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Helon, prince of Zebulun (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Zebulun's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:24).

people.name: Eliab
people.summary: Reubenite, son of Pallu, and father of Dathan, Abiram and Nemuel.
know: Son of Pallu, grandson of Reuben (Num 26:8).
Father of Dathan and Abiram (Num 16:1).

people.name: Eliasaph
people.summary: Son of Deuel and leader of the tribe of Gad in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Gad's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Deuel, prince of Gad (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Gad's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:42).

people.name: Elizur
people.summary: Son of Shedeur and leader of the tribe of Reuben in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Reuben's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Shedeur, prince of Reuben (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Reuben's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:30).

people.name: Elzaphan
people.summary: Son of Uzziel, cousin of Aaron. He helped carry out the bodies of Nadab and Abihu, and as Elizaphan was made prince of the Kohathite clans.
know: Son of Uzziel (Exo 6:22).
Called Elizaphan, prince of the Kohathites (Num 3:30).
Helped remove Nadab and Abihu's bodies (Lev 10:4).

people.name: Esarhaddon
people.summary: Esarhaddon succeeded his murdered father Sennacherib; he settled foreign peoples in Samaria, and Tobit (calling him Sarchedonus) says he made Achiacharus (Ahikar), Tobit's nephew, second to himself.
know: Called Sarchedonus in Tobit

people.name: Ethan the Ezrahite
people.summary: A Merarite Levite musician appointed under David with Heman and Asaph, and one of the wise men whom Solomon surpassed. Psalm 89, on God's covenant with David and its apparent failure, is ascribed to him.
people.catholic: Psalm 89 ('I have made a covenant with my chosen one', Ps 89:3) is a central text for the Church's reading of Christ as the eternal Son of David; it is sung at Christmas Vigil and on the solemnity of St Joseph.
know: Son of Kishi/Kushaiah, of Merari (1 Chr 6:44; 15:17).
Psalm 89 bears his name.
Named in 1 Kgs 4:31.
Possibly identical with Jeduthun.

people.name: Eve
people.summary: The first woman, built by God from the man's rib to be his partner. Deceived by the serpent, she ate the forbidden fruit and gave it to Adam; God announced enmity between the serpent and the woman's offspring. Adam named her Eve because she was 'the mother of all the living'; she bore Cain, Abel and Seth.
people.catholic: The Fathers contrast Eve with Mary, the New Eve: St Irenaeus wrote that 'the knot of Eve's disobedience was untied by Mary's obedience', and St Jerome 'death through Eve, life through Mary' (both quoted in CCC 494). Gen 3:15, the 'protoevangelium' or first announcement of the Gospel, is read by Christian tradition as foretelling the New Adam and the New Eve, Mary, who shares in his victory over sin (CCC 410-411). Mary is thus honoured as the true 'mother of the living' in the order of grace. The Catechism also names Eve among the women whose mission prepared for Mary's (CCC 489).
know: Created from Adam's rib as 'bone of my bones' (Gen 2:21-23)
Name means roughly 'living': 'mother of all the living' (Gen 3:20)
Gen 3:15 promises enmity between the woman's offspring and the serpent
The Fathers call Mary the 'New Eve'
Mother of Cain, Abel and Seth (Gen 4:1-2, 25)

people.name: Gamaliel
people.summary: Son of Pedahzur and leader of the tribe of Manasseh in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Manasseh's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Pedahzur, prince of Manasseh (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Manasseh's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:54).

people.name: Hadad the Edomite
people.summary: Hadad, of the Edomite royal house, escaped Joab's massacre as a child, grew up in Egypt married to Pharaoh's sister-in-law, and returned to oppose Solomon.
know: Raised up by God as an adversary to Solomon

people.name: Haggith
people.summary: Haggith bore David his fourth son, Adonijah, at Hebron.
know: Mother of Adonijah

people.name: Hammedatha
people.summary: Father of Haman, called 'the Bugaean' and once 'the Macedonian' (Est 9:24).
know: Known only as Haman's father.

people.name: Hanani the seer
people.summary: Hanani the seer rebuked King Asa for relying on the king of Syria instead of the LORD - 'the eyes of the LORD run back and forth throughout the whole earth' - and was put in the stocks for it.
know: Imprisoned by Asa
Father of the prophet Jehu

people.name: Hathach
people.summary: The chamberlain who carried messages between Esther and Mordecai during the crisis.
know: Carried Mordecai's 'for such a time' message (Est 4:9-14).

people.name: Hepher
people.summary: Son of Gilead of Manasseh, father of Zelophehad.
know: Son of Gilead, father of Zelophehad (Num 26:32-33).

people.name: Hiram the craftsman
people.summary: Hiram of Tyre, son of a widow of Naphtali (Chronicles: of Dan) and a Tyrian bronze-worker, cast the Temple's bronze pillars Jachin and Boaz, the bronze Sea and its furnishings. Chronicles calls him Huram-abi.
know: Made the pillars Jachin and Boaz
Cast the bronze Sea
Called Huram-abi in Chronicles

people.name: Hophni
people.summary: Hophni, son of Eli, was a priest at Shiloh who with his brother Phinehas treated the LORD's offerings with contempt. Both died on the same day when the Philistines captured the Ark at Aphek.
know: Called 'worthless men' who did not know the LORD
Took the people's sacrifices by force
Died with his brother in battle as foretold

people.name: Jason
people.summary: Jason welcomed Paul and Silas into his house at Thessalonica. A mob attacked the house and dragged Jason before the city rulers, accusing those who 'turned the world upside down'; he had to give security before being released.
know: His house was attacked by a mob (Acts 17:5-9).
A Jason, Paul's relative, sends greetings in Romans 16:21; he may be the same man, but this is not certain.

people.name: Jehu son of Hanani
people.summary: The prophet Jehu son of Hanani pronounced God's judgement on Baasha of Israel, and decades later rebuked Jehoshaphat of Judah for helping the wicked Ahab; he also wrote a history of Jehoshaphat.
know: Prophesied against Baasha
Rebuked Jehoshaphat
Not King Jehu

people.name: Jerahmeel
people.summary: Jerahmeel, firstborn of Hezron, is the ancestor of the Jerahmeelite clans of the Negeb (1 Chr 2:9, 25-33; cf. 1 Sam 27:10).

people.name: Jether
people.summary: Jether (Ithra), called an Ishmaelite in Chronicles and an Israelite in Samuel, fathered Amasa by David's sister Abigail.
know: Also called Ithra

people.name: John (Jonah), father of Peter
people.summary: The father of Simon Peter and Andrew is named in Jesus' words 'Simon Bar Jonah' (Mt 16:17) and 'Simon son of Jonah' (Jn 1:42; 21:15-17).
know: The World English Bible reads 'Jonah'; many manuscripts and translations of John read 'John'.
Father of the apostles Peter and Andrew.

people.name: Joses
people.summary: Joses is named among the 'brothers' of Jesus at Nazareth (Mt 13:55; Mk 6:3) and as a son of the Mary who watched the crucifixion and burial (Mt 27:56; Mk 15:40, 47).
people.catholic: Joses shows the Catholic reading of the 'brothers of the Lord': he and James are explicitly sons of another Mary, so they are Jesus' kinsmen rather than children of the Virgin Mary (CCC 500).
know: Brother of James 'the less' (Mk 15:40).
His mother 'Mary the mother of Joses' saw where Jesus was laid (Mk 15:47).
Not to be confused with Joses called Barnabas (Acts 4:36).

people.name: Korah (son of Esau)
people.role: Son of Esau; chief of Edom
people.summary: A son of Esau by Oholibamah, born in Canaan, and a chief of Edom.
know: Son of Esau and Oholibamah (Gen 36:5)
Not Korah the Levite who rebelled against Moses

people.name: Libni
people.summary: Son of Gershon and grandson of Levi, listed in the Levitical genealogies; head of a Levite clan.
know: Grandson of Levi through Gershon.
Named in the genealogy of Exodus 6 and the census of Numbers 3.

people.name: Mahli
people.summary: Son of Merari and grandson of Levi, listed in the Levitical genealogies; head of a Levite clan.
know: Grandson of Levi through Merari.
Named in the genealogy of Exodus 6 and the census of Numbers 3.

people.name: Malchishua
people.summary: Malchishua, a son of Saul, was killed by the Philistines with his father and brothers on Mount Gilboa.
know: Died at Gilboa

people.name: Michael
people.summary: Michael is 'one of the chief princes' who helps the angel speaking to Daniel against the prince of Persia, and 'the great prince who stands for the children of your people' at the end time. In the New Testament he disputes with the devil over Moses' body and leads the angels in the war in heaven against the dragon.
people.catholic: St Michael is venerated as protector of the Church and defender against Satan; the Prayer to St Michael composed under Pope Leo XIII ('defend us in battle') is widely prayed. The Church celebrates him with Sts Gabriel and Raphael on September 29 and remembers him in the liturgy (CCC 335).
know: Name means 'Who is like God?'
Protector of God's people (Dan 10:13, 21; 12:1).
Called 'the archangel' in Jude 9.
Casts down the dragon in Revelation 12:7-9.

people.name: Midian
people.summary: A son of Abraham by Keturah, ancestor of the Midianites; his sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida and Eldaah.
know: Ancestor of the Midianites, to whom Joseph was sold (Gen 37:28) and among whom Moses later lived
Father of Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida and Eldaah (Gen 25:4)

people.name: Nathan son of David
people.summary: Nathan, a son of David and Bathsheba born in Jerusalem, is otherwise unknown in the Old Testament, but Luke traces the genealogy of Jesus back to David through him rather than through Solomon.
people.catholic: Luke's genealogy (Lk 3:31) runs through Nathan, Matthew's through Solomon. A long tradition, found already in early writers, explains the two lines as Mary's (Luke) and Joseph's (Matthew), or as Joseph's natural and legal descent; either way both make Jesus truly 'Son of David'. Zechariah 12:12 mentions 'the family of the house of Nathan' mourning the pierced one.
know: Son of Bathsheba, full brother of Solomon
Ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy
Not the prophet Nathan

people.name: Nethanel
people.summary: Son of Zuar and leader of the tribe of Issachar in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Issachar's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Zuar, prince of Issachar (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Issachar's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:18).

people.name: Nicodemus
people.role: Pharisee; ruler of the Jews; disciple
people.summary: Nicodemus, a Pharisee and member of the Sanhedrin, came to Jesus by night and was taught that one must be born of water and the Spirit to enter the Kingdom of God. Later he urged the council to give Jesus a fair hearing, and after the crucifixion he brought about a hundred pounds of myrrh and aloes to help Joseph of Arimathea bury Jesus.
people.catholic: Jesus' words to Nicodemus, 'unless one is born of water and the Spirit' (Jn 3:5), are a foundational text for the necessity of Baptism (CCC 1215, 1257), and the same discourse contains 'God so loved the world' (Jn 3:16). He is cited with Joseph of Arimathea as one of the religious leaders who were secret disciples (CCC 595). His journey from night to open devotion models gradual conversion.
know: Came to Jesus by night (Jn 3:2).
Heard 'born of water and the Spirit' and 'God so loved the world' (Jn 3:5, 16).
Defended Jesus before the Pharisees (Jn 7:50-51).
Helped bury Jesus with myrrh and aloes (Jn 19:39).
people.feast: August 31 (Sts Joseph of Arimathea and Nicodemus, Roman Martyrology)

people.name: Oholiab
people.summary: Son of Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan, appointed by God to assist Bezalel. He was an engraver, designer and embroiderer in blue, purple and scarlet, and teacher of others in the work of the tabernacle.
people.catholic: With Bezalel, Oholiab shows that craftsmanship and beauty serve the worship of God; the pairing of a man of Judah and a man of Dan has been noted as all Israel contributing to the sanctuary.
know: Son of Ahisamach, of Dan (Exo 31:6).
Engraver, designer and embroiderer (Exo 38:23).
Given ability to teach (Exo 35:34).

people.name: Pagiel
people.summary: Son of Ochran and leader of the tribe of Asher in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Asher's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Ochran, prince of Asher (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Asher's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:72).

people.name: Pallu
people.summary: Son of Reuben who went down to Egypt with Jacob; ancestor of the Palluite clan and grandfather of Dathan and Abiram.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)
Ancestor of Dathan and Abiram (Num 26:8-9)
Son of Reuben (Gen 46:9).
Father of Eliab (Num 26:8).

people.name: Salmon
people.summary: Son of Nahshon of Judah and father of Boaz. Matthew's genealogy names Rahab of Jericho as the mother of Boaz, making Salmon her husband.
people.catholic: Matthew and Luke include him in the genealogy of Jesus, so he is one of the links through which the promise to Judah ('the scepter will not depart from Judah', Gen 49:10) passes to David and to Christ. His marriage to Rahab (Mt 1:5) brings a Canaanite woman of faith into the Messiah's ancestry.
know: Son of Nahshon (Ruth 4:20).
Father of Boaz by Rahab (Mt 1:5).
Called Salma in 1 Chr 2:11.

people.name: Seleucus IV Philopator
people.summary: King of Asia who at first paid for the Temple sacrifices from his own revenues, then sent his chancellor Heliodorus to seize the Temple treasury. Father of Demetrius I; succeeded by his brother Antiochus IV.
know: Honored the Temple (2 Macc 3:3).
Sent Heliodorus (2 Macc 3:7).
Father of Demetrius I (1 Macc 7:1).

people.name: Seraiah
people.summary: Seraiah, chief priest when Jerusalem fell in 587 BC, was taken by Nebuzaradan to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah and executed. He was the father of Jehozadak, and Ezra traces his ancestry to him.
know: Last high priest of Solomon's Temple
Executed at Riblah
Ancestor of Ezra

people.name: Shelumiel
people.summary: Son of Zurishaddai and leader of the tribe of Simeon in the wilderness. He assisted Moses in the census at Sinai, led Simeon's division on the march, and presented the tribe's offering at the dedication of the altar.
know: Son of Zurishaddai, prince of Simeon (Num 1).
Helped Moses and Aaron take the census.
Brought Simeon's dedication offering for the altar (Num 7:36).

people.name: Shemaiah
