people.summary: Shemaiah the man of God told Rehoboam not to fight the northern tribes, 'for this thing is from me', and the army went home. When Shishak invaded he told Judah's leaders they had forsaken God; they humbled themselves and were spared complete destruction.
know: Prevented civil war after the schism
Called Judah to repentance before Shishak

people.name: Tychicus
people.summary: Tychicus of the province of Asia accompanied Paul toward Jerusalem and later served as his trusted messenger, carrying the letters to the Ephesians and Colossians and news of Paul's imprisonment.
know: 'The beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord' (Eph 6:21).
Bearer of Ephesians and Colossians (Eph 6:21-22; Col 4:7-8).
Sent to Ephesus (2 Tim 4:12).

people.name: Uri
people.summary: Son of Hur of the tribe of Judah and father of Bezalel, the chief craftsman of the tabernacle.
know: Son of Hur, father of Bezalel (Exo 31:2).
Of the tribe of Judah.

people.name: Zebul
people.summary: Ruler of the city of Shechem under Abimelech, who secretly warned him of Gaal's revolt, taunted Gaal, and expelled Gaal's kin from the city.
know: Abimelech's officer over Shechem (Jdg 9:28, 30).
Warned Abimelech of Gaal's plot.

people.name: Abinadab of Kiriath-jearim
people.summary: When the Philistines returned the Ark, it was brought to Abinadab's house on the hill at Kiriath-jearim, where it remained about twenty years until David came to move it.
know: The Ark stayed in his house for decades
Father of Eleazar, Uzzah and Ahio

people.name: Abinadab son of Saul
people.summary: Abinadab, a son of Saul, died with his father on Mount Gilboa.
know: Died at Gilboa

people.name: Abinoam
people.summary: Man of Kedesh in Naphtali, father of Barak.
know: Father of Barak (Jdg 4:6).

people.name: Abishua
people.summary: Abishua is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

people.name: Ahaz
people.summary: Son of Mica in the genealogy of Benjamin, house of Saul (1 Chr 8:35; 9:41; 8:36; 9:42).

people.name: Alphaeus
people.summary: Alphaeus is known only as the father of the apostle James (Mt 10:3; Mk 3:18; Lk 6:15; Acts 1:13).
know: Father of James son of Alphaeus.
Some ancient writers identified him with Clopas (Jn 19:25); this is uncertain.
Scripture does not say whether he is the same as Levi's father (Mk 2:14).

people.name: Amariah son of Azariah
people.summary: Amariah son of Azariah is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6. An Amariah was chief priest 'over all matters of the LORD' under Jehoshaphat (2 Chr 19:11).
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

people.name: Annas
people.summary: Annas had been high priest (AD 6-15) and remained the senior power in the priestly family; five of his sons and his son-in-law Caiaphas held the office after him. After his arrest Jesus was led first to Annas, who questioned him about his disciples and teaching before sending him bound to Caiaphas.
people.catholic: Luke's phrase 'the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas' (Lk 3:2) reflects Annas's continuing authority. With Caiaphas he later confronted the apostles in Acts 4.
know: Father-in-law of Caiaphas (Jn 18:13).
Questioned Jesus first after his arrest (Jn 18:19-24).
Named with Caiaphas in Luke 3:2 and Acts 4:6.

people.name: Arba
people.summary: Great man among the Anakim, father of Anak, after whom Kiriath Arba (Hebron) was named.
know: Kiriath Arba (Hebron) named after him (Jos 14:15; 15:13).
Father of Anak.

people.name: Arioch
people.summary: Arioch was sent to execute Babylon's wise men when none could tell Nebuchadnezzar his dream; Daniel's tactful question gained time, and Arioch brought Daniel before the king.
know: Not the King Arioch of Genesis 14.

people.name: Arphaxad
people.summary: The king of the Medes at Ecbatana defeated and killed by Nebuchadnezzar at the opening of the book of Judith.
know: Not Arphaxad son of Shem.
Killed in the mountains of Ragau (Jdt 1:15).

people.name: Azel
people.summary: Son of Eleasah in the genealogy of Benjamin, house of Saul (1 Chr 8:37-38; 9:43-44).

people.name: Baal Hanan
people.summary: Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned as king of Edom after Shaul (Gen 36:38; 1 Chr 1:49).

people.name: Baanah son of Rimmon
people.summary: Baanah, Rechab's brother, shared in the murder of Ishbosheth and was executed by David.
know: Murdered Ishbosheth with Rechab

people.name: Becher
people.summary: A son of Benjamin who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)

people.name: Bela son of Beor
people.summary: Bela son of Beor reigned in Edom from the city of Dinhabah, the first of the kings of Edom 'before any king reigned over the children of Israel' (Gen 36:32; 1 Chr 1:43).

people.name: Ben-hadad I
people.summary: Ben-hadad son of Tabrimmon son of Hezion, king of Syria at Damascus, broke his treaty with Baasha of Israel when Asa of Judah bribed him with Temple treasure, and ravaged northern Israel.
know: Hired by Asa against Baasha

people.name: Carmi (son of Reuben)
people.summary: A son of Reuben who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)
Not Carmi of Judah, father of Achan

people.name: Chimham
people.summary: Chimham, presumably Barzillai's son, went with David to Jerusalem in his father's place.
know: A place near Bethlehem later bore his name

people.name: Dishan
people.summary: Son of Seir the Horite in the genealogy of Seir the Horite (Gen 36:21; 36:28; 1 Chr 1:38; 1:42).

people.name: Dishon
people.summary: Son of Seir the Horite in the genealogy of Seir the Horite (Gen 36:21; 36:26; 1 Chr 1:38; 1:41).

people.name: Eglon
people.summary: King of Moab who, allied with Ammon and Amalek, took Jericho (the city of palms) and ruled Israel eighteen years, until Ehud assassinated him.
know: Ruled Israel eighteen years (Jdg 3:14).
Described as very fat (Jdg 3:17).
Killed by Ehud.

people.name: Elah
people.summary: Elah son of Baasha reigned two years; while getting drunk at Tirzah he was murdered by his chariot commander Zimri, who destroyed Baasha's house.
know: Killed while drunk

people.name: Eliezer
people.summary: Second son of Moses and Zipporah. Moses named him Eliezer ('my God is help'), saying that the God of his father had delivered him from Pharaoh's sword.
know: Second son of Moses (Exo 18:4).
Name means 'my God is help'.
Father of Rehabiah (1 Chr 23:17).

people.name: Eliphelet
people.summary: Eliphelet was the last-named son of David born in Jerusalem.
know: Born in Jerusalem

people.name: Elishama
people.summary: Elishama was a son of David born in Jerusalem.
know: Born in Jerusalem

people.name: Ezer
people.summary: Son of Seir the Horite in the genealogy of Seir the Horite (Gen 36:21; 36:27; 1 Chr 1:38; 1:42).

people.name: Gabriel
people.summary: Gabriel is the angel who explains Daniel's vision of the ram and the goat and later brings him the prophecy of the seventy weeks. In the New Testament he announces the birth of John the Baptist to Zechariah and the conception of Jesus to the Virgin Mary.
people.catholic: St Gabriel is venerated as the archangel of the Annunciation; his greeting 'Hail, full of grace' (Lk 1:28) begins the Hail Mary and the Angelus. The Church celebrates him with Sts Michael and Raphael on September 29 and remembers these angels in the liturgy (CCC 335). Daniel's seventy weeks, which Gabriel brings 'to anoint the most holy', were read by the Fathers as pointing to the time of the Messiah.
know: Name means 'God is my strength' (traditional).
Appears to Daniel twice (Dan 8:16; 9:21).
'I am Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God' (Lk 1:19).
Announced the Incarnation to Mary (Lk 1:26-38).

people.name: Gemariah son of Shaphan
people.summary: In Gemariah's chamber in the Temple Baruch read Jeremiah's scroll to the people; Gemariah later urged King Jehoiakim not to burn it.
know: Son of Shaphan the scribe; brother of Ahikam.
Father of Micaiah, who reported the scroll to the princes.

people.name: Gera (son of Benjamin)
people.summary: A son of Benjamin who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)

people.name: Geshem the Arabian
people.summary: An Arabian leader who joined Sanballat and Tobiah in mocking Nehemiah and spreading the rumor that he planned to rebel and make himself king.
know: Also called Gashmu (Neh 6:6).

people.name: Gomer
people.summary: A son of Japheth listed in the Table of Nations as ancestor of a people.
know: Father of Ashkenaz, Riphath and Togarmah; not Gomer the wife of Hosea

people.name: Hadad son of Bedad
people.summary: Hadad son of Bedad, king of Edom from Avith, defeated Midian in the field of Moab (Gen 36:35; 1 Chr 1:46).

people.name: Hanamel
people.summary: Hanamel, Jeremiah's cousin, came to him in the court of the guard during the Babylonian siege and sold him the family field at Anathoth for seventeen shekels — a sign that houses and fields would again be bought in the land.
know: Jeremiah's 'uncle's son'.
The purchase was a prophetic act of hope (Jer 32:15).
The deed was given to Baruch in clay jars.

people.name: Hanoch (son of Reuben)
people.summary: A son of Reuben who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)

people.name: Heber (son of Beriah)
people.summary: A son of Beriah who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)
Great-grandson of Jacob
Not Heber the Kenite (Jdg 4)

people.name: Heber the Kenite
people.summary: Kenite descended from Hobab, Moses' brother-in-law, who had separated from his clan and camped near Kedesh; he was at peace with Jabin. Sisera fled to the tent of his wife Jael.
know: Descendant of Hobab (Jdg 4:11).
At peace with Jabin of Hazor (Jdg 4:17).
Husband of Jael.

people.name: Hebron
people.summary: Son of Kohath and brother of Amram; ancestor of the Hebronite clan of Levites.
know: Son of Kohath (Exo 6:18).
Not to be confused with the city of Hebron.

people.name: Hoglah
people.summary: Hoglah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who stood before Moses, Eleazar and the leaders at the Tent of Meeting and asked for their father's inheritance. The LORD declared their request right, and they later received their portion in Manasseh under Joshua, marrying within their tribe.
people.catholic: The daughters of Zelophehad are often cited in Catholic reflection on the dignity of women in Scripture: their petition is upheld by God himself, and the law is developed to do them justice (Num 27:7).
know: One of Zelophehad's five daughters (Num 26:33).
Petitioned Moses for an inheritance (Num 27:1-4).
God said, 'The daughters of Zelophehad speak right' (Num 27:7).
Married cousins within Manasseh (Num 36:10-12).

people.name: Husham
people.summary: Husham of the land of the Temanites succeeded Jobab as king of Edom (Gen 36:34; 1 Chr 1:45).

people.name: Iddo
people.summary: Iddo was the grandfather of the prophet Zechariah, who is sometimes called simply 'son of Iddo'. A priestly family of Iddo returned with Zerubbabel (Neh 12:4, 16).
know: Not the seer Iddo of Chronicles.
Probably the priest Iddo who returned from exile (Neh 12:4).

people.name: Jalam
people.role: Son of Esau; chief of Edom
people.summary: A son of Esau by Oholibamah, born in Canaan, and a chief of Edom.
know: Son of Esau and Oholibamah (Gen 36:5)

people.name: Jamin (son of Simeon)
people.summary: A son of Simeon who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)

people.name: Javan
people.summary: A son of Japheth listed in the Table of Nations as ancestor of a people.
know: Associated with the Greeks (Ionians)

people.name: Jeush
people.role: Son of Esau; chief of Edom
people.summary: A son of Esau by Oholibamah, born in Canaan, and a chief of Edom.
know: Son of Esau and Oholibamah (Gen 36:5)

people.name: Jezreel
people.summary: Jezreel, Hosea and Gomer's first son, was named for the valley where Jehu shed royal blood, announcing God's judgment on Jehu's dynasty; later the name ('God sows') becomes a promise of restoration.
know: 'She bore him a son' (Hos 1:3).
Name means 'God sows'.
'Great will be the day of Jezreel' (Hos 1:11).

people.name: Joakim the high priest
people.summary: The high priest in Jerusalem in the book of Judith, who organized the defense of the mountain passes, led the people in fasting and prayer, and came with the elders to bless Judith after her victory.
know: Not King Jehoiakim (also called Joakim in Bar 1:3).
Ordered Bethulia to hold the passes (Jdt 4:6-7).
Led penitential prayer in the Temple (Jdt 4:14-15).
Blessed Judith (Jdt 15:8-10).

people.name: Jobab
people.summary: Jobab son of Zerah of Bozrah succeeded Bela as king of Edom (Gen 36:33; 1 Chr 1:44).

people.name: John Gaddis
people.summary: The eldest of Mattathias' five sons, surnamed Gaddis. He was seized and killed by the 'children of Jambri' while leading the family's baggage to the Nabataeans, and his brothers Jonathan and Simon avenged him.
know: Surnamed Gaddis (1 Macc 2:2).
Killed by the sons of Jambri near Medaba (1 Macc 9:35-38).
Possibly the 'Joseph' of 2 Macc 8:22 (a disputed reading).

people.name: Joiada son of Eliashib
people.summary: Son of the high priest Eliashib and next in the high-priestly line; one of his sons married a daughter of Sanballat and was driven away by Nehemiah.
know: Son of Eliashib, father of Jonathan/Johanan.
His son became Sanballat's son-in-law (Neh 13:28).

people.name: Jonadab
people.summary: Jonadab son of Shimeah, a 'very subtle man', advised his cousin Amnon how to trap Tamar, and later told David that only Amnon had been killed by Absalom.
know: Plotted with Amnon against Tamar

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: Joseph, son of Mattathias, appears only in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, which runs from Joseph back through David's son Nathan to Adam; he is listed as the father of Jannai (Lk 3:24).
know: Named only in Luke's genealogy (Lk 3:24).
Son of Mattathias; father of Jannai.

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: Joseph, son of Judah, appears only in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, which runs from Joseph back through David's son Nathan to Adam; he is listed as the father of Semein (Lk 3:26).
know: Named only in Luke's genealogy (Lk 3:26).
Son of Judah; father of Semein.

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: Joseph, son of Jonan, appears only in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, which runs from Joseph back through David's son Nathan to Adam; he is listed as the father of Judah (Lk 3:30).
know: Named only in Luke's genealogy (Lk 3:30).
Son of Jonan; father of Judah.

people.name: Jotham (son of Gideon)
people.summary: Youngest son of Gideon, the only one to escape Abimelech's massacre. From Mount Gerizim he told the people of Shechem the fable of the trees who sought a king and ended with the bramble, cursing Shechem and Abimelech; then he fled to Beer.
people.catholic: Jotham's fable (Jdg 9:7-15), the oldest fable in Scripture, is a classic critique of power seized by the unworthy; the curse he pronounced is said to have come upon both Abimelech and Shechem (Jdg 9:57).
know: Youngest son of Gideon; hid and survived (Jdg 9:5).
Told the fable of the trees from Gerizim (Jdg 9:7-15).
His curse was fulfilled (Jdg 9:57).

people.name: Keturah
people.summary: A wife whom Abraham took (called a concubine in 1 Chr 1:32), who bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak and Shuah. Abraham gave her sons gifts and sent them east, away from Isaac.
know: Mother of six sons of Abraham (Gen 25:2)
Ancestress of Midian, the people of Jethro
Called a concubine in 1 Chr 1:32

people.name: Lamech (son of Methushael)
people.summary: A descendant of Cain who took two wives, Adah and Zillah, and boasted to them in a song of vengeance that he had killed a man for wounding him, claiming to be avenged 'seventy-seven times'.
people.catholic: Lamech's song shows sin escalating after the Fall: vengeance multiplied seventy-seven times. Many commentators note that Jesus reverses it when he tells Peter to forgive 'seventy times seven' (Mt 18:22).
know: First man recorded with two wives (Gen 4:19)
Boasted of being avenged seventy-seven times (Gen 4:24)
Not the same as Lamech father of Noah

people.name: Lazarus (the beggar in the parable)
people.summary: In Jesus' parable of the rich man and Lazarus, a poor man covered with sores lay at a rich man's gate; at death he was carried by angels to Abraham's bosom while the rich man suffered torment. Abraham told the rich man that those who will not hear Moses and the prophets would not be persuaded even if someone rose from the dead.
people.catholic: Lazarus is the only named character in any of Jesus' parables. The Church cites the parable for the 'bosom of Abraham' where the just awaited Christ (CCC 633), for the immediate judgment after death, and as a summons to recognize Christ in the poor (CCC 2463).
know: The only named character in a parable of Jesus.
Carried to 'Abraham's bosom' (Lk 16:22).
Distinct from Lazarus of Bethany.

people.name: Lotan
people.summary: Son of Seir the Horite in the genealogy of Seir the Horite (Gen 36:20; 36:22; 1 Chr 1:38-39).

people.name: Lysimachus
people.summary: Menelaus' brother and deputy, who committed sacrileges in Jerusalem and was killed by the outraged people near the treasury.
know: Killed by a crowd in Jerusalem (2 Macc 4:39-42).

people.name: Mahlah
people.summary: Mahlah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who stood before Moses, Eleazar and the leaders at the Tent of Meeting and asked for their father's inheritance. The LORD declared their request right, and they later received their portion in Manasseh under Joshua, marrying within their tribe.
people.catholic: The daughters of Zelophehad are often cited in Catholic reflection on the dignity of women in Scripture: their petition is upheld by God himself, and the law is developed to do them justice (Num 27:7).
know: One of Zelophehad's five daughters (Num 26:33).
Petitioned Moses for an inheritance (Num 27:1-4).
God said, 'The daughters of Zelophehad speak right' (Num 27:7).
Married cousins within Manasseh (Num 36:10-12).

people.name: Mahlon
people.summary: Elder son of Elimelech and Naomi, who married Ruth in Moab and died there childless; Boaz acquired Ruth 'to raise up the name of the dead' on his inheritance.
know: Son of Elimelech and Naomi (Ruth 1:2).
First husband of Ruth (Ruth 4:10).
Died in Moab.

people.name: Mattaniah
people.summary: Mattaniah son of Mica, of the sons of Asaph, led the thanksgiving in prayer among the Levites of post-exilic Jerusalem (1 Chr 9:15; Neh 11:17; 12:8).

people.name: Merab
people.summary: Merab, Saul's elder daughter, was promised to David but given instead to Adriel the Meholathite; her five sons were later handed to the Gibeonites.
know: Promised to David, married to Adriel

people.name: Meraioth
people.summary: Meraioth is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

people.name: Meshelemiah
people.summary: Meshelemiah son of Kore was a Korahite gatekeeper in David's time, father of Zechariah, keeper of the door of the Tent of Meeting (1 Chr 9:21; 26:1-2).

people.name: Milcah
people.summary: Milcah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who stood before Moses, Eleazar and the leaders at the Tent of Meeting and asked for their father's inheritance. The LORD declared their request right, and they later received their portion in Manasseh under Joshua, marrying within their tribe.
people.catholic: The daughters of Zelophehad are often cited in Catholic reflection on the dignity of women in Scripture: their petition is upheld by God himself, and the law is developed to do them justice (Num 27:7).
know: One of Zelophehad's five daughters (Num 26:33).
Petitioned Moses for an inheritance (Num 27:1-4).
God said, 'The daughters of Zelophehad speak right' (Num 27:7).
Married cousins within Manasseh (Num 36:10-12).

people.name: Mizraim
people.summary: A son of Ham; 'Mizraim' is the Hebrew name for Egypt, whose peoples are traced to him.
know: Mizraim is the Hebrew word for Egypt
Ancestor of the Ludim, Casluhim and others; the Philistines came from the Casluhim (Gen 10:14)

people.name: Moza
people.summary: Son of Zimri in the genealogy of Benjamin, house of Saul (1 Chr 8:36-37; 9:42-43).

people.name: Naaman (son of Benjamin)
people.summary: A son of Benjamin who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)
Not Naaman the Syrian (2 Kgs 5)

people.name: Nadab
people.summary: Nadab son of Jeroboam reigned two years and was assassinated by Baasha while besieging Gibbethon; Baasha then exterminated Jeroboam's house as Ahijah had prophesied.
know: Reigned two years
Killed by Baasha

people.name: Nebaioth
people.summary: A son of Ishmael and ancestor of an Arabian tribe.
know: One of the twelve princes descended from Ishmael (Gen 25:16)
Ishmael's firstborn; brother of Esau's wife Basemath/Mahalath (Gen 28:9; 36:3)

people.name: Nimrod
people.summary: A son of Cush who 'began to be a mighty one in the earth' and 'a mighty hunter before the LORD'. His kingdom began in Babel, Erech, Accad and Calneh in Shinar, and he built Nineveh in Assyria.
people.catholic: Later Jewish and Christian tradition linked Nimrod with the building of the tower of Babel, but Genesis itself does not say this.
know: 'A mighty hunter before the LORD' (Gen 10:9)
His kingdom began in Babel in Shinar (Gen 10:10)
Assyria is called 'the land of Nimrod' (Mic 5:6)

people.name: Noah
people.summary: Noah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who stood before Moses, Eleazar and the leaders at the Tent of Meeting and asked for their father's inheritance. The LORD declared their request right, and they later received their portion in Manasseh under Joshua, marrying within their tribe.
people.catholic: The daughters of Zelophehad are often cited in Catholic reflection on the dignity of women in Scripture: their petition is upheld by God himself, and the law is developed to do them justice (Num 27:7).
know: One of Zelophehad's five daughters (Num 26:33).
Petitioned Moses for an inheritance (Num 27:1-4).
God said, 'The daughters of Zelophehad speak right' (Num 27:7).
Married cousins within Manasseh (Num 36:10-12).

people.name: Numenius son of Antiochus
people.summary: Jonathan's and later Simon's envoy to Rome and Sparta, who brought Rome a great gold shield and returned with letters guaranteeing Jewish independence.
know: Envoy under both Jonathan and Simon.

people.name: Onias the high priest (of Arius' letter)
people.summary: An earlier high priest named Onias (probably Onias I, c. 300 BC) who received Arius' letter of friendship from Sparta.
know: Distinct from Onias III of 2 Maccabees.

people.name: Oreb
people.summary: One of the two princes of Midian during Gideon's war, captured and killed by the Ephraimites at the rock of Oreb; his head was brought to Gideon.
know: Prince of Midian (Jdg 7:25).
Remembered in Ps 83:11 among God's defeated enemies.

people.name: Pashhur son of Immer
people.role: Priest, chief officer of the Temple
people.summary: Pashhur, the priest in charge of the Temple, had Jeremiah beaten and put in the stocks at the Benjamin gate. Released the next day, Jeremiah renamed him 'Magor-missabib' ('terror on every side') and foretold he would die in captivity in Babylon.
know: First recorded persecutor of Jeremiah (Jer 20:1-6).
Renamed 'Magormissabib' by Jeremiah.
This episode leads into Jeremiah's 'confessions': 'You enticed me, LORD' (Jer 20:7).

people.name: Pharaoh (in Abraham's time)
people.summary: The unnamed king of Egypt who took Sarai into his household when Abram, fearing for his life, said she was his sister. God struck Pharaoh's house with plagues, and he returned Sarai and sent Abram away.
know: Not named in Scripture
God protected Sarai with plagues on his house (Gen 12:17)

people.name: Rechab son of Rimmon
people.summary: Rechab, a captain of Ishbosheth, killed the sleeping king with his brother Baanah and brought his head to David, who had them executed.
know: Murdered Ishbosheth
Executed by David

people.name: Rehum the chancellor
people.summary: Persian official in Samaria who, with Shimshai the scribe, wrote to Artaxerxes accusing Jerusalem of rebellion and then forcibly stopped the work.
know: Wrote the accusing letter of Ezra 4:8-16.
Stopped the rebuilding by force (Ezra 4:23).

people.name: Rizpah
people.summary: Rizpah daughter of Aiah was Saul's concubine. When her two sons were executed by the Gibeonites, she kept vigil over their bodies on a rock from the beginning of harvest until the rains, guarding them from birds and beasts; her devotion moved David to give Saul's house honourable burial.
people.catholic: Rizpah's long vigil over her dead sons is often seen as an icon of a mother's sorrowing fidelity, recalling the Mother standing at the Cross.
know: Abner was accused over her
Mother of Armoni and Mephibosheth
Guarded her sons' bodies for months

people.name: Salome
aliases: mother of the sons of Zebedee
people.role: Disciple; mother of James and John
people.summary: Salome was among the women who followed Jesus from Galilee, watched the crucifixion, and came with spices to anoint his body on Easter morning (Mk 15:40; 16:1). Comparing Mark with Matthew's 'mother of the sons of Zebedee' (Mt 27:56), she is generally identified as the mother of James and John, who asked Jesus that her sons sit at his right and left in his Kingdom.
people.catholic: Her request prompted Jesus' teaching that greatness in the Kingdom means service and drinking his cup (Mt 20:20-28). Some interpreters also identify her with the sister of Jesus' mother at the cross (Jn 19:25), which would make James and John kinsmen of Jesus; this is uncertain. She is honoured among the myrrh-bearing women, first witnesses of the empty tomb.
know: Named only in Mark (Mk 15:40; 16:1).
Generally identified with 'the mother of the sons of Zebedee' (Mt 20:20; 27:56).
Brought spices to the tomb on Easter morning.

relations.type: asked places of honour for her sons from

people.name: Samlah
people.summary: Samlah of Masrekah succeeded Hadad son of Bedad as king of Edom (Gen 36:36; 1 Chr 1:47).

people.name: Shallum
people.summary: Shallum son of Jabesh killed Zechariah and reigned one month in Samaria before Menahem killed him.
know: Reigned one month

people.name: Shaphat
people.summary: Shaphat of Abel Meholah was the father of the prophet Elisha.
know: Elisha left his oxen to follow Elijah

people.name: Shaul (son of Simeon)
people.summary: A son of Simeon who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)
'The son of a Canaanite woman' (Gen 46:10)

people.name: Shaul of Rehoboth
people.summary: Shaul of Rehoboth by the River reigned as king of Edom after Samlah (Gen 36:37; 1 Chr 1:48).

people.name: Sheshbazzar
people.summary: The 'prince of Judah' to whom Cyrus handed over the Temple vessels through the treasurer Mithredath; he brought them back to Jerusalem and laid the foundations of the house of God. Whether he is the same person as Zerubbabel or his predecessor as governor is debated.
know: Received the 5,400 gold and silver vessels (Ezra 1:8-11).
Appointed governor by Cyrus (Ezra 5:14).
Sometimes identified with Zerubbabel.

people.name: Shethar-bozenai
people.summary: Colleague of Tattenai who joined in questioning the Temple rebuilding.
know: Spelled 'Shetharbozenai' in the text.

people.name: Shimshai
people.summary: The scribe who co-wrote the letter against Jerusalem with Rehum.
know: Persian-appointed scribe in Samaria.

people.name: Shobal
people.summary: Son of Seir the Horite in the genealogy of Seir the Horite (Gen 36:20; 36:23; 1 Chr 1:38; 1:40).

people.name: Shobal
people.summary: Son of Hur in the genealogy of Judah, house of Hur (1 Chr 2:50; 2:52; 4:1-2). Called 'the father of Kiriath-jearim'.

people.name: Simon Iscariot
people.summary: Simon Iscariot is named only as the father of Judas the betrayer (Jn 6:71; 13:26).
know: Father of Judas Iscariot.
Named only in John's Gospel.

people.name: Simon Magus
people.summary: Simon practised sorcery in Samaria and was hailed as 'the great power of God'. He believed Philip's preaching and was baptized, but when he saw the Spirit given through the apostles' laying on of hands he offered them money for that power. Peter sharply rebuked him and called him to repent.
people.catholic: His attempt to buy spiritual power gave its name to the sin of simony, the buying or selling of spiritual things (CCC 2121). The episode also shows the gift of the Spirit through the apostles' laying on of hands after Baptism (Acts 8:17-18), read by the Church as a witness to Confirmation. Later legend (not Scripture) makes him the father of Gnostic heresy and an opponent of Peter at Rome.
know: Called 'the great power of God' by the Samaritans.
Baptized by Philip.
Offered money for the power to give the Spirit: origin of the word 'simony'.
Peter told him: 'May your silver perish with you' (Acts 8:20).

relations.type: witnessed the laying on of hands by

people.name: Simon the Zealot
people.summary: Simon, called 'the Zealot', appears in each list of the Twelve (Mt 10:4; Mk 3:18; Lk 6:15; Acts 1:13), distinguished from Simon Peter by his surname.
people.catholic: His surname may point to zeal for the Law or to the nationalist movement; either way, Jesus gathered into one band a former 'zealot' and a former tax collector (Matthew). Tradition holds he preached with Jude in Persia, where both were martyred, so they share a feast.
know: Called 'the Zealot' to distinguish him from Peter.
Nothing else is recorded of him in Scripture.
Feast October 28, with St Jude.

people.name: Tattenai
people.summary: Persian governor of the province 'beyond the River' who, with Shethar-bozenai, questioned the Temple rebuilding and wrote to Darius; when Darius confirmed Cyrus' decree, he complied 'with all diligence'.
know: Wrote to Darius about the Temple work.
Obeyed Darius' order to assist the builders.

people.name: Tirzah
people.summary: Tirzah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who stood before Moses, Eleazar and the leaders at the Tent of Meeting and asked for their father's inheritance. The LORD declared their request right, and they later received their portion in Manasseh under Joshua, marrying within their tribe.
people.catholic: The daughters of Zelophehad are often cited in Catholic reflection on the dignity of women in Scripture: their petition is upheld by God himself, and the law is developed to do them justice (Num 27:7).
know: One of Zelophehad's five daughters (Num 26:33).
Petitioned Moses for an inheritance (Num 27:1-4).
God said, 'The daughters of Zelophehad speak right' (Num 27:7).
Married cousins within Manasseh (Num 36:10-12).

people.name: Tola (son of Issachar)
people.summary: A son of Issachar who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)
Not Tola the judge (Jdg 10:1)

people.name: Uzzi
people.summary: Uzzi is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

people.name: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah
people.summary: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah, leader of Ahab's court prophets, made iron horns to promise victory at Ramoth-gilead and struck Micaiah on the cheek.
know: Made iron horns as a sign
Struck Micaiah

people.name: Zophar the Naamathite
people.summary: The third of Job's friends, the bluntest, who told Job that God was punishing him less than his guilt deserved.
know: Speaks in Job 11 and 20.
Rebuked by God (Job 42:7-9).

people.name: Abigail, sister of David
people.summary: Abigail, sister of David and Zeruiah, was the mother of Amasa by Jether (Ithra); 2 Samuel calls her the daughter of Nahash.
know: Mother of Amasa
Not David's wife Abigail

people.name: Abinadab son of Jesse
people.summary: Abinadab, Jesse's second son, was passed over by Samuel and served in Saul's army against Goliath.
know: Second son of Jesse

people.name: Achbor
people.summary: Achbor is the father of Baal-hanan, king of Edom (Gen 36:38; 1 Chr 1:49); not the Achbor of Josiah's court.

people.name: Adah (wife of Lamech)
people.summary: First wife of Lamech of Cain's line; mother of Jabal and Jubal.
know: Not the same as Adah wife of Esau (Gen 36)

people.name: Adoni-Bezek
people.summary: Canaanite king defeated by Judah and Simeon at Bezek. His captors cut off his thumbs and big toes, and he confessed that God had repaid him for doing the same to seventy kings.
know: Defeated at Bezek (Jdg 1:4-5).
Had mutilated seventy kings (Jdg 1:7).
Died at Jerusalem.

people.name: Ahiman
people.summary: One of the three sons of Anak living at Hebron when the spies came; Caleb (and Judah) later drove them out.
know: Son of Anak at Hebron (Num 13:22).
Driven out by Caleb (Jos 15:14; Jdg 1:10).

people.name: Ahio
people.summary: Ahio, son of Abinadab, walked ahead of the cart carrying the Ark when David first tried to bring it to Jerusalem.
know: Brother of Uzzah

people.name: Ahisamach
people.summary: Danite, father of the craftsman Oholiab.
know: Father of Oholiab (Exo 31:6).
Of the tribe of Dan.

people.name: Alexander the Great
people.summary: Alexander the Macedonian, son of Philip, who conquered the Persian Empire of Darius III and ruled 'to the ends of the earth' for twelve years, then died and left his empire divided among his generals. 1 Maccabees opens with him to explain the origin of the Seleucid kingdom.
people.catholic: The Fathers identified Alexander with the swift he-goat and the 'mighty king' of Daniel's visions (Dan 8:5-8, 21; 11:3-4). His conquests spread the Greek language that became the vehicle of the Septuagint and of the New Testament — a providential preparation for the Gospel.
know: Son of Philip of Macedon (1 Macc 1:1).
Reigned twelve years (1 Macc 1:7).
Divided his kingdom among his servants (1 Macc 1:6-9).
Identified with the he-goat of Daniel 8.

people.name: Amalek
people.summary: Son of Eliphaz by Timna and a chief of Edom; eponymous ancestor of the Amalekites, Israel's persistent enemies in the wilderness.
know: Ancestor of the Amalekites (cf. Ex 17:8-16)
Grandson of Esau (Gen 36:12)

people.name: Amariah son of Meraioth
people.summary: Amariah son of Meraioth is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

people.name: Amaziah, priest of Bethel
people.summary: Amaziah, priest of the royal shrine at Bethel, reported Amos to King Jeroboam II for conspiracy and ordered the prophet back to Judah; Amos answered with a word of judgment against Amaziah's family.
know: Not King Amaziah of Judah.
'Bethel is the king's sanctuary' (Amos 7:13).

people.name: Aminadab (father of Esther)
people.summary: Esther's father, the brother of Mordecai's father; he and his wife died when Esther was young. The Hebrew text calls him Abihail.
know: Uncle of Mordecai.
Not the Amminadab of David's genealogy.

people.name: Ammihud
people.summary: Ammihud son of Ladan, of Ephraim, was the father of Elishama, the tribal leader in the wilderness, and great-grandfather of Joshua (1 Chr 7:26; Num 1:10).

people.name: Anah
people.summary: Son of Seir the Horite in the genealogy of Seir the Horite (Gen 36:20; 36:29; 1 Chr 1:38). Distinct from Anah son of Zibeon (Gen 36:24).

people.name: Ananias
people.summary: Ananias sold a property and, with his wife Sapphira's knowledge, kept back part of the price while presenting the rest to the apostles as if it were the whole. Peter told him he had lied not to men but to the Holy Spirit, and he fell down dead.
people.catholic: The Fathers read the episode as a warning against hypocrisy and sacrilege in the young Church. Peter's words ('you have lied to the Holy Spirit... You haven't lied to men, but to God', Acts 5:3-4) are a classic scriptural witness that the Holy Spirit is God. It also shows Peter exercising authority and discernment over the community.
know: Kept back part of the price of a field while pretending to give all.
Peter said he had lied to the Holy Spirit, i.e. to God.
Fell dead at Peter's word; his wife Sapphira died three hours later.

people.name: Aram
people.summary: A son of Shem, ancestor of the Arameans (Syrians); father of Uz, Hul, Gether and Mash.
know: Ancestor of the Arameans, the people of Laban (Gen 25:20)
Not the same as Aram son of Kemuel (Gen 22:21)

people.name: Arsaces
people.summary: The Parthian king (Mithridates I) who captured Demetrius II when he invaded Media.
know: 'Arsaces' was the dynastic name of the Parthian kings.

people.name: Asaiah
people.summary: Asaiah son of Haggiah, a Merarite Levite, is probably the Asaiah who led the Merarites when David brought the ark to Jerusalem (1 Chr 6:30; 15:6, 11).

people.name: Asenath
people.summary: Egyptian daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, given to Joseph as wife by Pharaoh; she bore Manasseh and Ephraim before the years of famine.
people.catholic: Asenath, an Egyptian woman whose sons became two tribes of Israel, is often noted as one of the Gentile women grafted into God's people. The later Jewish romance 'Joseph and Aseneth' tells of her conversion, but it is not Scripture.
know: Daughter of Potiphera, priest of On (Gen 41:45)
Mother of Manasseh and Ephraim (Gen 41:50-52)
Her sons became heads of two tribes

people.name: Ashbel
people.summary: A son of Benjamin who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)

people.name: Asriel
people.summary: Son of Manasseh and Manasseh's Aramean concubine in the genealogy of Manasseh (1 Chr 7:14; Num 26:31; Josh 17:2). Num 26:31 counts him among the sons of Gilead.

people.name: Azarias (commander)
people.summary: Joseph son of Zacharias' co-commander in Judea, defeated with him at Jamnia after disobeying Judas' orders.
know: Not the angel Raphael's alias 'Azarias' in Tobit.

people.name: Ben-hadad son of Hazael
people.summary: Ben-hadad son of Hazael lost three battles and the captured towns to Jehoash of Israel, as Elisha's arrows had foretold.
know: Defeated three times by Jehoash

people.name: Bernice
people.summary: Bernice was the sister of King Agrippa II and accompanied him with great pomp when Paul made his defense before Festus at Caesarea.
know: Daughter of Herod Agrippa I and sister of Agrippa II (per Josephus).
Present at Paul's hearing (Acts 25:23; 26:30).

people.name: Bukki
people.summary: Bukki is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

people.name: Carmi
people.summary: Judahite, son of Zabdi and father of Achan.
know: Father of Achan (Jos 7:1).
Not Carmi the son of Reuben.

people.name: Chabris
people.summary: Chabris son of Gothoniel, one of the three rulers of Bethulia.
know: Summoned by Judith with Ozias and Charmis (Jdt 8:10).

people.name: Charmis
people.summary: Charmis son of Melchiel, one of the three rulers of Bethulia.
know: Watched Judith leave the city (Jdt 10:6).

people.name: Chilion
people.summary: Younger son of Elimelech and Naomi, who married the Moabite Orpah and died in Moab.
know: Son of Elimelech and Naomi (Ruth 1:2).
Husband of Orpah.
Died in Moab.

people.name: Debir
people.summary: King of Eglon, one of the five Amorite kings who joined Adoni-Zedek against Gibeon and were defeated by Joshua and executed at Makkedah.
know: King of Eglon (Jos 10:3).
Member of the five-king coalition.
Executed at Makkedah (Jos 10:26).

people.name: Demas
people.summary: Demas is listed as Paul's fellow worker in Colossians and Philemon, but in 2 Timothy Paul laments that 'Demas left me, having loved this present world'.
people.catholic: Demas is a sobering example of perseverance lost: the love of 'this present world' drawing a disciple away from the mission.
know: A fellow worker of Paul (Philem 24).
Deserted Paul for Thessalonica (2 Tim 4:10).

people.name: Dositheus
people.summary: With Sosipater, a captain of Judas Maccabeus who destroyed Timotheus' garrison and captured Timotheus but let him go. (A different Dositheus, a horseman of Bacenor's company, grappled with Gorgias, 2 Macc 12:35.)
know: Captured and released Timotheus (2 Macc 12:24-25).

people.name: Eleazar Avaran
people.summary: The fourth son of Mattathias, surnamed Avaran. At the battle of Beth-zechariah he ran beneath the tallest royal war elephant, thinking the king rode on it, stabbed it from beneath and was crushed when it fell — giving his life 'to get himself an everlasting name'.
know: Surnamed Avaran (1 Macc 2:5).
Killed beneath an elephant (1 Macc 6:43-46).
The 'Eleazer' who read the sacred book before battle (2 Macc 8:23) is likely he.

people.name: Eliada
people.summary: Eliada (Beeliada in 1 Chr 14:7) was a son of David born in Jerusalem.
know: Also called Beeliada

people.name: Eliam
people.summary: Eliam (Ammiel in Chronicles) was Bathsheba's father; an Eliam son of Ahithophel is listed among David's mighty men, and many interpreters identify the two.
know: Called Ammiel in 1 Chr 3:5
Possibly Ahithophel's son, which would make Ahithophel Bathsheba's grandfather

people.name: Eliel
people.summary: Son of Toah in the genealogy of Levi, among the Kohathites (1 Chr 6:27; 6:34; 1 Sam 1:1). In the ancestry of Samuel and Heman the singer.

people.name: Elishama the scribe
people.summary: Elishama was the royal scribe in whose chamber the princes met and where Jeremiah's scroll was kept before it was read to Jehoiakim.

people.name: Elkanah
people.summary: Son of Joel in the genealogy of Levi, among the Kohathites (1 Chr 6:25; 6:35-36). In the ancestry of Samuel and Heman the singer.

people.name: Elnathan son of Achbor
people.summary: Elnathan was sent by Jehoiakim to bring the prophet Uriah back from Egypt; later he was among the princes who begged the king not to burn Jeremiah's scroll.
know: Both an agent of Jehoiakim and an intercessor for Jeremiah's scroll.

people.name: Elpaal
people.summary: Son of Shaharaim and Hushim in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:11-12; 8:18).

people.name: Epaphras
people.role: Founder of the church at Colossae
people.summary: Epaphras, a Colossian, taught the Colossians the gospel and laboured for the churches of Laodicea and Hierapolis. He was with Paul as a 'fellow prisoner', always wrestling in prayer for his people.
people.catholic: He is a model of the pastor who intercedes constantly for his flock (Col 4:12-13).
know: The Colossians learned the gospel from him (Col 1:7).
Paul's fellow prisoner (Philem 23).
Prayed earnestly for Colossae, Laodicea and Hierapolis (Col 4:12-13).

people.name: Ephrath
people.role: Wife of Caleb son of Hezron
people.summary: Ephrath (Ephrathah) married Caleb son of Hezron after Azubah's death and bore Hur, the grandfather of Bezalel and ancestor of the Bethlehem clans (1 Chr 2:19, 50; 4:4).

people.name: Erastus
people.summary: Erastus was sent with Timothy into Macedonia while Paul stayed in Asia. An Erastus, 'the treasurer of the city', sends greetings from Corinth in Romans, and 2 Timothy notes that Erastus remained at Corinth.
know: Sent with Timothy to Macedonia (Acts 19:22).
The city treasurer of Rom 16:23 and the Erastus of Acts may or may not be the same man.

people.name: Ezekiel
people.summary: Ezekiel son of Buzi, a priest, was deported to Babylon with King Jehoiachin in 597 BC and was called by the river Chebar in a vision of God's glory on a chariot of living creatures. He announced Jerusalem's fall through dramatic sign-acts, saw God's glory leave the Temple, and after 587 BC proclaimed restoration: a new heart and spirit, the valley of dry bones, the good shepherd and a new Temple from which life-giving water flows.
people.catholic: The Church reads Ezek 36:25-27 (clean water, a new heart, God's Spirit within) as a prophecy of Baptism and the gift of the Spirit (cf. Jn 3:5; CCC 1287), and it is the seventh Old Testament reading of the Easter Vigil; the Easter-season sprinkling antiphon 'Vidi aquam' draws on the water flowing from the Temple (Ezek 47). The dry bones (Ezek 37) prefigure the resurrection, and God's promise to shepherd his flock himself (Ezek 34) is fulfilled in Christ the Good Shepherd (Jn 10). Fathers such as St Ambrose and St Jerome read the shut eastern gate through which only the Lord enters (Ezek 44:2) as a figure of Mary's perpetual virginity, and the four faces of the living creatures (Ezek 1:10) became the symbols of the four Evangelists.
know: A priest in exile, called 'son of man' by God over ninety times.
Ate the scroll of God's word (Ezek 2:8-3:3) and was made Israel's watchman (Ezek 3:17).
His wife's death became a sign he was forbidden to mourn (Ezek 24:15-24).
Visions: God's glory, the dry bones, the new Temple and its river (Ezek 1; 37; 47).

people.name: Gallio
people.summary: Gallio, proconsul of Achaia, refused to judge the case the Jews of Corinth brought against Paul, calling it a dispute about words and names and their own law, and drove them from his judgment seat.
know: Proconsul of Achaia at Corinth (Acts 18:12).
An inscription at Delphi dates his term to about AD 51-52, a fixed point for dating Paul's ministry.
Brother of the philosopher Seneca (historical sources).

people.name: Gatam
people.summary: Son of Eliphaz in the genealogy of Esau (Edom) (Gen 36:11; 36:16; 1 Chr 1:36).

people.name: Guni
people.summary: A son of Naphtali who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)

people.name: Hadar
people.summary: Hadar (Hadad in 1 Chr 1:50) was the last king of Edom in the list, reigning from Pau/Pai; his wife was Mehetabel daughter of Matred (Gen 36:39; 1 Chr 1:50).

people.name: Hamul
people.summary: Son of Perez and brother of Hezron; ancestor of the Hamulite clan.
know: Son of Perez (Gen 46:12)

people.name: Hamutal
people.summary: Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah was a wife of Josiah and mother of two kings, Jehoahaz and Zedekiah.
know: Mother of Jehoahaz and Zedekiah
Her father is not the prophet Jeremiah

people.name: Helkias
people.summary: Helkias was the righteous father of Susanna, who with his wife taught her the law of Moses and praised God when she was vindicated.
know: Greek form of Hilkiah.

people.name: Hosea
people.summary: Hosea son of Beeri prophesied in the northern kingdom in the last decades before its fall (8th century BC). God commanded him to marry Gomer, an unfaithful woman, and to give their children names of judgment — Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah, Lo-ammi — so that his broken marriage became a living parable of Israel's infidelity and of God's unfailing, redeeming love.
people.catholic: Hosea is the great prophet of God's spousal love: the Church teaches that the prophets, seeing God's covenant with Israel in the image of exclusive and faithful married love, prepared the way for the New Covenant in which Christ is Bridegroom of the Church (CCC 1611; Eph 5:25-32). 'Out of Egypt I called my son' (Hos 11:1) is fulfilled in the Holy Family's return (Mt 2:15); Jesus twice quotes 'I desire mercy, not sacrifice' (Hos 6:6; Mt 9:13; 12:7); and 'on the third day he will raise us up' (Hos 6:2) was read by the Fathers in light of the Resurrection. Paul and Peter apply 'Not my people... my people' to the Church gathered from Jews and Gentiles (Rom 9:25-26; 1 Pet 2:10).
know: Son of Beeri, prophet to the northern kingdom under Jeroboam II.
Married Gomer, daughter of Diblaim (Hos 1:3).
His children's names were prophecies: Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah ('not pitied'), Lo-ammi ('not my people').
'I will allure her... into the wilderness, and speak tenderly to her' (Hos 2:14).
First of the Twelve (Minor) Prophets in canonical order.

people.name: Huppim
people.summary: A son of Benjamin who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)

people.name: Hur
people.summary: Leader of Israel who, with Aaron, went up the hill with Moses during the battle against Amalek and held up Moses' hands until sunset, so Israel prevailed. When Moses ascended Sinai he left Aaron and Hur in charge of the people.
people.catholic: The image of Aaron and Hur supporting the arms of Moses at prayer (Exo 17:12) has been used by the Fathers as a figure of the outstretched arms of Christ on the Cross, and more widely of the support the faithful give to the prayer of their shepherds.
know: Held up Moses' hands with Aaron at Rephidim (Exo 17:10-12).
Left in charge with Aaron while Moses was on Sinai (Exo 24:14).
Jewish tradition identifies him with the grandfather of Bezalel, but Scripture does not say so.

people.name: Ibhar
people.summary: Ibhar was a son of David born in Jerusalem.
know: Born in Jerusalem

people.name: Iddo the seer
people.summary: Iddo the seer is cited by Chronicles as an author of visions concerning Jeroboam and of records of Rehoboam and Abijah.
know: A lost prophetic source used by the Chronicler

people.name: Imnah
people.summary: A son of Asher who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)

people.name: Ishvi
people.summary: A son of Asher who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)

people.name: Jachin (son of Simeon)
people.summary: A son of Simeon who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)

people.name: Jair (judge)
people.summary: Gileadite who judged Israel twenty-two years; he had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkeys and ruled thirty towns called Havvoth Jair.
know: Minor judge from Gilead (Jdg 10:3).
Judged twenty-two years.
Thirty sons on thirty donkeys (Jdg 10:4).

people.name: Japhia
people.summary: Japhia was a son of David born in Jerusalem.
know: Born in Jerusalem

people.name: Jediael
people.summary: Son of Benjamin in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:6; 7:10-11).

people.name: Jehudi
people.summary: Jehudi son of Nethaniah fetched Baruch and later read Jeremiah's scroll aloud to King Jehoiakim, who cut off each few columns and threw them into the brazier.
know: Read the scroll to the king column by column (Jer 36:23).

people.name: Jeroham
people.summary: Jeroham son of Eliel (Elihu) was the father of Elkanah and grandfather of the prophet Samuel (1 Sam 1:1; 1 Chr 6:27, 34).

people.name: Jezer
people.summary: A son of Naphtali who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)

people.name: Joiakim
people.summary: Son of Jeshua and his successor as high priest in the generation after the return.
know: Son of Jeshua the high priest.
Father of the high priest Eliashib (Neh 12:10).

people.name: Jokshan
people.summary: A son of Abraham by Keturah, sent away eastward with gifts.
know: Son of Abraham and Keturah (Gen 25:2)
Father of Sheba and Dedan (Gen 25:3)

people.name: Jonathan the scribe
people.summary: Jeremiah was beaten and imprisoned in the dungeon of Jonathan the scribe's house, which had been made a prison; Jeremiah begged Zedekiah not to be sent back there.

people.name: Joseph son of Zacharias
people.summary: Left with Azarias to guard Judea while Judas and his brothers campaigned in Gilead and Galilee; seeking glory against orders, the two attacked Jamnia and were routed by Gorgias with the loss of two thousand men.
people.catholic: 1 Maccabees comments that 'they were not of the family of those men by whose hand deliverance was given to Israel' (1 Macc 5:62) — success depends on God's chosen instruments, not on the desire to 'get a name'.
know: Defeated by Gorgias at Jamnia (1 Macc 5:59-60).

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Judah, son of Joanan, appears only in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, which runs from Joseph back through David's son Nathan to Adam; he is listed as the father of Joseph (Lk 3:26).
know: Named only in Luke's genealogy (Lk 3:26).
Son of Joanan; father of Joseph.

people.name: Judah
people.summary: Judah, son of Joseph, appears only in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, which runs from Joseph back through David's son Nathan to Adam; he is listed as the father of Simeon (Lk 3:30).
know: Named only in Luke's genealogy (Lk 3:30).
Son of Joseph; father of Simeon.

people.name: Judas Barsabbas
people.summary: Judas called Barsabbas was one of the 'chief men among the brothers' chosen by the apostles and elders, with Silas, to carry the decision of the Council of Jerusalem to Antioch. Being a prophet, he encouraged and strengthened the brothers there.
people.catholic: He was one of the bearers of the apostolic letter of Acts 15, which spoke with the authority of 'the Holy Spirit and us' (Acts 15:28), an early witness to the Church's teaching authority.
know: Chosen with Silas to carry the Council's letter to Antioch.
A prophet who strengthened the church (Acts 15:32).

people.name: Judas son of Simon
people.summary: Simon's son, who was wounded fighting Cendebaeus and later murdered with his father at Dok.
know: Wounded in battle (1 Macc 16:9).
Killed by Ptolemy son of Abubus (1 Macc 16:14-16).

people.name: Kenaz
people.summary: Son of Eliphaz in the genealogy of Esau (Edom) (Gen 36:11; 36:15; 1 Chr 1:36).

people.name: Luke
people.summary: Luke, 'the beloved physician', was a companion of Paul who stayed with him to the end ('Only Luke is with me'). The 'we' passages of Acts (from Acts 16:10) suggest that the author travelled with Paul to Philippi, to Jerusalem, and on the voyage to Rome.
people.catholic: The Church honors St Luke as the author of the third Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles; his feast is October 18 and his symbol is the ox. His Gospel gives the Church the infancy narratives and the canticles prayed daily in the Liturgy of the Hours (the Benedictus, Magnificat and Nunc Dimittis), and Acts recounts the birth of the Church at Pentecost. Tradition holds that he painted icons of the Virgin Mary; he is patron of physicians and artists.
know: Called 'the beloved physician' (Col 4:14).
Faithful to Paul in his final imprisonment (2 Tim 4:11).
Traditionally the author of Luke and Acts, both addressed to Theophilus.
Feast October 18.

people.name: Mahseiah
people.summary: Mahseiah was the father of Neriah and grandfather of Baruch and Seraiah.
know: Called 'Maaseas' in Bar 1:1.

people.name: Malchiel
people.summary: A son of Beriah who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)
Great-grandson of Jacob

people.name: Malchijah
people.summary: Malchijah, of a priestly house, was the father of Pashhur (1 Chr 9:12); Jeremiah's opponent Pashhur 'son of Malchijah' is probably of the same family (Jer 21:1; 38:1).

people.name: Meshech
people.summary: A son of Japheth listed in the Table of Nations as ancestor of a people.
know: Associated with a people of Asia Minor

people.name: Mica
people.summary: Son of Zichri in the genealogy of the Levites who resettled Jerusalem (1 Chr 9:15; Neh 11:17; 11:22).

people.name: Mikloth
people.summary: Son of Jeiel and Maacah in the genealogy of Benjamin, house of Saul (1 Chr 8:32; 9:37-38).

people.name: Mizzah
people.summary: Son of Reuel in the genealogy of Esau (Edom) (Gen 36:13; 36:17; 1 Chr 1:37).

people.name: Naamah
people.summary: Naamah the Ammonitess, a wife of Solomon, was the mother of King Rehoboam and is named as queen mother in the regnal formula.
know: An Ammonite princess
Mother of Rehoboam

people.name: Nahath
people.summary: Son of Reuel in the genealogy of Esau (Edom) (Gen 36:13; 36:17; 1 Chr 1:37).

people.name: Nepheg
people.summary: Nepheg was a son of David born in Jerusalem.
know: Born in Jerusalem

people.name: Omar
people.summary: Son of Eliphaz in the genealogy of Esau (Edom) (Gen 36:11; 36:15; 1 Chr 1:36).

people.name: Pekahiah
people.summary: Pekahiah son of Menahem reigned two years before his officer Pekah killed him in the palace at Samaria.
know: Assassinated by Pekah

people.name: Phicol
people.summary: Captain of the army of Abimelech king of Gerar, present at the covenants with Abraham and with Isaac.
know: Witness to the oaths at Beersheba (Gen 21:22, 32; 26:26)

people.name: Philip the Phrygian
people.summary: The governor Antiochus IV left in Jerusalem, 'more barbarous than him who set him there', who burned Jews keeping the Sabbath in caves and called for reinforcements against Judas.
know: Governor of Jerusalem (2 Macc 5:22).
Burned Sabbath-keepers in caves (2 Macc 6:11).

people.name: Potiphar
people.role: Egyptian officer; captain of the guard
people.summary: An officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard who bought Joseph from the Ishmaelites and put him in charge of his house. When his wife falsely accused Joseph of assault, he threw Joseph into the king's prison.
know: Bought Joseph as a slave (Gen 39:1)
His household was blessed for Joseph's sake (Gen 39:5)
Imprisoned Joseph on his wife's false accusation (Gen 39:19-20)
Not to be confused with Potiphera, Joseph's father-in-law

people.name: Potiphera
people.summary: Priest of On (Heliopolis) in Egypt and father of Asenath, whom Pharaoh gave to Joseph as wife.
know: Father-in-law of Joseph (Gen 41:45)
Not the same person as Potiphar

people.name: Ptolemy son of Abubus
people.summary: Simon's son-in-law, governor of the plain of Jericho, who, ambitious to rule the country, murdered Simon and two of his sons at a banquet in the fortress of Dok and tried to kill John Hyrcanus.
know: 'The high priest's son-in-law' (1 Macc 16:12).
Murdered Simon at Dok (1 Macc 16:16).

people.name: Ram
people.summary: Son of Jerahmeel in the genealogy of Judah, among the Jerahmeelites (1 Chr 2:25; 2:27).

people.name: Seir the Horite
people.summary: Seir the Horite is the ancestor of the Horite clans who lived in the land of Edom before Esau's descendants (Gen 36:20-21; 1 Chr 1:38).

people.name: Serah
people.summary: A daughter of Asher who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)
One of the very few granddaughters of Jacob named in Scripture

people.name: Shallum
people.summary: Shallum son of Kore, a Korahite, was chief of the gatekeepers of the house of the LORD among those who resettled Jerusalem (1 Chr 9:17-19).

people.name: Shammah
people.summary: Son of Reuel in the genealogy of Esau (Edom) (Gen 36:13; 36:17; 1 Chr 1:37).

people.name: Shammua
people.summary: Shammua (Shimea), born in Jerusalem, is listed first among Bathsheba's four sons.
know: Called Shimea in 1 Chr 3:5

people.name: Shemaiah the Nehelamite
people.summary: Shemaiah, among the exiles in Babylon, wrote to the priests in Jerusalem demanding that Jeremiah be put in the stocks for advising the exiles to settle down. Jeremiah answered that God had not sent him and that none of his descendants would see the good God would do.
know: A false prophet among the exiles (Jer 29:24-32).

people.name: Shemida
people.summary: Son of Gilead in the genealogy of Manasseh (Num 26:32; Josh 17:2; 1 Chr 7:19).

people.name: Sheshai
people.summary: One of the three sons of Anak living at Hebron when the spies came; Caleb (and Judah) later drove them out.
know: Son of Anak at Hebron (Num 13:22).
Driven out by Caleb (Jos 15:14; Jdg 1:10).

people.name: Sheshan
people.summary: Sheshan son of Ishi, a Jerahmeelite, had only daughters and gave one in marriage to his Egyptian servant Jarha, founding a long line (1 Chr 2:31, 34-35).

people.name: Shimron
people.summary: A son of Issachar who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)

people.name: Shobab
people.summary: Shobab, son of David and Bathsheba, was born in Jerusalem.
know: Born in Jerusalem

people.name: Shua
people.summary: A Canaanite whose daughter Judah married.
know: His daughter bore Er, Onan and Shelah (Gen 38:2-5; 1 Ch 2:3)

people.name: Shuthelah
people.summary: Son of Ephraim in the genealogy of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:20; Num 26:35-36).

people.name: Sidon
people.summary: Firstborn son of Canaan, eponymous ancestor of the Phoenician city of Sidon.
know: The city of Sidon bears his name

people.name: Simon of Cyrene
people.summary: Simon, a man of Cyrene coming in from the country, was compelled by the soldiers to carry Jesus' cross to Golgotha. Mark names him as the father of Alexander and Rufus, evidently known to Mark's readers.
people.catholic: Simon is remembered in the Fifth Station of the Cross. Luke's phrase that he carried the cross 'after Jesus' (Lk 23:26) makes him an image of every disciple who takes up the cross and follows Christ (Lk 9:23).
know: From Cyrene in North Africa (Mt 27:32).
Compelled to carry Jesus' cross (Mk 15:21).
Father of Alexander and Rufus (Mk 15:21).

people.name: Simon the Pharisee
people.summary: Simon, a Pharisee, invited Jesus to dine. When a sinful woman wept at Jesus' feet, wiped them with her hair and anointed them, Simon doubted Jesus was a prophet; Jesus told the parable of the two debtors and declared, 'Her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much'.
people.catholic: The episode teaches the link between forgiveness and love and is a classic text for the sacrament of Penance and for contrition born of love. Western tradition after St Gregory the Great identified the sinful woman with Mary Magdalene, a view the Church no longer assumes.
know: A Pharisee who hosted Jesus (Lk 7:36, 40).
Heard the parable of the two debtors (Lk 7:41-43).
Distinct in the text from Simon the leper of Bethany.

people.name: Simon the tanner
people.summary: Simon was a tanner at Joppa whose house was by the sea. Peter stayed with him many days, and it was on his roof that Peter saw the vision of the sheet of clean and unclean animals before going to Cornelius.
people.catholic: A tanner's trade made him ritually unclean in the eyes of strict Jews; Peter's lodging with him quietly anticipates the vision that opens the Church to the Gentiles.
know: A tanner whose house stood by the sea at Joppa.
Peter received the vision of the sheet on his roof (Acts 10:9-16).

people.name: Stephanas
people.summary: Stephanas and his household were the first converts of Achaia and devoted themselves to serving the saints; Paul baptized them himself. He came to Paul with Fortunatus and Achaicus, and Paul asks the Corinthians to be subject to such workers.
people.catholic: The baptism of his household (1 Cor 1:16) is among the household baptisms cited in the Church's tradition of baptizing whole families.
know: His household was 'the first fruits of Achaia' (1 Cor 16:15).
Baptized by Paul with his household (1 Cor 1:16).
Visited Paul at Ephesus (1 Cor 16:17).

people.name: Tabitha
people.summary: Tabitha, called Dorcas in Greek (both mean 'gazelle'), was a disciple at Joppa full of good works and almsgiving, who made garments for widows. When she died, Peter was summoned; he knelt, prayed, and said 'Tabitha, get up', and she was restored to life.
people.catholic: She is a model of the corporal works of mercy, especially care for widows and the poor. Her raising echoes Jesus' raising of Jairus' daughter ('Talitha, koum') and shows Peter acting with Christ's own power.
know: Also called Dorcas; both names mean 'gazelle'.
Known for clothing the widows of Joppa.
Raised from the dead by Peter.

people.name: Talmai
people.summary: Talmai son of Ammihud, king of Geshur, was David's father-in-law; Absalom took refuge with him for three years after killing Amnon.
know: Grandfather of Absalom

people.name: Talmai
people.summary: One of the three sons of Anak living at Hebron when the spies came; Caleb (and Judah) later drove them out.
know: Son of Anak at Hebron (Num 13:22).
Driven out by Caleb (Jos 15:14; Jdg 1:10).

people.name: Teman
people.summary: Son of Eliphaz in the genealogy of Esau (Edom) (Gen 36:11; 36:15; 1 Chr 1:36).

people.name: Ten sons of Haman
people.summary: Haman's ten sons, named in Greek form (Pharsannes, Delphon, Phasga, Pharadatha, Barea, Sarbaca, Marmasima, Ruphaeus, Arsaeus, Zabuthaeus), killed in Susa when the Jews defended themselves.
know: Group entry.
Named in Est 9:7-9.

people.name: The Shunammite woman
people.summary: A wealthy woman of Shunem persuaded Elisha to eat at her house and, with her husband, built him a small upper room. Elisha promised her a son; years later the boy died in her lap, and she rode to Mount Carmel, clung to Elisha's feet and would not leave him until he came and raised the child. Warned of famine, she lived seven years in Philistia, and the king restored her land.
people.catholic: Her hospitality to the man of God is read on the 13th Sunday in Ordinary Time (Year A) with Jesus' words 'whoever receives a prophet...'. The raising of her son anticipates Jesus raising the widow's son at Nain, near Shunem (Lk 7:11-17), and her faith - 'It is well' - is a model of trust in grief.
know: Built a room for Elisha
Received a son by Elisha's promise
Her son was raised from the dead
Her land was restored by the king

people.name: Toah
people.summary: Son of Zuph in the genealogy of Levi, among the Kohathites (1 Chr 6:26; 6:34; 1 Sam 1:1). In the ancestry of Samuel and Heman the singer.

people.name: Trophimus
people.summary: Trophimus, an Ephesian Gentile, accompanied Paul to Jerusalem. Jews from Asia, having seen him with Paul in the city, supposed Paul had brought him into the Temple, sparking the riot that led to Paul's arrest. Paul later left him sick at Miletus.
know: An Ephesian (Acts 21:29).
Suspicion about him triggered Paul's arrest.
Left sick at Miletus (2 Tim 4:20).

people.name: Uriah son of Shemaiah
people.summary: Uriah of Kiriath-jearim prophesied the same message as Jeremiah. When King Jehoiakim sought to kill him he fled to Egypt, but was brought back by Elnathan and struck down with the sword.
people.catholic: He belongs to the line of prophets slain for God's word whom Jesus laments (Mt 23:37).
know: A faithful prophet martyred by Jehoiakim (Jer 26:20-23).
His fate shows the danger Jeremiah faced.

people.name: Widow of Zarephath
people.summary: During the drought God sent Elijah to a Gentile widow at Zarephath in Sidon who was gathering sticks to bake a last meal for herself and her son. She gave Elijah her little cake first, and her jar of flour and jug of oil did not fail until the rain came. When her son died, Elijah stretched himself on the child three times and the LORD restored his life.
people.catholic: Jesus cites her in his Nazareth sermon (Lk 4:25-26) - Elijah was sent to none of Israel's widows but to her - as a sign that God's mercy reaches the Gentiles; the passage is read on the Monday of the 3rd week of Lent. Her gift from her poverty is paired liturgically with the widow's mite (32nd Sunday, Year B), and the unfailing flour and oil have been read as a figure of the Eucharist. The Catechism notes that Elijah taught her to believe in God's word (CCC 2583).
know: A Gentile widow in Sidon
Fed Elijah with her last flour and oil
Her flour and oil did not run out
Her son was raised by Elijah
Mentioned by Jesus in Luke 4

people.name: Zabdi
people.summary: Judahite of the clan of Zerah, grandfather of Achan.
know: Son of Zerah, father of Carmi (Jos 7:1).

people.name: Zabdiel the Arabian
people.summary: The Arab who beheaded the fugitive Alexander Balas and sent his head to Ptolemy VI.
know: Killed Alexander Balas (1 Macc 11:17).

people.name: Zacchaeus
people.summary: Zacchaeus, a rich chief tax collector of Jericho, was short and climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus. Jesus called him down and stayed at his house; Zacchaeus promised half his goods to the poor and fourfold restitution to any he had defrauded, and Jesus declared, 'Today, salvation has come to this house'.
people.catholic: Zacchaeus is the Church's model of conversion shown in restitution: the Catechism cites his pledge in teaching that justice requires restoring what was unjustly taken (CCC 2412). His story is the Gospel for the Dedication of a Church, as Christ comes to dwell in his house, and ends with the mission statement 'the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost'.
know: Chief tax collector at Jericho (Lk 19:2).
Climbed a sycamore to see Jesus (Lk 19:4).
Promised fourfold restitution (Lk 19:8).
'Today, salvation has come to this house' (Lk 19:9).

people.name: Zadok son of Ahitub (II)
people.summary: Zadok son of Ahitub (II) is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

people.name: Zechariah
people.summary: Zechariah, firstborn of Meshelemiah, was gatekeeper of the door of the Tent of Meeting and 'a wise counselor' (1 Chr 9:21; 26:2, 14).

people.name: Zechariah
people.summary: Zechariah son of Jeroboam II reigned six months before Shallum killed him publicly, ending Jehu's dynasty in the fourth generation as the LORD had promised.
know: Last king of Jehu's dynasty

people.name: Zechariah son of Jehoiada
people.summary: After Jehoiada's death the princes of Judah turned to idols; Jehoiada's son Zechariah, clothed by the Spirit of God, rebuked them, and at King Joash's command he was stoned in the Temple court, crying 'May the LORD look on it and avenge it'.
people.catholic: Jesus speaks of the blood of the righteous 'from Abel to Zechariah', killed between the sanctuary and the altar (Mt 23:35; Lk 11:51) - a reference generally taken to this Zechariah, the last murder recorded in the last book of the Hebrew canon. Matthew calls him 'son of Barachiah', a difficulty discussed since the Fathers. He prefigures the martyrs and Christ, the prophet rejected in the Temple.
know: Spoke by the Spirit of God
Stoned in the Temple court at Joash's command
Cited by Jesus with Abel

people.name: Zedekiah son of Maaseiah
people.summary: Zedekiah son of Maaseiah was a false prophet among the exiles, condemned with Ahab son of Kolaiah to be roasted in the fire by the king of Babylon.
know: Not King Zedekiah of Judah.

people.name: Zeeb
people.summary: One of the two princes of Midian during Gideon's war, captured and killed by the Ephraimites at the winepress of Zeeb; his head was brought to Gideon.
know: Prince of Midian (Jdg 7:25).
Remembered in Ps 83:11 among God's defeated enemies.

people.name: Zepho
people.summary: Son of Eliphaz in the genealogy of Esau (Edom) (Gen 36:11; 36:15; 1 Chr 1:36).

people.name: Zerah
people.summary: Son of Reuel in the genealogy of Esau (Edom) (Gen 36:13; 36:17; 1 Chr 1:37).

people.name: Zerahiah
people.summary: Zerahiah is listed in the high-priestly line of Eleazar son of Aaron in 1 Chronicles 6.
know: Part of the Aaronic line from Eleazar to the Exile

people.name: Zeresh
people.summary: Haman's wife, who advised him to build the gallows for Mordecai, and later warned that he could not prevail against Mordecai if he was a Jew.
know: Suggested the gallows (Est 5:14).
Predicted Haman's fall (Est 6:13).

people.name: Zillah
people.summary: Second wife of Lamech of Cain's line; mother of Tubal Cain and Naamah.
know: Addressed in Lamech's song (Gen 4:23)

people.name: Zipporah
people.summary: Daughter of Jethro (Reuel), priest of Midian, given to Moses as wife after he defended her and her sisters at a well. She bore him Gershom and Eliezer and, on the road back to Egypt, circumcised her son to avert the LORD's threat against Moses.
people.catholic: Zipporah's urgent circumcision of her son (Exo 4:24-26) underlines the seriousness of the covenant sign, which the Church sees fulfilled in Baptism, the 'circumcision of Christ' (Col 2:11-12). As a Midianite woman joined to Moses she is also read as a sign of the nations being drawn into God's people.
know: Daughter of the priest of Midian (Exo 2:16-21).
Mother of Gershom and Eliezer.
Circumcised her son with a flint (Exo 4:25).
Brought back to Moses by Jethro at Sinai (Exo 18:2-6).
Whether the 'Cushite woman' of Num 12:1 is Zipporah or a second wife is debated.

people.name: Zuph
people.summary: Son of Elkanah in the genealogy of Levi, among the Kohathites (1 Chr 6:26; 6:35; 1 Sam 1:1). In the ancestry of Samuel and Heman the singer.

people.name: Zur
people.summary: One of the five kings (princes) of Midian killed by Israel in the war of vengeance for Peor, in which Balaam was also slain; Joshua 13:21 calls them princes of Sihon. His daughter Cozbi was killed with Zimri at Peor.
know: One of the five kings of Midian (Num 31:8).
Killed in Israel's war against Midian.

people.name: Abdon
people.summary: Son of Jeiel and Maacah in the genealogy of Benjamin, house of Saul (1 Chr 8:30; 9:36).

people.name: Abdon
people.summary: Son of Hillel the Pirathonite, who judged Israel eight years; he had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy donkeys, and was buried in Pirathon in Ephraim.
know: Minor judge from Ephraim (Jdg 12:13-15).
Judged eight years.
Forty sons and thirty grandsons.

people.name: Abi
people.summary: Abi (Abijah) daughter of Zechariah was the wife of Ahaz and mother of King Hezekiah.
know: Mother of Hezekiah

people.name: Abida
people.summary: Son of Midian in the genealogy of Abraham's descendants through Keturah (Gen 25:4; 1 Chr 1:33).

people.name: Abiel
people.summary: Abiel, a Benjaminite, was the father of Kish (Saul's father) and of Ner (Abner's father).
know: Grandfather of both Saul and Abner

people.name: Abiezer
people.summary: Son of Hammolecheth in the genealogy of Manasseh (1 Chr 7:18; Josh 17:2). Ancestor of the Abiezrite clan of Gideon (Josh 17:2; Judg 6:11).

people.name: Abimael
people.summary: Son of Joktan in the genealogy of the Table of Nations (Gen 10:28; 1 Chr 1:22).

people.name: Abishur
people.summary: Son of Shammai in the genealogy of Judah, among the Jerahmeelites (1 Chr 2:28-29).

people.name: Abital
people.summary: Abital bore David his fifth son, Shephatiah, at Hebron.
know: Mother of Shephatiah

people.name: Adaiah
people.summary: Adaiah son of Jeroham was a priest who resettled Jerusalem after the exile (1 Chr 9:12); Neh 11:12 lists a longer ancestry back to Pashhur son of Malchijah.

people.name: Adbeel
people.summary: A son of Ishmael and ancestor of an Arabian tribe.
know: One of the twelve princes descended from Ishmael (Gen 25:16)

people.name: Adoni-Zedek
people.summary: Amorite king of Jerusalem who, alarmed at Gibeon's treaty with Israel, formed a coalition of five kings to attack Gibeon. Joshua routed them in the battle when the sun stood still; the kings hid in a cave at Makkedah and were executed.
people.catholic: His name ('my lord is righteousness') echoes that of Melchizedek, earlier king of Salem; Christian writers have contrasted the unjust king of Jerusalem with Christ, the true King of Righteousness.
know: King of Jerusalem (Jos 10:1).
Led the five-king coalition against Gibeon.
Executed at Makkedah (Jos 10:22-27).

people.name: Adrammelech
people.summary: Adrammelech, son of Sennacherib, killed his father with Sharezer and fled to Ararat.
know: Patricide

people.name: Adriel
people.summary: Adriel the Meholathite, son of Barzillai, married Saul's daughter Merab.
know: Not the same Barzillai as David's Gileadite friend

people.name: Aeneas
people.summary: Aeneas of Lydda had been bedridden and paralysed for eight years. Peter said to him, 'Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed', and he rose at once; many in Lydda and Sharon turned to the Lord.
people.catholic: His healing, in the name of Jesus Christ, shows the apostles continuing Christ's works of healing, a sign the Church sees fulfilled in the sacraments of healing.
know: Paralysed for eight years.
Healed by Peter at Lydda in Jesus' name.

people.name: Agabus
people.summary: Agabus was a prophet from Jerusalem who foretold by the Spirit a great famine in the days of Claudius, prompting the Antioch church to send relief to Judea. Years later at Caesarea he bound his own hands and feet with Paul's belt to foretell Paul's arrest in Jerusalem.
people.catholic: Agabus witnesses to the charism of prophecy in the apostolic Church. His first prophecy led to the first recorded collection between churches (Acts 11:29-30), an early sign of communion and charity among local Churches.
know: Predicted a worldwide famine under Claudius (Acts 11:28).
Acted out Paul's coming arrest with Paul's belt (Acts 21:10-11).

relations.type: foretold a famine in the reign of

people.name: Ahab son of Kolaiah
people.summary: Ahab son of Kolaiah prophesied lies in God's name among the exiles in Babylon and committed adultery; Jeremiah foretold that Nebuchadnezzar would roast him in the fire.
know: Not King Ahab of Israel.
His fate became a curse formula among the exiles (Jer 29:22).

people.name: Ahijah
people.summary: Ahijah son of Ahitub, great-grandson of Eli, wore the ephod and was with Saul at Gibeah during the battle of Michmash.
know: Carried the ephod in Saul's camp
Possibly the same person as Ahimelech of Nob

people.name: Ahio
people.summary: Son of Jeiel and Maacah in the genealogy of Benjamin, house of Saul (1 Chr 8:31; 9:37).

people.name: Aiah
people.summary: Son of Zibeon in the genealogy of Seir the Horite (Gen 36:24; 1 Chr 1:40).

people.name: Akan
people.summary: Son of Ezer in the genealogy of Seir the Horite (Gen 36:27; 1 Chr 1:42).

people.name: Alemeth
people.summary: Son of Jehoaddah in the genealogy of Benjamin, house of Saul (1 Chr 8:36; 9:42).

people.name: Almodad
people.summary: Son of Joktan in the genealogy of the Table of Nations (Gen 10:26; 1 Chr 1:20).

people.name: Alvan
people.summary: Son of Shobal in the genealogy of Seir the Horite (Gen 36:23; 1 Chr 1:40).

people.name: Amasai
people.summary: Son of Elkanah in the genealogy of Levi, among the Kohathites (1 Chr 6:25; 6:35). In the ancestry of Samuel and Heman the singer.

people.name: Amittai
people.summary: Amittai is named only as the father of the prophet Jonah.

people.name: Amraphel
people.summary: Amraphel, king of Shinar, was one of the four eastern kings who warred against the cities of the plain and carried off Lot; Abram defeated them.
know: One of the 'four kings against the five' (Gen 14:9)

people.name: Ananias (high priest)
people.summary: Ananias was the high priest who ordered Paul struck on the mouth during his hearing before the council; Paul replied, 'God will strike you, you whitewashed wall!' He then went down to Caesarea with the orator Tertullus to accuse Paul before Felix.
know: Ordered Paul struck on the mouth (Acts 23:2).
Paul apologized on learning he was the high priest, citing Exodus 22:28 (Acts 23:5).
Accused Paul before Felix (Acts 24:1).

people.name: Anath
people.summary: Named as the parent of the judge Shamgar ('son of Anath').
know: Shamgar is called 'son of Anath' (Jdg 3:31).

people.name: Aner
people.summary: An Amorite chief allied with Abram who went with him to rescue Lot and received a share of the spoil.
know: Brother of Mamre and Eshcol (Gen 14:13)

people.name: Apollonius
people.summary: The commander who gathered a Gentile army from Samaria against Israel and was killed by Judas, who took his sword and fought with it all his days. (Several other men named Apollonius appear in 1-2 Maccabees.)
