people.summary: Son of Shaharaim and Hodesh in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:9).

people.name: Mesha
people.summary: Mesha king of Moab, a great sheep-breeder, rebelled against Israel after Ahab's death; besieged by Israel, Judah and Edom, he sacrificed his eldest son on the city wall and the invaders withdrew.
know: Also known from the Moabite Stone (Mesha Stele)

people.name: Meshillemith
people.summary: Son of Immer in the genealogy of the priests who resettled Jerusalem (1 Chr 9:12).

people.name: Meshullam
people.summary: Son of Zerubbabel in the genealogy of the royal line of David (1 Chr 3:19).

people.name: Meshullam
people.summary: Son of Abihail in the genealogy of Gad (1 Chr 5:13-14).

people.name: Meshullam
people.summary: Son of Elpaal in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:17).

people.name: Meshullam
people.summary: Son of Hodaviah in the genealogy of Benjamin, among those who resettled Jerusalem (1 Chr 9:7).

people.name: Meshullam
people.summary: Son of Shephatiah in the genealogy of Benjamin, among those who resettled Jerusalem (1 Chr 9:8).

people.name: Meshullam
people.summary: Son of Meshillemith in the genealogy of the priests who resettled Jerusalem (1 Chr 9:12).

people.name: Meshullemeth
people.summary: Meshullemeth daughter of Haruz of Jotbah was the wife of Manasseh and mother of King Amon.
know: Mother of Amon

people.name: Methushael
people.summary: Son of Mehujael in the line of Cain; father of Lamech.
know: Not to be confused with Methuselah of Seth's line

people.name: Mibsam
people.summary: Son of Shallum in the genealogy of Simeon (1 Chr 4:25).

people.name: Micah
people.summary: Son of Shimei in the genealogy of Reuben (1 Chr 5:5).

people.name: Michael
people.summary: Son of Jeshishai in the genealogy of Gad (1 Chr 5:14).

people.name: Michael
people.summary: Son of Baaseiah in the genealogy of Levi, among the Gershonites (1 Chr 6:40). In the ancestry of Asaph the singer.

people.name: Michael
people.summary: Son of Izrahiah in the genealogy of Issachar (1 Chr 7:3).

people.name: Michael
people.summary: Son of Beriah in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:16).

people.name: Michri
people.summary: Michri is named in the genealogy of Benjamin, among those who resettled Jerusalem (1 Chr 9:8).

people.name: Miriam
people.summary: Miriam is the first-named child of Mered and Bithiah daughter of Pharaoh in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chr 4:17); not Moses' sister.

people.name: Mirmah
people.summary: Son of Shaharaim and Hodesh in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:10).

people.name: Misham
people.summary: Son of Elpaal in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:12).

people.name: Mithredath
people.summary: Cyrus' treasurer who counted out the Temple vessels to Sheshbazzar.
know: Persian royal treasurer.
A different Mithredath wrote against Jerusalem in Ezra 4:7.

people.name: Mnason
people.summary: Mnason of Cyprus, 'an early disciple', hosted Paul and his companions on their way up to Jerusalem.
know: An 'early disciple' from Cyprus (Acts 21:16).

people.name: Moab
people.summary: Son of Lot by his elder daughter, born after the destruction of Sodom; ancestor of the Moabites.
people.catholic: Through the Moabite Ruth, a descendant of Lot's line enters the ancestry of David and of Christ (Mt 1:5).
know: Ancestor of the Moabites (Gen 19:37)
Ruth the Moabitess descends from his people

people.name: Molid
people.summary: Son of Abishur and Abihail in the genealogy of Judah, among the Jerahmeelites (1 Chr 2:29).

people.name: Moza
people.summary: Son of Caleb and Ephah in the genealogy of Judah, among the Calebites (1 Chr 2:46).

people.name: Muppim
people.summary: A son of Benjamin who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)

people.name: Naam
people.summary: Son of Caleb in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chr 4:15).

people.name: Naamah (daughter of Lamech)
people.summary: Daughter of Lamech and Zillah, sister of Tubal Cain.
know: One of the few women named in the early genealogies
Not the same as Naamah the Ammonite, mother of King Rehoboam

people.name: Naaman
people.summary: Son of Bela in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:4).

people.name: Naggai
people.summary: Naggai, son of Maath, appears only in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, which runs from Joseph back through David's son Nathan to Adam; he is listed as the father of Esli (Lk 3:25).
know: Named only in Luke's genealogy (Lk 3:25).
Son of Maath; father of Esli.

people.name: Nahbi
people.summary: Son of Vophsi, the man of Naphtali among the twelve sent by Moses to scout Canaan. With nine others he brought back an 'evil report' that discouraged the people; those ten died by plague before the LORD.
know: Represented Naphtali among the twelve spies (Num 13).
Brought back a discouraging report.
Died by plague (Num 14:36-37).

people.name: Nahum
people.summary: Nahum, son of Esli, appears only in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, which runs from Joseph back through David's son Nathan to Adam; he is listed as the father of Amos (Lk 3:25).
know: Named only in Luke's genealogy (Lk 3:25).
Son of Esli; father of Amos.

people.name: Nahum
people.summary: Nahum the Elkoshite announced the fall of Nineveh, the cruel Assyrian capital, which happened in 612 BC. His poem celebrates God as slow to anger but great in power, a refuge for those who trust him and a judge of oppressors.
people.catholic: Nahum 1:15 ('on the mountains the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace') is echoed in Isaiah 52:7 and applied by St Paul to the preachers of the Gospel (Rom 10:15).
know: From Elkosh (location unknown).
Prophesied the fall of Nineveh (612 BC).
Contrast with Jonah, where Nineveh repents.

people.name: Narcissus
people.summary: Narcissus is named in the greetings of Paul's Letter to the Romans. Paul greets those of his household 'who are in the Lord'.
know: Paul greets those of his household 'who are in the Lord'.

people.name: Nasbas
people.summary: Named in Tob 11:18 as coming with Achiacharus to Tobias' wedding feast, described as 'his brother's son' (a nephew).
know: Appears only in Tob 11:18.

people.name: Nathan
people.summary: Son of Attai in the genealogy of Judah, among the Jerahmeelites (1 Chr 2:36).

people.name: Neariah
people.summary: Son of Ishi in the genealogy of Simeon (1 Chr 4:42-43).

people.name: Nedabiah
people.summary: Nedabiah is listed among the sons of Jehoiachin (Jeconiah) the captive.
know: Born in the Babylonian exile

people.name: Nehushta
people.summary: Nehushta daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem, wife of Jehoiakim, was queen mother of Jehoiachin and went into exile with him to Babylon.
know: Taken to Babylon with her son
Jeremiah addressed 'the king and the queen mother' (Jer 13:18)

people.name: Nereus
people.summary: Nereus is named in the greetings of Paul's Letter to the Romans. Greeted with 'his sister'.
know: Greeted with 'his sister'.

people.name: Neri
people.summary: Neri, son of Melchi, appears only in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, which runs from Joseph back through David's son Nathan to Adam; he is listed as the father of Shealtiel (Lk 3:27).
people.catholic: Luke traces Jesus' ancestry back to Adam, 'the son of God' (Lk 3:38), showing him as Saviour of the whole human race; unlike Matthew, his line descends through David's son Nathan rather than Solomon.
know: Named only in Luke's genealogy (Lk 3:27).
Son of Melchi; father of Shealtiel.
Luke makes him Shealtiel's father, whereas Matthew 1:12 and 1 Chronicles 3:17 give Jechoniah.

relations.type: father of (per Luke 3:27; Matthew 1:12 gives Jechoniah)

people.name: Nethanel son of Jesse
people.summary: Nethanel is listed as Jesse's fourth son.
know: Known only from the genealogy

people.name: Nicanor
people.summary: Nicanor was one of the Seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, chosen by the Jerusalem church to serve at table so the apostles could devote themselves to prayer and the ministry of the word.
people.catholic: The choice of the Seven, on whom the apostles laid hands after prayer (Acts 6:6), is traditionally read as the institution of the diaconate, the first degree of Holy Orders, ordained 'not unto the priesthood but unto the ministry' (CCC 1569-1571).
know: Named among the Seven in Acts 6:5.
Received the laying on of hands from the apostles (Acts 6:6).

people.name: Nicolaus
people.summary: Nicolaus, 'a proselyte of Antioch', was the last named of the Seven chosen to serve the Jerusalem church; as a convert to Judaism from paganism he shows the early Church already drawing in Gentile-born believers.
people.catholic: The choice of the Seven, on whom the apostles laid hands after prayer (Acts 6:6), is traditionally read as the institution of the diaconate, the first degree of Holy Orders, ordained 'not unto the priesthood but unto the ministry' (CCC 1569-1571). Some early writers (e.g. St Irenaeus) connected the Nicolaitans of Revelation 2 with him, but this is uncertain and other Fathers defended his memory.
know: The only one of the Seven whose origin is given: a proselyte of Antioch.
Received the laying on of hands (Acts 6:6).
Any link with the Nicolaitans (Rev 2:6, 2:15) is a later and disputed tradition.

people.name: Nohah
people.summary: Son of Benjamin in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:2).

people.name: Nymphas
people.summary: Nymphas hosted a church in his house in the region of Laodicea; Paul sends greetings to him.
know: A church met in his house (Col 4:15).
Some manuscripts read 'Nympha' and 'her house', a woman.

people.name: Obadiah
people.summary: Son of Izrahiah in the genealogy of Issachar (1 Chr 7:3).

people.name: Obadiah
people.summary: Obadiah is the author of the shortest book of the Old Testament, a single vision against Edom for gloating over and plundering Jerusalem on the day of its fall, ending with the promise that 'the kingdom will be the LORD's'.
people.catholic: Obadiah teaches that God judges pride and cruelty toward a brother nation (Edom descended from Esau, Israel from Jacob) and that the final kingdom belongs to God, fulfilled in the Kingdom Christ inaugurates.
know: Shortest book of the Old Testament (21 verses).
Not the Obadiah of Ahab's household in 1 Kings 18.
Usually dated after Jerusalem's fall in 587 BC.

people.name: Ohel
people.summary: Son of Zerubbabel in the genealogy of the royal line of David (1 Chr 3:20).

people.name: Olympas
people.summary: Olympas is named in the greetings of Paul's Letter to the Romans. Greeted with the saints with him.
know: Greeted with the saints with him.

people.name: Omri
people.summary: Son of Becher in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:8).

people.name: Omri
people.summary: Son of Imri in the genealogy of Judah, among those who resettled Jerusalem (1 Chr 9:4).

people.name: On
people.summary: Reubenite, son of Peleth, named at the start of Korah's rebellion with Dathan and Abiram, though he is not mentioned again.
know: Son of Peleth, of Reuben (Num 16:1).
Named among Korah's allies but not in the judgement scene.

people.name: Oren
people.summary: Son of Jerahmeel in the genealogy of Judah, among the Jerahmeelites (1 Chr 2:25).

people.name: Ozem
people.summary: Son of Jerahmeel in the genealogy of Judah, among the Jerahmeelites (1 Chr 2:25).

people.name: Palti
people.summary: Son of Raphu, the man of Benjamin among the twelve sent by Moses to scout Canaan. With nine others he brought back an 'evil report' that discouraged the people; those ten died by plague before the LORD.
know: Represented Benjamin among the twelve spies (Num 13).
Brought back a discouraging report.
Died by plague (Num 14:36-37).

people.name: Parmenas
people.summary: Parmenas was one of the Seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, chosen by the Jerusalem church to serve at table so the apostles could devote themselves to prayer and the ministry of the word.
people.catholic: The choice of the Seven, on whom the apostles laid hands after prayer (Acts 6:6), is traditionally read as the institution of the diaconate, the first degree of Holy Orders, ordained 'not unto the priesthood but unto the ministry' (CCC 1569-1571).
know: Named among the Seven in Acts 6:5.
Received the laying on of hands from the apostles (Acts 6:6).

people.name: Pasach
people.summary: Son of Japhlet in the genealogy of Asher (1 Chr 7:33).

people.name: Paseah
people.summary: Son of Eshton in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chr 4:12).

people.name: Patrobas
people.summary: Patrobas is named in the greetings of Paul's Letter to the Romans. Greeted with Asyncritus and others.
know: Greeted with Asyncritus and others.

people.name: Pelaiah
people.summary: Son of Elioenai in the genealogy of the royal line of David (1 Chr 3:24).

people.name: Pelatiah
people.summary: Son of Hananiah in the genealogy of the royal line of David (1 Chr 3:21).

people.name: Pelatiah
people.summary: Son of Ishi in the genealogy of Simeon (1 Chr 4:42-43).

people.name: Pelet
people.summary: Son of Jahdai in the genealogy of Judah, among the Calebites (1 Chr 2:47).

people.name: Peleth
people.summary: Son of Jonathan in the genealogy of Judah, among the Jerahmeelites (1 Chr 2:33).

people.name: Penuel
people.summary: Son of Hur in the genealogy of Judah, house of Hur (1 Chr 4:4). Called 'the father of Gedor'.

people.name: Penuel
people.summary: Son of Shashak in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:25).

people.name: Peresh
people.summary: Son of Machir and Maacah in the genealogy of Manasseh (1 Chr 7:16).

people.name: Persis
people.summary: Persis is named in the greetings of Paul's Letter to the Romans. 'The beloved, who labored much in the Lord'.
know: 'The beloved, who labored much in the Lord'.

people.name: Pethuel
people.summary: Pethuel is named only as the father of the prophet Joel.

people.name: Phanuel
people.summary: Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher, is named only as the father of Anna the prophetess (Lk 2:36).
know: Father of Anna (Lk 2:36).
Of the tribe of Asher.

people.name: Philemon
people.summary: Philemon was a beloved fellow worker of Paul, in whose house a church met, and the master of the slave Onesimus. Paul's shortest letter asks him to welcome Onesimus back as a brother in Christ.
people.catholic: Philemon is a model of the house church and of the charity that must reshape relationships between Christians; Paul appeals 'for love's sake' rather than commanding (Philem 8-9). See CCC 2414 on Onesimus.
know: Addressee of the Letter to Philemon.
A church met in his house (Philem 2).
Paul says Philemon owes him 'even your own self' (Philem 19), implying Paul converted him.
Apphia and Archippus are greeted with him; they are often thought to be his wife and son, but the letter does not say so.

people.name: Philetus
people.summary: Philetus, with Hymenaeus, taught that the resurrection was already past, overthrowing the faith of some.
know: Named with Hymenaeus in 2 Tim 2:17.

people.name: Philip the tetrarch
people.summary: Philip, son of Herod the Great and brother of Antipas, was tetrarch of Ituraea and Trachonitis (4 BC - AD 34) in the fifteenth year of Tiberius (Lk 3:1). He rebuilt Paneas as Caesarea Philippi, where Peter would confess Jesus as the Christ.
know: Named in Luke 3:1.
Founder of Caesarea Philippi (Mt 16:13) - historically known from Josephus.
Married Salome, daughter of Herodias (Josephus).
Most scholars distinguish him from Herodias's first husband.

people.name: Philologus
people.summary: Philologus is named in the greetings of Paul's Letter to the Romans. Greeted with Julia; perhaps a married couple.
know: Greeted with Julia; perhaps a married couple.

people.name: Phlegon
people.summary: Phlegon is named in the greetings of Paul's Letter to the Romans. Greeted with Asyncritus and others.
know: Greeted with Asyncritus and others.

people.name: Phoebe
people.role: Minister of the church at Cenchreae
people.summary: Phoebe, 'our sister', was a servant (Greek diakonos) of the church at Cenchreae, the port of Corinth. Paul commends her to the Romans, who are to welcome her and help her, for she had been a patron of many, including Paul; she is generally thought to have carried the Letter to the Romans.
people.catholic: She is honored as a saint. Her title diakonos ('servant, minister') shows that women held recognized ministries of service in the apostolic Church; the precise nature of her role is discussed by scholars, and the Church distinguishes later deaconesses from the ordained diaconate.
know: From Cenchreae near Corinth (Rom 16:1).
Called diakonos, 'servant' or 'minister', of the church.
A 'helper' (patron) of many and of Paul (Rom 16:2).

people.name: Phygelus
people.summary: Phygelus is named among all those in Asia who turned away from Paul during his final imprisonment.
know: Named in 2 Tim 1:15 as one who turned away from Paul.

people.name: Pildash
people.summary: A son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by Milcah.
know: Son of Nahor and Milcah

people.name: Piram
people.summary: King of Jarmuth, one of the five Amorite kings who joined Adoni-Zedek against Gibeon and were defeated by Joshua and executed at Makkedah.
know: King of Jarmuth (Jos 10:3).
Member of the five-king coalition.
Executed at Makkedah (Jos 10:26).

people.name: Pispa
people.summary: Son of Jether in the genealogy of Asher (1 Chr 7:38).

people.name: Prochorus
people.summary: Prochorus was one of the Seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, chosen by the Jerusalem church to serve at table so the apostles could devote themselves to prayer and the ministry of the word.
people.catholic: The choice of the Seven, on whom the apostles laid hands after prayer (Acts 6:6), is traditionally read as the institution of the diaconate, the first degree of Holy Orders, ordained 'not unto the priesthood but unto the ministry' (CCC 1569-1571).
know: Named among the Seven in Acts 6:5.
Received the laying on of hands from the apostles (Acts 6:6).

people.name: Puah
people.summary: The second of the two Hebrew midwives who feared God and refused Pharaoh's order to kill the Hebrew baby boys.
people.catholic: With Shiphrah, Puah is held up as a witness to the dignity of human life and to obeying God rather than an unjust law.
know: Hebrew midwife in Egypt (Exo 1:15).
Defied Pharaoh to save newborn boys.
Not the same as Puah, father of the judge Tola.

people.name: Puah (father of Tola)
people.summary: Man of Issachar, son of Dodo and father of the judge Tola.
know: Father of Tola (Jdg 10:1).
Not the Hebrew midwife Puah.

people.name: Pudens
people.summary: Pudens is one of the Roman Christians who send greetings to Timothy at the close of Paul's last letter.
know: Sends greetings in 2 Tim 4:21.

people.name: Quartus
people.summary: Quartus is named in the greetings of Paul's Letter to the Romans. 'The brother', who sends greetings from Corinth.
know: 'The brother', who sends greetings from Corinth.

people.name: Quirinius
people.summary: Publius Sulpicius Quirinius was governor of Syria; Luke dates the enrollment that brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem as 'the first enrollment made when Quirinius was governor of Syria' (Lk 2:2).
know: Named in Luke 2:2.
The dating is debated, since Josephus records a census under Quirinius in AD 6; proposed solutions include an earlier administrative role or reading 'first' as 'before'.

people.name: Raddai
people.summary: Raddai is listed as Jesse's fifth son.
know: Known only from the genealogy

people.name: Raham
people.summary: Son of Shema in the genealogy of Judah, among the Calebites (1 Chr 2:44). Called 'the father of Jorkeam'.

people.name: Rakem
people.summary: Son of Sheresh in the genealogy of Manasseh (1 Chr 7:16).

people.name: Rapha
people.summary: Son of Benjamin in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:2).

people.name: Razis
people.summary: An elder of Jerusalem called 'Father of the Jews' for his goodwill, whom Nicanor tried to arrest. Rather than fall into the hands of sinners he took his own life in a dramatic manner, calling on the Lord of life to give his body back to him.
people.catholic: The Church does not hold up Razis' suicide as an example — Catholic moral teaching forbids suicide (CCC 2280-2283) — but the passage is a witness to his faith in bodily resurrection (2 Macc 14:46). St Augustine, answering Donatists who cited Razis, denied that his death was an example to imitate.
know: Called 'Father of the Jews' (2 Macc 14:37).
Died rather than be captured by Nicanor (2 Macc 14:37-46).

people.name: Reaiah
people.summary: Son of Micah in the genealogy of Reuben (1 Chr 5:5).

people.name: Regem
people.summary: Son of Jahdai in the genealogy of Judah, among the Calebites (1 Chr 2:47).

people.name: Rephah
people.summary: Son of Beriah in the genealogy of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:25). In the ancestry of Joshua.

people.name: Rephaiah
people.summary: Son of Ishi in the genealogy of Simeon (1 Chr 4:42-43).

people.name: Rephaiah
people.summary: Son of Tola in the genealogy of Issachar (1 Chr 7:2).

people.name: Resheph
people.summary: Son of Rephah in the genealogy of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:25). In the ancestry of Joshua.

people.name: Reuel
people.summary: Son of Ibnijah in the genealogy of Benjamin, among those who resettled Jerusalem (1 Chr 9:8).

people.name: Reumah
people.summary: Concubine of Abraham's brother Nahor, who bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash and Maacah.
know: Mother of four of Nahor's twelve children (Gen 22:24)

people.name: Rezon
people.summary: Rezon son of Eliada fled his master Hadadezer, became a raider chief, took Damascus and was an adversary of Israel all Solomon's days.
know: Founded Aramean power in Damascus

people.name: Rhesa
people.summary: Rhesa, son of Zerubbabel, appears only in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, which runs from Joseph back through David's son Nathan to Adam; he is listed as the father of Joanan (Lk 3:27).
people.catholic: Luke traces Jesus' ancestry back to Adam, 'the son of God' (Lk 3:38), showing him as Saviour of the whole human race; unlike Matthew, his line descends through David's son Nathan rather than Solomon.
know: Named only in Luke's genealogy (Lk 3:27).
Son of Zerubbabel; father of Joanan.
Luke's line leaves Matthew's at Zerubbabel: Matthew continues through Abiud, Luke through Rhesa.

people.name: Rhoda
people.summary: Rhoda was a servant girl in the house of Mary, mother of John Mark. When Peter, freed from prison by an angel, knocked at the gate, she recognized his voice and in her joy ran to tell the others without opening the door.
people.catholic: A vivid detail of the praying Church in Jerusalem, whose prayer for Peter was answered while they still doubted.
know: Recognized Peter's voice at the gate.
Ran in to announce him before opening, and was not believed at first.

people.name: Rinnah
people.summary: Son of Shimon in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chr 4:20).

people.name: Rizia
people.summary: Son of Ulla in the genealogy of Asher (1 Chr 7:39).

people.name: Rohgah
people.summary: Son of Shomer in the genealogy of Asher (1 Chr 7:34).

people.name: Rosh
people.summary: A son of Benjamin who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)

people.name: Rufus, son of Simon of Cyrene
people.summary: Rufus is named, with his brother Alexander, as a son of Simon of Cyrene (Mk 15:21).
know: Son of Simon of Cyrene; brother of Alexander.
Possibly the Rufus 'chosen in the Lord' greeted in Romans 16:13, since Mark is traditionally linked with Rome; this is uncertain.

people.name: Sapphira
people.summary: Wife of Ananias, she conspired with him to keep back part of the price of their land. Questioned by Peter three hours after her husband's death, she repeated the lie and died at once.
people.catholic: Her story pairs with her husband's as a sober lesson on honesty before God and the seriousness of sins against the Holy Spirit in the Church.
know: Wife of Ananias, she shared in his deception.
Peter asked her directly the price of the land; she lied.
She died and was buried beside her husband.

people.name: Saraph
people.summary: Son of Shelah in the genealogy of Judah, house of Shelah (1 Chr 4:22). He and Joash 'had dominion in Moab'.

people.name: Sceva
people.summary: Sceva was a Jewish chief priest whose seven sons, itinerant exorcists, tried to cast out demons 'by Jesus whom Paul preaches'; the evil spirit answered, 'Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who are you?' and overpowered them.
people.catholic: The episode shows that the name of Jesus is not a magic formula; the Church's exorcisms are acts of faith exercised in the Church's authority.
know: Father of seven sons who were itinerant exorcists (Acts 19:14).
The episode led many in Ephesus to burn their magic books (Acts 19:19).

relations.type: his sons invoked the name preached by

people.name: Secundus
people.summary: Secundus of Thessalonica accompanied Paul from Greece toward Jerusalem.
know: A Thessalonian delegate for the collection journey.

people.name: Seled
people.summary: Son of Nadab in the genealogy of Judah, among the Jerahmeelites (1 Chr 2:30). He died without children.

people.name: Semein
people.summary: Semein, son of Joseph, appears only in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, which runs from Joseph back through David's son Nathan to Adam; he is listed as the father of Mattathias (Lk 3:26).
know: Named only in Luke's genealogy (Lk 3:26).
Son of Joseph; father of Mattathias.

people.name: Seraiah
people.summary: Son of Asiel in the genealogy of Simeon (1 Chr 4:35).

people.name: Sergius Paulus
people.summary: Sergius Paulus, proconsul of Cyprus and 'a man of understanding', summoned Barnabas and Saul to hear the word of God. When the sorcerer Elymas opposed them and was struck blind, the proconsul believed, astonished at the teaching of the Lord.
people.catholic: The first Roman official recorded as believing in Acts; it is at this encounter that Saul is first called Paul (Acts 13:9).
know: Proconsul of Cyprus at Paphos.
Believed after Elymas was blinded (Acts 13:12).

people.name: Sethur
people.summary: Son of Michael, the man of Asher among the twelve sent by Moses to scout Canaan. With nine others he brought back an 'evil report' that discouraged the people; those ten died by plague before the LORD.
know: Represented Asher among the twelve spies (Num 13).
Brought back a discouraging report.
Died by plague (Num 14:36-37).

people.name: Shaaph
people.summary: Son of Jahdai in the genealogy of Judah, among the Calebites (1 Chr 2:47).

people.name: Shaaph
people.summary: Son of Caleb and Maacah in the genealogy of Judah, among the Calebites (1 Chr 2:49).

people.name: Shachia
people.summary: Son of Shaharaim and Hodesh in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:10).

people.name: Shaharaim
people.summary: Shaharaim, a Benjamite, fathered children in the field of Moab by his wives Hushim, Baara and Hodesh (1 Chr 8:8-11).

people.name: Shallum
people.summary: Son of Shaul in the genealogy of Simeon (1 Chr 4:25).

people.name: Shallum (Jeremiah's uncle)
people.summary: Shallum was Jeremiah's uncle and the father of Hanamel, who sold Jeremiah the family field at Anathoth.
know: Named only as Hanamel's father and Jeremiah's uncle (Jer 32:7).

people.name: Shamma
people.summary: Son of Zophah in the genealogy of Asher (1 Chr 7:37).

people.name: Shammai
people.summary: Son of Mered and Bithiah in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chr 4:17).

people.name: Shammua
people.summary: Son of Zaccur, the man of Reuben among the twelve sent by Moses to scout Canaan. With nine others he brought back an 'evil report' that discouraged the people; those ten died by plague before the LORD.
know: Represented Reuben among the twelve spies (Num 13).
Brought back a discouraging report.
Died by plague (Num 14:36-37).

people.name: Shamsherai
people.summary: Son of Jeroham in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:26; 8:27).

people.name: Shaphat
people.summary: Son of Shemaiah in the genealogy of the royal line of David (1 Chr 3:22).

people.name: Shaphat
people.summary: Son of Hori, the man of Simeon among the twelve sent by Moses to scout Canaan. With nine others he brought back an 'evil report' that discouraged the people; those ten died by plague before the LORD.
know: Represented Simeon among the twelve spies (Num 13).
Brought back a discouraging report.
Died by plague (Num 14:36-37).

people.name: Shaul
people.summary: Son of Uzziah in the genealogy of Levi, among the Kohathites (1 Chr 6:24).

people.name: Shear-jashub
people.summary: Isaiah's son, who went with his father to meet King Ahaz at the upper pool. His name means 'a remnant will return', a living sign of Isaiah's message.
people.catholic: His name embodies the prophetic theme of the faithful remnant, which the Church sees fulfilled in those who receive Christ (cf. Rom 9:27, 11:5).
know: Name means 'a remnant shall return'.
Accompanied Isaiah to meet Ahaz (Isa 7:3).
Isaiah says he and his children are 'for signs' in Israel (Isa 8:18).

people.name: Sheba
people.summary: Son of Abihail in the genealogy of Gad (1 Chr 5:13-14).

people.name: Sheber
people.summary: Son of Caleb and Maacah in the genealogy of Judah, among the Calebites (1 Chr 2:48).

people.name: Shecaniah son of Jehiel
people.summary: A layman of the clan of Elam who confessed Israel's sin of mixed marriages and urged Ezra to lead a covenant of reform, promising the people's support.
know: Said 'there is hope for Israel concerning this thing' (Ezra 10:2).

people.name: Shechem
people.summary: Son of Shemida in the genealogy of Manasseh (1 Chr 7:19).

people.name: Sheerah
people.summary: Sheerah, of the house of Ephraim, built Lower and Upper Beth-horon and Uzzen-sheerah - a rare woman city-builder in Scripture (1 Chr 7:24).

people.name: Shehariah
people.summary: Son of Jeroham in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:26; 8:27).

people.name: Shelesh
people.summary: Son of Hotham in the genealogy of Asher (1 Chr 7:35).

people.name: Shelomith
people.summary: Daughter of Zerubbabel in the genealogy of the royal line of David (1 Chr 3:19).

people.name: Shelomith
people.summary: Daughter of Dibri of the tribe of Dan, whose son by an Egyptian father blasphemed the Name in a quarrel in the camp and was stoned at the LORD's command.
know: Daughter of Dibri, of Dan (Lev 24:11).
Mother of the blasphemer of Lev 24.

people.name: Shema
people.summary: Son of Joel in the genealogy of Reuben (1 Chr 5:8).

people.name: Shema
people.summary: Son of Elpaal in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:13). He and Beriah were heads in Aijalon and put the inhabitants of Gath to flight.

people.name: Shemaiah
people.summary: Son of Shecaniah in the genealogy of the royal line of David (1 Chr 3:22).

people.name: Shemaiah
people.summary: Shemaiah is named in the genealogy of Simeon (1 Chr 4:37).

people.name: Shemaiah
people.summary: Son of Joel in the genealogy of Reuben (1 Chr 5:4).

people.name: Shemaiah son of Delaiah
people.summary: A man hired by Tobiah and Sanballat to persuade Nehemiah to hide in the Temple so that he could be discredited; Nehemiah refused.
know: Nehemiah: 'Should a man like me flee?' (Neh 6:11).

people.name: Shemeber
people.summary: Shemeber, king of Zeboiim, was one of the five kings of the cities of the plain who rebelled against Chedorlaomer and were defeated in the valley of Siddim.
know: One of the five kings of the cities of the plain (Gen 14:2)

people.name: Shemed
people.summary: Son of Elpaal in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:12). He built Ono and Lod.

people.name: Shemer
people.summary: Son of Mahli in the genealogy of Levi, among the Merarites (1 Chr 6:46). In the ancestry of Ethan the singer.

people.name: Shemuel
people.summary: Son of Tola in the genealogy of Issachar (1 Chr 7:2).

people.name: Shenazzar
people.summary: Shenazzar is listed among the sons of Jehoiachin (Jeconiah) the captive.
know: Born in the Babylonian exile

people.name: Shephatiah
people.summary: Son of Reuel in the genealogy of Benjamin, among those who resettled Jerusalem (1 Chr 9:8).

people.name: Shephatiah
people.summary: Son of Mahalalel in the genealogy of Judah, among those who settled in Jerusalem under Nehemiah (Neh 11:4).

people.name: Shephatiah son of Mattan
people.summary: Shephatiah was one of the officials who heard Jeremiah urge surrender to Babylon and persuaded Zedekiah to let them throw him into a cistern.

people.name: Shephuphan
people.summary: Son of Bela in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:5).

people.name: Sheresh
people.summary: Son of Machir in the genealogy of Manasseh (1 Chr 7:16).

people.name: Sheva
people.summary: Son of Caleb and Maacah in the genealogy of Judah, among the Calebites (1 Chr 2:49).

people.name: Shilshah
people.summary: Son of Zophah in the genealogy of Asher (1 Chr 7:37).

people.name: Shimea
people.summary: Son of Michael in the genealogy of Levi, among the Gershonites (1 Chr 6:39-40). In the ancestry of Asaph the singer.

people.name: Shimea
people.summary: Son of Uzzah in the genealogy of Levi, among the Merarites (1 Chr 6:30).

people.name: Shimei
people.summary: Son of Pedaiah in the genealogy of the royal line of David (1 Chr 3:19).

people.name: Shimei
people.summary: Son of Gog in the genealogy of Reuben (1 Chr 5:4).

people.name: Shimei
people.summary: Son of Jahath in the genealogy of Levi, among the Gershonites (1 Chr 6:42). In the ancestry of Asaph the singer.

people.name: Shimei
people.summary: Son of Libni in the genealogy of Levi, among the Merarites (1 Chr 6:29).

people.name: Shimei
people.summary: Shimei is the head of a Benjamite family living in Jerusalem whose nine sons are listed in 1 Chr 8:19-21 (perhaps the Shema of 8:13).

people.name: Shimon
people.summary: Shimon heads a Judahite family whose four sons are listed in 1 Chr 4:20.

people.name: Shimrath
people.summary: Son of Shimei in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:21).

people.name: Shimri
people.summary: Son of Shemaiah in the genealogy of Simeon (1 Chr 4:37).

people.name: Shinab
people.summary: Shinab, king of Admah, was one of the five kings of the cities of the plain who rebelled against Chedorlaomer and were defeated in the valley of Siddim.
know: One of the five kings of the cities of the plain (Gen 14:2)

people.name: Shiphi
people.summary: Son of Allon in the genealogy of Simeon (1 Chr 4:37).

people.name: Shiphrah
people.summary: One of two Hebrew midwives ordered by Pharaoh to kill newborn Hebrew boys. Fearing God, she and Puah let the boys live, and God dealt well with them and gave them households.
people.catholic: Shiphrah and Puah are often cited in Catholic teaching as early examples of conscientious refusal to take innocent life at the command of the state: they 'feared God' rather than the king (Exo 1:17).
know: Hebrew midwife in Egypt (Exo 1:15).
Refused Pharaoh's order to kill the boys.
God rewarded her with a household (Exo 1:21).

people.name: Shobab
people.summary: Son of Caleb in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chr 2:18).

people.name: Shua
people.summary: Daughter of Heber in the genealogy of Asher (1 Chr 7:32).

people.name: Shual
people.summary: Son of Zophah in the genealogy of Asher (1 Chr 7:36).

people.name: Shuthelah
people.summary: Son of Zabad in the genealogy of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:21).

people.name: Simeon
people.summary: Simeon, son of Judah, appears only in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, which runs from Joseph back through David's son Nathan to Adam; he is listed as the father of Levi (Lk 3:30).
know: Named only in Luke's genealogy (Lk 3:30).
Son of Judah; father of Levi.

people.name: Simeon called Niger
people.summary: Simeon, called Niger ('black'), was one of the prophets and teachers of the church at Antioch who, at the Spirit's command, laid hands on Barnabas and Saul and sent them out.
people.catholic: With the other leaders of Antioch he took part in the prayer, fasting and laying on of hands that commissioned the first missionary journey (Acts 13:3).
know: Listed among the prophets and teachers at Antioch.
Some suggest, without certainty, that he is Simon of Cyrene.

people.name: Simon II the high priest
people.summary: Simon son of Onias, high priest around 200 BC, who repaired and fortified the Temple and the city. Sirach ends his 'praise of the fathers' with a glowing portrait of him coming out of the sanctuary in his vestments and offering sacrifice amid the trumpets and the people's prayer, blessing the people in the Lord's name.
people.catholic: Sirach 50 is one of the most vivid descriptions of Temple liturgy in Scripture; the high priest emerging 'like the morning star' to bless the people has been read as a figure of Christ the High Priest who enters the true sanctuary and blesses his people (Heb 9:11-12; Luke 24:50-51).
know: Praised in Sirach 50:1-21.
Son of Onias (Sir 50:1).
According to Josephus, father of Onias III (not stated in Scripture).

people.name: Sismai
people.summary: Son of Eleasah in the genealogy of Judah, among the Jerahmeelites (1 Chr 2:40).

people.name: Sopater
people.summary: Sopater of Beroea, son of Pyrrhus in some manuscripts, accompanied Paul from Greece toward Jerusalem.
know: Possibly the same as Sosipater of Romans 16:21; uncertain.

people.name: Sosipater
people.summary: Sosipater is named in the greetings of Paul's Letter to the Romans. One of Paul's 'relatives' who sends greetings; possibly Sopater of Beroea (Acts 20:4).
know: One of Paul's 'relatives' who sends greetings; possibly Sopater of Beroea (Acts 20:4).

people.name: Stachys
people.summary: Stachys is named in the greetings of Paul's Letter to the Romans. 'My beloved'.
know: 'My beloved'.

people.name: Suah
people.summary: Son of Zophah in the genealogy of Asher (1 Chr 7:36).

people.name: Susanna (follower of Jesus)
people.summary: Susanna is named among the women who had been healed by Jesus and who travelled with him and the Twelve, providing for them from their possessions (Lk 8:3).
know: Named once, in Luke 8:3.
Distinct from Susanna of the Book of Daniel.

people.name: Syntyche
people.summary: Syntyche was one of two women at Philippi who had laboured with Paul in the gospel; Paul urges her and Euodia to 'think the same way in the Lord' and asks a 'true partner' to help them reconcile.
people.catholic: Paul's appeal is a model of fraternal reconciliation within the Church; he honors both women as co-workers whose names are in the book of life.
know: Laboured with Paul in the gospel (Phil 4:3).
Urged to agree with her fellow worker (Phil 4:2).

people.name: Tahan
people.summary: Son of Telah in the genealogy of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:25). In the ancestry of Joshua.

people.name: Tahash
people.summary: A child of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by his concubine Reumah.
know: Child of Nahor and Reumah (Gen 22:24)

people.name: Tahath
people.summary: Son of Bered in the genealogy of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:20).

people.name: Tahath
people.summary: Son of Eleadah in the genealogy of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:20).

people.name: Tamar daughter of Absalom
people.summary: Absalom named his only daughter Tamar, after his sister; she was 'a woman of beautiful face'.
know: Possibly the mother of Rehoboam's wife Maacah

people.name: Tappuah
people.summary: Son of Hebron in the genealogy of Judah, among the Calebites (1 Chr 2:43).

people.name: Tarshish
people.summary: Son of Bilhan in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:10).

people.name: Tebah
people.summary: A child of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by his concubine Reumah.
know: Child of Nahor and Reumah (Gen 22:24)

people.name: Tehinnah
people.summary: Son of Eshton in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chr 4:12). Called 'the father of Ir-nahash'.

people.name: Telah
people.summary: Son of Resheph in the genealogy of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:25). In the ancestry of Joshua.

people.name: Temeni
people.summary: Son of Ashhur and Naarah in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chr 4:6).

people.name: Tertius
people.summary: Tertius is named in the greetings of Paul's Letter to the Romans. Paul's scribe: 'I, Tertius, who write the letter, greet you in the Lord.'
know: Paul's scribe: 'I, Tertius, who write the letter, greet you in the Lord.'

people.name: Theudas
people.summary: Theudas was a would-be leader cited by Gamaliel: he gathered about four hundred men, but he was killed and his followers scattered.
know: Cited by Gamaliel as a failed movement of merely human origin.

people.name: Tiberius Caesar
people.summary: Tiberius succeeded Augustus as emperor (AD 14-37). Luke dates the start of John the Baptist's ministry to 'the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar' (Lk 3:1), and Jesus' public life, death and resurrection took place under his rule.
people.catholic: The 'Caesar' whose image was on the denarius when Jesus said 'Give to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's' (Mt 22:21) was Tiberius - a key text for Catholic teaching on the relation of Church and state. Antipas named the city of Tiberias, on the Sea of Tiberias, after him (Jn 6:1).
know: Emperor AD 14-37; adopted son and successor of Augustus.
His fifteenth year dates John's ministry (Lk 3:1).
Reigning emperor during Jesus' ministry and crucifixion.

people.name: Tilon
people.summary: Son of Shimon in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chr 4:20).

people.name: Timaeus
people.summary: Timaeus is named only as the father of the blind beggar Bartimaeus of Jericho (Mk 10:46).
know: Father of Bartimaeus.
Named only in Mark 10:46.

people.name: Timon
people.summary: Timon was one of the Seven men of good reputation, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, chosen by the Jerusalem church to serve at table so the apostles could devote themselves to prayer and the ministry of the word.
people.catholic: The choice of the Seven, on whom the apostles laid hands after prayer (Acts 6:6), is traditionally read as the institution of the diaconate, the first degree of Holy Orders, ordained 'not unto the priesthood but unto the ministry' (CCC 1569-1571).
know: Named among the Seven in Acts 6:5.
Received the laying on of hands from the apostles (Acts 6:6).

people.name: Tirhanah
people.summary: Son of Caleb and Maacah in the genealogy of Judah, among the Calebites (1 Chr 2:48).

people.name: Tiria
people.summary: Son of Jehallelel in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chr 4:16).

people.name: Tobiel
people.summary: Father of Tobit, of the tribe of Naphtali; he died while Tobit was young, leaving him an orphan.
know: Tobit was raised by his grandmother Deborah (Tob 1:8).

people.name: Tola
people.summary: Son of Puah son of Dodo, of Issachar, who rose to save Israel after Abimelech and judged Israel twenty-three years, living in Shamir in Ephraim.
know: Minor judge from Issachar (Jdg 10:1).
Judged twenty-three years (Jdg 10:2).

people.name: Tryphaena
people.summary: Tryphaena is named in the greetings of Paul's Letter to the Romans. Greeted with Tryphosa as women 'who labor in the Lord'.
know: Greeted with Tryphosa as women 'who labor in the Lord'.

people.name: Tryphosa
people.summary: Tryphosa is named in the greetings of Paul's Letter to the Romans. Greeted with Tryphaena as women 'who labor in the Lord'.
know: Greeted with Tryphaena as women 'who labor in the Lord'.

people.name: Tubal Cain
people.summary: Son of Lamech and Zillah, forger of every cutting instrument of bronze and iron.
know: First named metalsmith (Gen 4:22)

people.name: Tyrannus
people.summary: Paul taught daily for two years in the school (lecture hall) of Tyrannus at Ephesus after leaving the synagogue, so that all who lived in Asia heard the word.
know: Paul taught in his school for two years (Acts 19:9-10).

people.name: Ulla
people.summary: Ulla, an Asherite clan head, was the father of Arah, Hanniel and Rizia (1 Chr 7:39).

people.name: Urbanus
people.summary: Urbanus is named in the greetings of Paul's Letter to the Romans. 'Our fellow worker in Christ'.
know: 'Our fellow worker in Christ'.

people.name: Uriah the priest
people.summary: Uriah the priest was one of the two 'faithful witnesses' Isaiah took when he wrote 'Maher Shalal Hash Baz' on a tablet.
know: Probably the same as Urijah the priest who built Ahaz's Damascus-style altar (2 Kings 16:10-16).

people.name: Uriel
people.summary: Son of Tahath in the genealogy of Levi, among the Kohathites (1 Chr 6:24).

people.name: Uthai
people.summary: Uthai son of Ammihud, of the line of Perez son of Judah, was among the first to resettle Jerusalem after the exile (1 Chr 9:3-4).

people.name: Uz
people.summary: A son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by Milcah.
know: Nahor's firstborn (Gen 22:21)

people.name: Uzzah
people.summary: Son of Shimei in the genealogy of Levi, among the Merarites (1 Chr 6:29).

people.name: Uzzi
people.summary: Son of Bela in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:7).

people.name: Uzzi
people.summary: Son of Michri in the genealogy of Benjamin, among those who resettled Jerusalem (1 Chr 9:8).

people.name: Uzzi
people.summary: Uzzi son of Bani, of the sons of Asaph, was overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem in Nehemiah's time (Neh 11:22).

people.name: Uzziah
people.summary: Son of Uriel in the genealogy of Levi, among the Kohathites (1 Chr 6:24).

people.name: Uzziah
people.summary: Son of Zechariah in the genealogy of Judah, among those who settled in Jerusalem under Nehemiah (Neh 11:4).

people.name: Uzziel
people.summary: Son of Ishi in the genealogy of Simeon (1 Chr 4:42-43).

people.name: Uzziel
people.summary: Son of Bela in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:7).

people.name: Zabad
people.summary: Son of Tahath in the genealogy of Ephraim (1 Chr 7:21).

people.name: Zabdi
people.summary: Son of Shimei in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:19; 8:21).

people.name: Zaccur
people.summary: Son of Hammuel in the genealogy of Simeon (1 Chr 4:26).

people.name: Zadok
people.summary: Zadok, son of Azor, appears only in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus as the father of Achim (Mt 1:14), in the line of David's royal heirs after the Babylonian exile.
know: Named only in Matthew 1 - a link in Jesus' royal Davidic line after the exile.
Son of Azor; father of Achim.

people.name: Zaza
people.summary: Son of Jonathan in the genealogy of Judah, among the Jerahmeelites (1 Chr 2:33).

people.name: Zebadiah
people.summary: Son of Beriah in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:15).

people.name: Zebadiah
people.summary: Son of Elpaal in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:17).

people.name: Zebidah
people.summary: Zebidah daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah was a wife of Josiah and mother of King Jehoiakim.
know: Mother of Jehoiakim

people.name: Zechariah
people.summary: Son of Amariah in the genealogy of Judah, among those who settled in Jerusalem under Nehemiah (Neh 11:4).

people.name: Zechariah
people.summary: Zechariah is named in the genealogy of Judah, among those who settled in Jerusalem under Nehemiah (Neh 11:5).

people.name: Zechariah son of Jeberechiah
people.summary: The second of Isaiah's two faithful witnesses to the tablet inscribed 'Maher Shalal Hash Baz'.
know: Not the post-exilic prophet Zechariah.

people.name: Zedekiah
people.summary: Son of Jehoiakim in the genealogy of the royal line of David (1 Chr 3:16). A son (or descendant) of Jehoiakim, distinct from King Zedekiah son of Josiah.

people.name: Zemirah
people.summary: Son of Becher in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:8).

people.name: Zenas
people.summary: Zenas 'the lawyer' was travelling with Apollos; Paul asks Titus to speed them on their journey with everything they need.
know: The only Christian in the New Testament called a lawyer (Titus 3:13).

people.name: Zephaniah
people.summary: Son of Tahath in the genealogy of Levi, among the Kohathites (1 Chr 6:36-37). In the ancestry of Samuel and Heman the singer.

people.name: Zephaniah
people.summary: Zephaniah, son of Cushi and a descendant of a certain Hezekiah, prophesied in the reign of King Josiah. He proclaimed the Day of the LORD as a day of wrath against idolatry in Judah and the nations, promised a humble and lowly remnant, and ended with a joyful song: 'Sing, daughter of Zion... the LORD your God is in the midst of you'.
people.catholic: The medieval sequence 'Dies irae' takes its opening words from Zephaniah 1:15 in the Latin Vulgate ('dies irae dies illa'). His call 'Sing, daughter of Zion' (Zeph 3:14-17), echoed in Gabriel's 'Rejoice' to Mary, is read in Advent and on the feast of the Visitation, and the Church sees Mary as the Daughter of Zion in whom the Lord dwells. His 'humble and lowly people' (Zeph 3:12) are the 'anawim', the poor of the Lord, whose spirituality Mary embodies in the Magnificat.
know: Genealogy back four generations to a 'Hezekiah' (Zeph 1:1), possibly the king.
Prophesied under Josiah (c. 640-609 BC).
Source of the 'Dies irae' (Zeph 1:15).
'Sing, daughter of Zion!' (Zeph 3:14).

people.name: Zerah
people.summary: Son of Iddo in the genealogy of Levi, among the Gershonites (1 Chr 6:21).

people.name: Zerah
people.summary: Son of Adaiah in the genealogy of Levi, among the Gershonites (1 Chr 6:41). In the ancestry of Asaph the singer.

people.name: Zereth
people.summary: Son of Ashhur and Helah in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chr 4:7).

people.name: Zeruah
people.summary: Zeruah, a widow, was the mother of Jeroboam I.
know: A widow of Zeredah

people.name: Zethan
people.summary: Son of Bilhan in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 7:10).

people.name: Zia
people.summary: Son of Abihail in the genealogy of Gad (1 Chr 5:13-14).

people.name: Zibia
people.summary: Son of Shaharaim and Hodesh in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:9).

people.name: Zichri
people.summary: Son of Shimei in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:19; 8:21).

people.name: Zichri
people.summary: Son of Shashak in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:23; 8:25).

people.name: Zichri
people.summary: Son of Jeroham in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:27).

people.name: Zillethai
people.summary: Son of Shimei in the genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr 8:20; 8:21).

people.name: Zimmah
people.summary: Son of Shimei in the genealogy of Levi, among the Gershonites (1 Chr 6:42). In the ancestry of Asaph the singer.

people.name: Ziph
people.summary: Son of Jehallelel in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chr 4:16).

people.name: Ziphah
people.summary: Son of Jehallelel in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chr 4:16).

people.name: Ziphion
people.summary: A son of Gad who went down to Egypt with Jacob's household.
know: Listed among the seventy of Jacob's house who came to Egypt (Gen 46)

people.name: Ziza
people.summary: Ziza son of Shiphi was one of the Simeonite princes who in Hezekiah's days seized pasture land at Gedor (1 Chr 4:37-41).

people.name: Zobebah
people.summary: Child of Hakkoz in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chr 4:8).

people.name: Zoheth
people.summary: Son of Ishi in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chr 4:20).

people.name: Anne
people.summary: Scripture does not name the Virgin Mary's mother. Tradition, beginning with the Protoevangelium of James, names her Anne, a long-childless wife who with Joachim was granted a daughter, Mary.
people.catholic: Tradition holds that Anne conceived Mary after years of barrenness and prayer, and the Church celebrates Mary's Immaculate Conception in Anne's womb (December 8) and her Nativity (September 8). St Anne is a beloved patroness of mothers, grandmothers and expectant women, with great shrines such as Sainte-Anne-de-Beaupre in Quebec. She is honoured with Joachim as grandmother of Jesus.
know: Known only from Tradition, not from the Bible.
By Tradition the mother of the Virgin Mary and grandmother of Jesus.
Shares the feast of July 26 with St Joachim.

people.name: Daughter of Machir
people.summary: The unnamed daughter of Machir, the father of Gilead, married Hezron when he was sixty and bore him Segub (1 Chr 2:21).

people.name: Daughter of Sheshan
people.summary: Sheshan gave this daughter as wife to his Egyptian servant Jarha, and she bore Attai (1 Chr 2:35).

people.name: Ezekiel's wife
people.summary: Ezekiel's wife, 'the desire of your eyes', died suddenly; God forbade the prophet to mourn openly, as a sign to the exiles of how they would react to the destruction of the Temple.
know: Unnamed in Scripture.
Her death and Ezekiel's silence were a sign-act (Ezek 24:15-24).

people.name: Gideon's concubine in Shechem
people.summary: Gideon's concubine from Shechem, mother of Abimelech, through whose kin in Shechem Abimelech seized power.
know: Lived in Shechem (Jdg 8:31).
Mother of Abimelech.

people.name: Jephthah's daughter
people.summary: Jephthah's only child, who came out with timbrels and dances to meet her victorious father and became the subject of his vow. She asked for two months to mourn her virginity on the mountains with her companions; afterward her father 'did to her according to his vow', and the daughters of Israel lamented her four days each year.
people.catholic: Her obedience and the annual lament of Israel's daughters have moved many Christian writers; some later interpreters argued she was dedicated to perpetual virginity rather than sacrificed, though the text is commonly read as a sacrifice. Either way, the Church reads her story as a condemnation of rash vows and of any 'offering' of innocent human life.
know: Jephthah's only child (Jdg 11:34).
Mourned her virginity two months (Jdg 11:37-38).
Israel's daughters lamented her yearly (Jdg 11:40).
Unnamed in Scripture.

people.name: Joachim
people.summary: Scripture does not name the Virgin Mary's parents. Tradition, beginning with the second-century Protoevangelium of James, names her father Joachim, a devout and prosperous man who with his wife Anne prayed long for a child.
people.catholic: Tradition holds that Joachim and Anne received Mary as the answer to their prayers and presented her in the Temple (commemorated on November 21). The Church honours them together as the grandparents of Jesus, and Pope Francis instituted (2021) the World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly on the fourth Sunday of July, close to their feast. Their story is not Scripture, but the liturgy honours them as the parents through whom God prepared the Immaculate Mother of his Son.
know: Known only from Tradition (Protoevangelium of James), not from the Bible.
Husband of St Anne and, by Tradition, father of the Virgin Mary.
Shares the feast of July 26 with St Anne.

people.name: Job's wife
people.summary: Job's unnamed wife, who in his affliction told him, 'Do you still maintain your integrity? Renounce God, and die.' Job rebuked her: 'Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?'
people.catholic: Her words are often read as the voice of temptation in suffering (St Augustine called her the devil's helper), though later writers have also pointed out that she too had lost all ten children. Job's reply is a classic expression of trusting acceptance of God's will.
know: Unnamed in Scripture.
Urged Job to curse God (Job 2:9).
Mentioned again in Job 19:17.

people.name: John (grandfather of the Maccabees)
people.summary: The father of Mattathias, son of Simeon, of the priestly course of Joarib.
know: Known only from Mattathias' genealogy (1 Macc 2:1).

people.name: Manasseh's Aramean concubine
people.summary: An Aramean concubine of Manasseh son of Joseph bore him Asriel and Machir the father of Gilead (1 Chr 7:14).

people.name: Mered's Judahite wife
people.summary: Mered's wife 'the Jewess' (of Judah) bore Jered, Heber and Jekuthiel, founders of Gedor, Soco and Zanoah (1 Chr 4:18).

people.name: Micah's mother
people.summary: Ephraimite woman who cursed the thief of her 1,100 pieces of silver; when her son Micah confessed and returned it, she blessed him and had part of it made into a carved and a molten image for his shrine.
know: Cursed the theft, then blessed her son (Jdg 17:2).
Dedicated silver to make idols 'for the LORD' (Jdg 17:3-4).
Unnamed in Scripture.

people.name: Mother of King Lemuel
people.summary: The queen mother whose instruction to her son, King Lemuel, forms Proverbs 31 — one of the rare biblical passages of teaching voiced by a woman.
know: Taught her son to speak for the voiceless (Prov 31:8-9).

people.name: Mother of the seven Maccabean brothers
people.summary: The mother who watched her seven sons tortured and killed in one day under Antiochus IV for refusing to eat pork, encouraging each of them in their ancestral language with faith in the Creator who would give back their breath and life. After urging the youngest not to accept the king's offer, she herself died last.
people.catholic: 1 and 2 Maccabees are deuterocanonical books, received in the Church's canon (Rome 382, Hippo 393, Carthage 397, Florence, and defined at Trent in 1546) though not in the Hebrew Bible or Protestant Old Testament. Her words are among Scripture's clearest statements of creation from nothing — God made all things 'not of things that were' (2 Macc 7:28; cited in CCC 297) — and of hope in bodily resurrection (2 Macc 7:22-23, 29). The Church honors her and her sons as the 'Holy Maccabees', the only Old Testament martyrs once kept on the universal Roman calendar (August 1); the Roman Martyrology still commemorates them on that day. Later tradition gives her names such as Solomonia (East) or Hannah (Jewish legend).
know: Saw seven sons die in one day (2 Macc 7:20).
Taught creation 'not of things that were' (2 Macc 7:28).
Hoped to 'receive you again with your brothers' (2 Macc 7:29).
Feast with her sons: August 1.

people.name: Peter's mother-in-law
people.summary: Simon Peter's mother-in-law lay sick with a fever in the house at Capernaum; Jesus took her by the hand, the fever left her, and she began to serve them.
people.catholic: Her immediate service after healing is read as a model of the grace that frees us for service. The episode also shows that Peter was married.
know: Unnamed in Scripture.
Healed in Peter's house at Capernaum (Mk 1:29-31).
Shows that Peter was married.

people.name: Samson's wife from Timnah
people.summary: Philistine woman of Timnah whom Samson married against his parents' wishes. Under threat from the Philistines she pressed Samson to reveal his riddle, then was given to his companion; in revenge for Samson's attack, the Philistines burned her and her father.
know: Philistine of Timnah (Jdg 14:1-2).
Extracted the riddle's answer (Jdg 14:15-17).
Burned by the Philistines (Jdg 15:6).
Unnamed in Scripture.

people.name: Seven Maccabean brothers
people.summary: Seven brothers arrested with their mother and tortured one after another before Antiochus IV for refusing swine's flesh. Each died professing faith: 'the King of the world will raise us who have died for his laws up to an everlasting renewal of life' (2 Macc 7:9).
people.catholic: 1 and 2 Maccabees are deuterocanonical books, received in the Church's canon (Rome 382, Hippo 393, Carthage 397, Florence, and defined at Trent in 1546) though not in the Hebrew Bible or Protestant Old Testament. The brothers' confessions are a high point of Old Testament faith in the resurrection of the body (2 Macc 7:9, 11, 14, 23), a step in the progressive revelation of the resurrection the Catechism describes (CCC 992). The youngest's offering of his life to 'bring to an end the wrath of the Almighty' on his nation (2 Macc 7:37-38) anticipates vicarious, redemptive suffering. Honored as the 'Holy Maccabees' on August 1; tradition held their relics at Antioch, and later in Rome at San Pietro in Vincoli.
know: Group entry for the seven sons.
Hope of resurrection (2 Macc 7:9-14).
Hebrews 11:35 likely alludes to them.
Feast: August 1 (Holy Maccabees).

people.name: Son of Shelomith (the blasphemer)
people.summary: Son of an Israelite mother, Shelomith, and an Egyptian father, who cursed the Name of the LORD during a fight in the camp. He was held until the LORD's will was known, then stoned outside the camp, and the law against blasphemy was given.
people.catholic: The episode underlies the Second Commandment's teaching on reverence for God's name, which the Catechism treats under the commandment 'You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain' (CCC 2142).
know: Unnamed; son of Shelomith and an Egyptian (Lev 24:10).
Blasphemed the Name (Lev 24:11).
Occasion of the law in Lev 24:15-16.

people.name: The Levite of Judges 19
people.summary: Levite living in the remote hill country of Ephraim whose concubine left him for her father's house in Bethlehem. Returning with her, he lodged in Gibeah of Benjamin, where the men of the town abused her through the night until she died. He cut her body into twelve pieces and sent them through Israel, provoking war against Benjamin.
people.catholic: The story shows the moral collapse of an Israel without a king (Jdg 19:1; 21:25). The Church reads it as an indictment of violence against women and as preparing for God's gift of a righteous king, ultimately Christ.
know: Levite from the hill country of Ephraim (Jdg 19:1).
Lodged at Gibeah (Jdg 19:15-21).
Sent his concubine's body through Israel (Jdg 19:29).
Unnamed in Scripture.

people.name: The Levite's concubine
people.summary: Woman of Bethlehem in Judah, concubine of the Levite of Judges 19, who was given over to the men of Gibeah, abused through the night, and found dead at the door at dawn. Her death led to the war against Benjamin.
people.catholic: Her story, one of the darkest in Scripture, is read as a lament over human cruelty and the failure of protectors; Hosea recalls 'the days of Gibeah' as a byword for corruption (Hos 9:9; 10:9).
know: From Bethlehem in Judah (Jdg 19:1).
Abused and killed at Gibeah (Jdg 19:25-28).
Unnamed in Scripture.

people.name: The prophetess (Isaiah's wife)
people.summary: Isaiah calls his wife 'the prophetess'; she bore him Maher-shalal-hash-baz, whose name was a sign of Assyria's coming plunder of Damascus and Samaria.
know: Unnamed in Scripture; called 'the prophetess' (Isa 8:3).

people.name: Wife of Manoah (mother of Samson)
people.summary: Barren Danite woman to whom the angel of the LORD appeared, announcing that she would bear a son who would be a Nazirite to God from the womb and begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines. She was to drink no wine and eat nothing unclean.
people.catholic: Her story stands in the line of barren mothers whose sons are gifts of God - Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel, Hannah, Elizabeth - and so prepares for the annunciation to Mary. Her calm faith ('if the LORD were pleased to kill us, he wouldn't have received a burnt offering', Jdg 13:23) contrasts with Manoah's fear.
know: Barren until the angel's visit (Jdg 13:2-3).
Told to abstain from wine and unclean food (Jdg 13:4).
Unnamed in Scripture.
Mother of Samson.
